title.zh: 卷509 列傳二百九十六 列女二
title.raw: 卷509 列傳二百九十六 列女二

sentences.zh: 張延祚妻蔡，漳浦人。

translations.literal: Cai, wife of Zhang Yanzuo, was a native of Zhangpu.
translations.idiomatic: Cai, the wife of Zhang Yanzuo, came from Zhangpu.

sentences.zh: 國初，師既下福建，濱海數百里，猶群起負固。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the dynasty, after the army had taken Fujian, for several hundred li along the coast people still rose up in groups and held out stubbornly.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the dynasty, once the imperial armies had conquered Fujian, bands along hundreds of miles of coastland still rose in stubborn resistance.

sentences.zh: 有方祐者，謀舉兵，延祚與語，不合，被殺。

translations.literal: There was one Fang You who plotted to raise troops; Yanzuo spoke with him, they did not agree, and he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Fang You planned an uprising; Zhang Yanzuo argued with him, their views clashed, and Zhang was killed.

sentences.zh: 子才十餘歲，蔡哀慟，謀復仇。

translations.literal: Their son was only a little over ten years old; Cai grieved bitterly and plotted revenge.
translations.idiomatic: Their son was barely in his teens; devastated, Cai plotted vengeance.

sentences.zh: 一日，聞祐將其徒至，方夕，易男子服，挾刃詣祐壘。

translations.literal: One day, hearing that You was leading his followers there, at dusk she changed into men's clothing, took a blade, and went to You's camp.
translations.idiomatic: One evening she heard Fang You was leading his men that way; she dressed as a man, armed herself, and set out for his camp.

sentences.zh: 未至，顧見其子踉蹌來，念母子並命，斬張氏祀，乃與俱歸。

translations.literal: Before she arrived, she looked back and saw her son staggering toward her; thinking that mother and son might both lose their lives and cut off the Zhang lineage, she returned together with him.
translations.idiomatic: Before she reached the camp she saw her son stumbling after her; fearing they would both die and the Zhang line would end, she turned back with him.

sentences.zh: 既，祐降為民，娶於蔡，其婦，蔡大母行也，因得常見祐。

translations.literal: Afterward, You surrendered and became a commoner; he married into the Cai family, and his wife was of the same generation as Cai's grandmother, so she was thus able to see You often.
translations.idiomatic: Later Fang You surrendered and married into the Cai clan; his wife was a kinswoman of Cai's grandmother's generation, which gave Cai frequent access to Fang You.

sentences.zh: 祐甘語謝蔡，蔡益憤，夜輒握刃刺壁，壁穿，刃猶擊。

translations.literal: You spoke sweet words to thank Cai; Cai grew ever more wrathful, and at night would grasp a blade and stab the wall—the wall was pierced through, yet the blade still struck.
translations.idiomatic: Fang You flattered her with thanks; Cai only grew angrier. Night after night she drove a blade into the wall until it passed clear through, the steel still ringing against stone.

sentences.zh: 順治五年春，蔡伺祐有所過，度道所必經，將其子止松林中，挾刃俟。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifth year of Shunzhi, Cai watched for You to pass by somewhere, reckoned the road he must take, left her son in the pine woods, and waited with a blade.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Shunzhi 5, she lay in wait on a road Fang You had to take, left her son in the pines, and waited with her blade drawn.

sentences.zh: 日午，祐雄服怒馬來，蔡自林中出叱祐，祐驚呼從者，從者駭走。

translations.literal: At noon, You came in martial dress on a fierce horse; Cai emerged from the woods and shouted at You; You cried out to his attendants, and they fled in terror.
translations.idiomatic: At noon Fang You rode up in battle dress on a spirited horse; Cai stepped from the woods and challenged him; he called to his followers, who fled in panic.

sentences.zh: 蔡持刀斫祐，祐墜馬，負創走，蔡疾追之。

translations.literal: Cai grasped her blade and struck at You; You fell from his horse and fled wounded; Cai pursued swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: She struck with her blade; Fang You fell from his horse and ran, bleeding; she gave chase.

sentences.zh: 行人聚而譁，蔡且奔且言曰：「吾夫為此賊害，有助者，吾與俱死！」

translations.literal: Passersby gathered and clamored; running, Cai cried: "My husband was harmed by this brigand—whoever helps me, I will die with them!"
translations.idiomatic: A crowd gathered as she ran, shouting: "This villain murdered my husband—help me, and we'll die together!"

sentences.zh: 追及祐，祐攀松枝與鬥，中蔡額，血被面，鬥益力。

translations.literal: She overtook You; You clutched a pine branch and fought; he struck Cai's forehead, blood covering her face, yet she fought all the harder.
translations.idiomatic: She caught him; he seized a pine bough to fight. He gashed her forehead until blood masked her face, yet she fought all the harder.

sentences.zh: 遂迫祐，左手捽祐，右手奮刃，斷其首，擲道旁，觀者皆大驚。

translations.literal: She pressed You close, seized him with her left hand, and with her right swung the blade and severed his head, casting it beside the road; all who watched were greatly startled.
translations.idiomatic: She seized him with her left hand and with her right swung the blade through his neck, tossing the head by the roadside; onlookers were thunderstruck.

sentences.zh: 蔡持祐首告於延祚墓，將其子詣巡按御史台門請死，巡按御史霍達異其事，問：「有主者乎？」

translations.literal: Cai carried You's head and reported at Yanzuo's tomb, then took her son to the censor's gate to request death; Censor Huo Da marveled at the affair and asked, "Was there someone directing this?"
translations.idiomatic: She presented Fang You's head at her husband's grave, then brought her son to the surveillance censor's gate to surrender herself for execution. Censor Huo Da was astonished and asked, "Did someone put you up to this?"

sentences.zh: 蔡哭對曰：「夫死，所以不即死者，以有子耳。

translations.literal: Cai wept and replied: "When my husband died, the reason I did not die at once was that I had a son.
translations.idiomatic: Weeping, she answered: "When my husband died, I lived on only because I had a son.

sentences.zh: 今子且不顧，安肯受他人指耶？

translations.literal: Now that I do not even care for my son, how could I accept direction from another?
translations.idiomatic: Now that I have set even my son aside, why would I take orders from anyone else?

sentences.zh: 然殺人當死，公毋撓國法。」

translations.literal: Yet killing a man deserves death; my lord, do not bend the national law."
translations.idiomatic: Still, murder is a capital crime—sir, do not bend the law for my sake."

sentences.zh: 達乃釋不問。

translations.literal: Da thereupon released her without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Huo Da released her without further prosecution.

sentences.zh: 陳時夏妻田，長樂人。

translations.literal: Tian, wife of Chen Shixia, was from Changle.
translations.idiomatic: Tian, the wife of Chen Shixia, came from Changle.

sentences.zh: 時夏父超鵬早卒，母高守節。

translations.literal: Shixia's father Chao Peng died young; his mother Gao preserved her chastity.
translations.idiomatic: Shixia's father Chao Peng had died young; his mother Gao remained a chaste widow.

sentences.zh: 田讀書，知大義。

translations.literal: Tian read books and understood great principles.
translations.idiomatic: Tian had studied and understood the larger moral duties of life.

sentences.zh: 時夏貧，事王姑及姑高，朝夕扶持，不去左右。

translations.literal: Shixia was poor; Tian served her husband's grandmother and mother Gao, supporting them morning and evening, never leaving their side.
translations.idiomatic: The family was poor; Tian waited on her husband's grandmother and on Gao, supporting them from morning to night and never straying from their side.

sentences.zh: 病不能食，輒以口哺。

translations.literal: When they were ill and could not eat, she would feed them mouth to mouth.
translations.idiomatic: When they fell ill and could not eat, she fed them from her own mouth.

sentences.zh: 時夏卒，督諸子讀，嘗自述與夫論學語，為敬和堂筆訓，以授諸子，粹然儒家言。

translations.literal: After Shixia died, she supervised the sons' reading, once set down in writing her conversations with her husband on learning as brush instructions of the Jinghe Hall, to teach the sons—pure Confucian teaching.
translations.idiomatic: After Shixia died she oversaw the boys' studies and wrote down her conversations with her husband on learning as Brush Instructions of the Jinghe Hall for her sons—utterly the voice of the Ru school.

sentences.zh: 其自序略曰：「餘苟延性命，祗以三子一女，冀其能自立，不至辱泉下耳！

translations.literal: Her preface in brief says: "I prolong my life only for three sons and one daughter, hoping they may stand on their own and not disgrace those beneath the springs!
translations.idiomatic: Her preface reads in part: "I cling to life only for three sons and one daughter, hoping they may stand on their own and not disgrace their father in the grave!

sentences.zh: 大兒今十一，猶有童心，況諸幼孤，未亡人心力垂盡。

translations.literal: The eldest son is now eleven and still childish in heart; how much more the young orphans—the widow's strength is nearly spent.
translations.idiomatic: My eldest is only eleven and still a child at heart; the younger orphans need me all the more, and this widow's strength is nearly gone.

sentences.zh: 恐旦暮死，而夫子之學行，與餘之出肝膽，忍艱苦以冀其有成者，將誰為餘告之耶？

translations.literal: I fear death morning or evening, and my husband's learning and conduct, together with what I have poured out from liver and gall and endured in hardship hoping they may succeed—who will tell them for me?
translations.idiomatic: I may die any day; who will tell them of their father's learning and conduct, and of all I have poured out and endured in hope they may succeed?

sentences.zh: 爰述先訓，書之於冊。

translations.literal: Therefore I relate the former instructions and set them down in a book.
translations.idiomatic: So I set down his teachings and commit them to writing.

sentences.zh: 嗟乎！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 小子異日讀此，其能自省，使餘生不負於子女，死不愧於夫子否耶？」

translations.literal: When you boys read this another day, will you be able to examine yourselves, so that in life I do not fail my children, and in death I am not ashamed before my husband?"
translations.idiomatic: When you read this one day, boys, will you examine yourselves so that in life I do not fail you, and in death I need not be ashamed before your father?"

sentences.zh: 居十餘年，卒。

translations.literal: She lived more than ten years, then died.
translations.idiomatic: She lived on more than ten years, then died.

sentences.zh: 傅光箕妻吳，宣城人。

translations.literal: Wu, wife of Fu Guangji, was from Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wu, the wife of Fu Guangji, came from Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 吳歸於傅，光箕已病矣，逾年卒。

translations.literal: When Wu married into the Fu family, Guangji was already ill; after a year he died.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu married into the Fu household, Guangji was already ill; within a year he was dead.

sentences.zh: 吳父母欲嫁之。

translations.literal: Wu's parents wished to remarry her.
translations.idiomatic: Her parents wanted to marry her off again.

sentences.zh: 吳歸，留吳而訟傅氏，衣食吳。

translations.literal: When Wu returned home, they kept Wu and sued the Fu family to provide food and clothing for Wu.
translations.idiomatic: When she went back to her parents' home they kept her there and sued the Fu clan to support her with food and clothing.

sentences.zh: 吳還傅氏，以訟故勿納。

translations.literal: Wu returned to the Fu family, but because of the lawsuit they would not admit her.
translations.idiomatic: She returned to the Fu household, but because of the lawsuit they refused to take her in.

sentences.zh: 吳復歸，請自食，無累父母。

translations.literal: Wu returned again, asking to support herself so as not to burden her parents.
translations.idiomatic: She went back to her parents once more and asked to support herself so she would not burden them.

sentences.zh: 力紡，聞有媒至，輒求死，乃別居。

translations.literal: She labored at spinning; whenever she heard a matchmaker was coming, she would seek death, so she lived apart.
translations.idiomatic: She spun for a living; whenever she heard a matchmaker was coming she threatened suicide, and so she lived apart.

sentences.zh: 明季，飢，恆餓。

translations.literal: In the late Ming, famine—she was often hungry.
translations.idiomatic: In the famine at the end of the Ming she was often starving.

sentences.zh: 鄰饋之，勿受。

translations.literal: When neighbors offered food, she would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When neighbors offered food she would not take it.

sentences.zh: 族姊歸於魏，亦嫠也，遺之米，乃半易糠覈。

translations.literal: A cousin who had married into the Wei family, also a widow, sent her rice; she exchanged half for chaff and husks.
translations.idiomatic: A widowed cousin married into the Wei clan sent her rice; she traded half of it for chaff and husks.

sentences.zh: 或怪問之，曰：「雜糜之，可一月不死也。」

translations.literal: When someone wondered and asked, she said: "Mixed with porridge, it can keep one alive a month."
translations.idiomatic: When someone asked why, she said, "Mixed into gruel, this will keep me alive a month."

sentences.zh: 久之，紡有餘錢，得婢曰春蘭，拾籜供爨事。

translations.literal: After a long time, from spinning she had surplus money and obtained a maid named Chunlan, who gathered bamboo sheaths for the kitchen fire.
translations.idiomatic: In time her spinning brought in a little spare cash and she hired a servant girl named Chunlan, who gathered bamboo sheaths for the cooking fire.

sentences.zh: 裡媼或呼春蘭食，吳必審所自，戒勿輕受食。

translations.literal: When village women called Chunlan to eat, Wu always inquired where the food came from and warned her not to accept food lightly.
translations.idiomatic: When village women called Chunlan to eat, Wu always asked where the food came from and warned her never to accept food lightly.

sentences.zh: 春蘭自是即不受裡媼食。

translations.literal: From then on Chunlan would not accept food from village women.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Chunlan would not take food from the village women.

sentences.zh: 鄭哲飛妻硃，哲飛，南安人；

translations.literal: Zhu, wife of Zheng Zhefei—Zhefei was from Nan'an;
translations.idiomatic: Zhu, wife of Zheng Zhefei—Zhefei was a native of Nan'an;

sentences.zh: 硃，明魯王以海女也。

translations.literal: Zhu was daughter of the Ming Prince of Lu, Yi Hai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu was the daughter of the Ming Prince of Lu, Zhu Yihai.

sentences.zh: 嫁哲飛，生丈夫子一，女子子三，而哲飛卒。

translations.literal: She married Zhefei and bore one son and three daughters, then Zhefei died.
translations.idiomatic: She married Zhefei and bore one son and three daughters before he died.

sentences.zh: 會以海亦殂，渡海至台灣，依明宗室寧靖王術桂以居。

translations.literal: When Yi Hai also died, she crossed the sea to Taiwan and lived relying on the Ming clansman Prince Ningjing, Zhu Shugui.
translations.idiomatic: When Yihai too died, she crossed to Taiwan and lived under the protection of the Ming clansman Prince Ningjing, Zhu Shugui.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十二年，師克台灣，術桂自殺，硃奉姑育諸孤，以女紅自給。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Kangxi, the army took Taiwan; Shugui killed himself; Zhu served her mother-in-law and raised the orphans, supporting herself by needlework.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 22 the imperial armies took Taiwan; Shugui took his own life. Zhu waited on her mother-in-law, raised the orphans, and supported them with her needlework.

sentences.zh: 居五十餘年乃卒，年八十餘。

translations.literal: She lived more than fifty years, then died at over eighty.
translations.idiomatic: She lived on more than fifty years and died in her eighties.

sentences.zh: 初師下舟山，以海妃陳入井死，以海諡之曰貞，而以海女又以節終。

translations.literal: Earlier when the army took Zhoushan, Yi Hai's consort Chen died by entering a well; Yi Hai was given the posthumous title "Chaste," and Yi Hai's daughter also ended in chastity.
translations.idiomatic: When the armies first took Zhoushan, Yihai's consort Chen drowned herself in a well; Yihai was posthumously titled "Chaste," and his daughter likewise ended her life in virtue.

sentences.zh: 李若金女，名訚，餘干人。

translations.literal: Daughter of Li Rujin, named Yin, from Yugan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Rujin's daughter, named Yin, came from Yugan.

sentences.zh: 明季，字淮王世子由桂。

translations.literal: In the late Ming, she was betrothed by letter to Zhu Yougui, heir of the Prince of Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Ming she was betrothed by letter to Zhu Yougui, heir of the Prince of Huai.

sentences.zh: 入國初，由桂出亡，訚誓不更字，嘗詠金環曰：「紅爐經百鍊，不失本來真。」

translations.literal: At the start of the dynasty Yougui fled; Yin vowed not to marry another, and once versified on a gold ring: "The red furnace refines a hundred times, yet does not lose its original truth."
translations.idiomatic: Early in the dynasty Yougui fled into exile; Yin swore never to marry another and once wrote on a gold ring: "The red furnace tempers it a hundred times, yet it does not lose its original nature."

sentences.zh: 事父母孝，年五十九卒。

translations.literal: She was filial to her parents and died at fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: She was filial to her parents and died at fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 王師課妻硃，蕭山人。

translations.literal: Zhu, wife of Wang Shike, from Xiaoshan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu, the wife of Wang Shike, came from Xiaoshan.

sentences.zh: 師課，明天啟中官太醫院​​院判，卒。

translations.literal: Shike, in the Tianqi reign of Ming, served as vice director of the Imperial Medical Institute, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Shike had served as vice director of the Imperial Medical Institute under the Ming emperor Tianqi and then died.

sentences.zh: 明亡兵亂，硃率二子避九里坳，嘗遇賊，脅以刃，硃奪刃剺面，哭且詈。

translations.literal: When the Ming fell and soldiers ravaged, Zhu led her two sons to shelter at Jiuli'ao; once they met bandits who threatened with blades; Zhu seized a blade and slashed her face, weeping and cursing.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ming fell and war spread, Zhu led her two sons to shelter at Jiuli'ao. Once they met bandits who threatened them with blades; she seized a blade and slashed her own face, weeping and cursing them.

sentences.zh: 賊欲殺之，二子號慟求代，得不死。

translations.literal: The bandits wished to kill her; the two sons wailed and begged to die in her place, and she was spared.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits meant to kill her; her two sons wailed and begged to die in her stead, and she was spared.

sentences.zh: 事平，歸老於家。

translations.literal: When things settled, she returned home to live out her days.
translations.idiomatic: When peace returned she went home to live out her days.

sentences.zh: 嘗為勗子歌五章，其三章曰：「我生之後逢世亂，白頭兵起蒼黃竄，膚血染點叢麻紅，母子支離宵不旦。

translations.literal: She once composed five chapters of songs to exhort her sons; the third chapter says: "After my birth I met a world in turmoil; gray-haired, war rose and we fled in panic; flesh and blood stained the red of brush thickets; mother and sons torn apart, night without dawn.
translations.idiomatic: She once wrote five songs to exhort her sons; the third runs: "Born into a world gone mad, I fled gray-haired when war broke out; flesh and blood stained the red thicket brush; mother and sons torn apart, night without dawn.

sentences.zh: 飛雷聚驚鼓鼙，秋雨淋漓斷薪爨。

translations.literal: Flying thunder gathered, drums and gongs alarmed; autumn rain poured down, cutting off cooking fires.
translations.idiomatic: Thunder rolled and drums clamored; autumn rain poured down and our cooking fires went out.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，九里坳邊真瓦全，爾曹性命天所憐。」

translations.literal: Alas, by Jiuli'ao the roof tiles were truly whole; your lives, Heaven pities."
translations.idiomatic: Alas—by Jiuli'ao our roof tiles still stood whole; Heaven itself pitied your lives."

sentences.zh: 五章曰：「庭闈肅潔辭親族，薄田聊許資饘粥，震盪扁舟波复風，兒才卻聘家回祿。

translations.literal: The fifth chapter says: "The courtyard kept pure, we left kin; scant fields barely supplied gruel; tossed on a small boat, waves and wind again; the son had just refused a match when fire returned to the house.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth runs: "We kept the household pure and left our kin; a few fields barely fed us gruel; tossed on a small boat through wind and wave; my son had just refused a match when fire consumed our home.

sentences.zh: 此身直緣正氣生，機杼猶能活枵腹。

translations.literal: This body was born straight from upright qi; the loom still could sustain an empty belly.
translations.idiomatic: This body was born of upright spirit; the loom still kept our empty bellies alive.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，但原長作太平民，何嘗俯仰慚天人。」

translations.literal: Alas, I only wish to be a peaceful subject all my life—how could I ever bow and rise ashamed before Heaven and men?"
translations.idiomatic: Alas—I only pray to live always as a peaceful subject; how could I ever bow my head in shame before Heaven and men?"

sentences.zh: 秦甲祐妻劉，三原人。

translations.literal: Liu, wife of Qin Jiayou, was from Sanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu, the wife of Qin Jiayou, came from Sanyuan.

sentences.zh: 甲祐病瘓，劉侍疾甚謹，筦家政甚飭。

translations.literal: Jiayou was paralyzed by illness; Liu nursed him with great care and managed the household with great order.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiayou was paralyzed by illness, Liu nursed him with scrupulous care and ran the household with strict discipline.

sentences.zh: 越十年，甲祐卒，時歲饑，兵未定。

translations.literal: After ten years Jiayou died; at the time famine prevailed and the army was not yet settled.
translations.idiomatic: Ten years later Jiayou died, in a time of famine when the armies had not yet been pacified.

sentences.zh: 劉撫二子四符、四採。

translations.literal: Liu raised the two sons Sifu and Sicai.
translations.idiomatic: Liu raised her two sons, Sifu and Sicai.

sentences.zh: 嘗訓之曰：「年荒，眾人之荒；

translations.literal: She once admonished them, saying: "When the year is barren, that is everyone's barrenness;
translations.idiomatic: She once told them: "When the harvest fails, that is everyone's famine;

sentences.zh: 學荒，則吾兒之荒也。

translations.literal: when learning is barren, that is my sons' barrenness.
translations.idiomatic: when learning fails, that famine is yours alone.

sentences.zh: 兵亂，眾人之亂；

translations.literal: When soldiers are in turmoil, that is everyone's turmoil;
translations.idiomatic: When war rages, that is everyone's chaos;

sentences.zh: 心亂，則吾一家之亂也。」

translations.literal: when the heart is in turmoil, that is our family's turmoil."
translations.idiomatic: when the heart loses its way, that chaos is ours alone."

sentences.zh: 聞者以為名言。

translations.literal: Those who heard took it for a famous saying.
translations.idiomatic: All who heard it took it for a saying worth remembering.

sentences.zh: 四符，甲祐前婦子也，劉愛之，均於所生。

translations.literal: Sifu was son of Jiayou's former wife; Liu loved him equally to those she herself bore.
translations.idiomatic: Sifu was the son of Jiayou's first wife; Liu loved him no less than her own children.

sentences.zh: 艾懷元妻姜，米脂人。

translations.literal: Jiang, wife of Ai Huaiyuan, was from Mizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang, the wife of Ai Huaiyuan, came from Mizhi.

sentences.zh: 懷元父穆，兄懷英，在明皆官參將。

translations.literal: Huaiyuan's father Mu and elder brother Huaiying had both served as deputy generals under the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiyuan's father Mu and his elder brother Huaiying had both held the rank of deputy general under the Ming.

sentences.zh: 穆卒，國初懷英降，入鑲藍旗，授牛錄章京，居京師。

translations.literal: Mu died; at the beginning of the dynasty Huaiying surrendered, entered the Bordered Blue Banner, was appointed a company commander, and lived in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After Mu died, Huaiying surrendered early in the dynasty, entered the Bordered Blue Banner, was made a company commander, and lived in Beijing.

sentences.zh: 順治八年，懷元往省其兄，既歸，仇家誣為逃人，遂亡命。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Shunzhi, Huaiyuan went to visit his brother; after he returned, an enemy household falsely accused him as a fugitive, and he fled for his life.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 8 Huaiyuan went to visit his brother; when he returned home, enemies denounced him as a fugitive and he fled for his life.

sentences.zh: 官收其孥，穆妻馬，老矣，妾金請代，姜方娠，皆就逮。

translations.literal: The authorities seized his family; Mu's wife Ma was old; concubine Jin asked to take her place; Jiang was pregnant—all were taken into custody.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities seized his household: Mu's aged wife Ma, concubine Jin who offered to go in her stead, and Jiang, who was pregnant—all were arrested.

sentences.zh: 明年，事雪，西還。

translations.literal: The next year the matter was cleared and they returned west.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the case was cleared and they returned west.

sentences.zh: 姜襁稚子，金與相扶持，行數千里。

translations.literal: Jiang carried an infant son; Jin supported her, and they traveled several thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang carried an infant in her arms; Jin helped her along on a journey of thousands of li.

sentences.zh: 又明年，馬與金皆卒，懷元遣信至，言母死不得奔喪，誓畢生不歸。

translations.literal: The year after, Ma and Jin both died; Huaiyuan sent word that his mother had died and he could not return for mourning, vowing never to come back in this life.
translations.idiomatic: The following year both Ma and Jin died. Word came from Huaiyuan that his mother was dead and he could not return to mourn her; he swore never to come home again as long as he lived.

sentences.zh: 姜食貧撫子，居四十餘年乃卒。

translations.literal: Jiang lived in poverty raising her son and lived more than forty years before she died.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang lived in poverty raising her son and survived more than forty years before she died.

sentences.zh: 周子寬妻黃，順德倫教村人。

translations.literal: Huang, wife of Zhou Zikuan, was from Lunejiao village in Shunde.
translations.idiomatic: Huang, the wife of Zhou Zikuan, came from Lunejiao village in Shunde.

sentences.zh: 子寬刺船，與其侶戲，侶溺，坐減死戍貴定。

translations.literal: Zikuan poled a boat; playing with his companion, the companion drowned; he was sentenced to commuted death and exile to Guiding.
translations.idiomatic: Zikuan worked a ferry boat; while playing with a companion the man drowned, and Zikuan was sentenced to penal servitude in Guiding in place of death.

sentences.zh: 黃求從夫行，譁縣門，吏為註官書。

translations.literal: Huang asked to follow her husband; she clamored at the county gate until the clerk entered it in the official record.
translations.idiomatic: Huang begged to accompany her husband, raising such an outcry at the county gate that the clerk entered it in the official register.

sentences.zh: 乃盡鬻嫁時物畀舅姑，制竹擔荷具從夫行。

translations.literal: She then sold all her bridal goods and gave the proceeds to her parents-in-law, made bamboo carrying poles, and followed her husband.
translations.idiomatic: She sold everything from her dowry and gave the money to her parents-in-law, fashioned bamboo carrying poles, and set out with her husband.

sentences.zh: 夫道病，黃行經村市，操土音歌，求錢，得藥物酒食奉夫。

translations.literal: Her husband fell ill on the road; Huang passed through villages and markets, singing in the local dialect to beg money, and obtained medicine, wine, and food to serve her husband.
translations.idiomatic: When her husband fell ill on the road, Huang passed through villages and markets singing in the local dialect for coins, buying medicine, wine, and food for him.

sentences.zh: 夫瘳，達戍所。

translations.literal: When her husband recovered, they reached the place of exile.
translations.idiomatic: When he recovered they reached the place of exile.

sentences.zh: 居十七年，舉一子、二女，而夫死。

translations.literal: They lived there seventeen years; she bore one son and two daughters, then her husband died.
translations.idiomatic: They lived there seventeen years; she bore one son and two daughters, and then her husband died.

sentences.zh: 黃求以夫骨歸，跪縣門搏顙二十餘日，吏許之，畀以牒。

translations.literal: Huang asked to return her husband's bones; she knelt at the county gate and beat her forehead for more than twenty days until the clerk consented and gave her a travel document.
translations.idiomatic: Huang begged to bring her husband's bones home, knelt at the county gate and knocked her forehead on the ground for more than twenty days until the clerk agreed and gave her a travel permit.

sentences.zh: 黃懷牒裹夫骨，筥負小兒女，獨身以行。

translations.literal: Huang carried the document, wrapped her husband's bones, bore the small son and daughters in a basket, and traveled alone.
translations.idiomatic: Huang carried the permit, wrapped her husband's bones, bore her small son and daughters in a basket, and set out alone.

sentences.zh: 其長女已嫁農家子，牽衣泣，黃斥不顧。

translations.literal: Her eldest daughter had married a farmer's son; she clutched Huang's robe and wept, but Huang rebuked her and paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: Her eldest daughter had married a farmer's son; the girl clutched her mother's robe and wept, but Huang scolded her and would not look back.

sentences.zh: 黔多虎，而黃負夫骨，逆旅禁不納。

translations.literal: Guizhou had many tigers, and because Huang carried her husband's bones, inns forbade her entry.
translations.idiomatic: Guizhou swarmed with tigers, and because she carried her husband's bones the inns would not admit her.

sentences.zh: 日汲於澗，拾樹枝以爨，夜宿道旁廢廟，恆見虎殘人，餘骼狼藉，無所怖。

translations.literal: By day she drew water from streams and gathered branches to cook; by night she slept in ruined temples beside the road, constantly seeing tigers maul people, bones scattered everywhere—yet she was not afraid.
translations.idiomatic: By day she drew water from the streams and gathered firewood; by night she slept in ruined temples along the road, often seeing tigers tear people apart and bones strewn about—yet she was not afraid.

sentences.zh: 及至村，黃齒既長，黧黑醜惡，又雜羅施語。

translations.literal: When she reached the village, Huang's teeth had grown long, her face was dark and ugly, and she also spoke a mix of Luoshi dialect.
translations.idiomatic: When she reached the village her teeth had grown long, her face was dark and gaunt, and she spoke a jumble of Luoshi dialect.

sentences.zh: 有叟獨識之，指道旁塚曰：「此而翁也，而姑僵牆陰，不食已一日。」

translations.literal: An old man alone recognized her and, pointing at a grave by the road, said: "This is your father-in-law; your mother-in-law lies stiff in the wall's shade, having eaten nothing for a day."
translations.idiomatic: One old man alone recognized her and pointed at a grave by the road: "That is your husband's grave; your mother-in-law lies stiff in the shade of the wall—she has not eaten for a day."

sentences.zh: 黃求得姑，姑兩目眊，黃引其手拊裹中骨，及筥中兒女。

translations.literal: Huang found her mother-in-law; the old woman's eyes were dim; Huang guided her hand to feel the bones in the wrapping and the children in the basket.
translations.idiomatic: Huang found her mother-in-law, whose eyes were nearly blind; she guided the old woman's hand to the bones in the bundle and to the children in the basket.

sentences.zh: 姑抱而噎，黃大號，筥中兒女亦號。

translations.literal: The mother-in-law embraced them and choked with sobs; Huang wailed loudly, and the children in the basket wailed too.
translations.idiomatic: The mother-in-law embraced them and sobbed until she choked; Huang cried out, and the children in the basket cried too.

sentences.zh: 鄉里皆走視，義之，畀以金，僦屋奉姑居。

translations.literal: The whole neighborhood came to look; moved by righteousness, they gave her money and rented a house for her to support her mother-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Neighbors came running to see; moved by her devotion, they gave her money and rented a house where she could care for her mother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 黃行逮歸十九年，順德人號曰「女蘇武」。

translations.literal: Huang's journey there and back took nineteen years; people of Shunde called her "the female Su Wu."
translations.idiomatic: Her journey out and back took nineteen years; the people of Shunde called her "the female Su Wu."

sentences.zh: 李有成妻王，常寧人。

translations.literal: Wang, wife of Li Youcheng, was from Changning.
translations.idiomatic: Wang, the wife of Li Youcheng, came from Changning.

sentences.zh: 寡，悉散奩飾於族鄰貧者。

translations.literal: A widow, she distributed all her trousseau ornaments to poor kin and neighbors.
translations.idiomatic: As a widow she gave away all her trousseau ornaments to poor kin and neighbors.

sentences.zh: 將卒，呼諸婦曰：「吾寡居四十餘年，耳目如聾瞶，未嘗妄視聽，汝曹其識之！」

translations.literal: When she was about to die, she called the women and said: "I have lived as a widow more than forty years; my ears and eyes are as if deaf and blind—I have never looked or listened amiss. You must remember this!"
translations.idiomatic: On her deathbed she called the women and said: "I have been a widow more than forty years; my ears and eyes might as well have been deaf and blind—I never looked or listened amiss. Remember this!"

sentences.zh: 楊方勗妻劉，宣城人。

translations.literal: Liu, wife of Yang Fangxu, was from Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu, the wife of Yang Fangxu, came from Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 嫁五日而寡，剪髮自誓。

translations.literal: She had been married five days when widowed; she cut her hair and swore an oath.
translations.idiomatic: Five days after her marriage she was widowed; she cut her hair and bound herself by oath.

sentences.zh: 鄰婦或微諷，劉出刀以示，曰：「吾晝以是為鏡，夜以是為枕。」

translations.literal: When a neighbor woman hinted obliquely, Liu produced a knife to show her and said: "By day I take this for my mirror; by night I take this for my pillow."
translations.idiomatic: When a neighbor woman dropped a hint, Liu showed her a knife and said: "By day this is my mirror; by night this is my pillow."

sentences.zh: 鄰婦懾，不敢復言。

translations.literal: The neighbor woman was frightened and dared speak no more.
translations.idiomatic: The neighbor was frightened and never spoke of it again.

sentences.zh: 鄒近泗妻邢，昆明人。

translations.literal: Xing, wife of Zou Jinsi, was from Kunming.
translations.idiomatic: Xing, the wife of Zou Jinsi, came from Kunming.

sentences.zh: 寡而貧，或諷之嫁，邢曰：「吾能忍飢寒，不能忍恥。」

translations.literal: A poor widow, when some hinted she should remarry, Xing said: "I can endure hunger and cold; I cannot endure shame."
translations.idiomatic: Poor and widowed, when some suggested she remarry, Xing said: "I can endure hunger and cold; I cannot endure shame."

sentences.zh: 卒以節終。

translations.literal: She ended her life in chastity.
translations.idiomatic: She lived out her days in virtue.

sentences.zh: 胡源渤妻董，臨清人。

translations.literal: Dong, wife of Hu Yuanbo, was from Linqing.
translations.idiomatic: Dong, the wife of Hu Yuanbo, came from Linqing.

sentences.zh: 源渤卒，董年十五，為嫠八十年，年九十五乃卒。

translations.literal: Yuanbo died when Dong was fifteen; she was a widow eighty years and died at ninety-five.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanbo died when Dong was fifteen; she remained a widow eighty years and died at ninety-five.

sentences.zh: 裡婦或問：「守節易乎？」

translations.literal: Village women sometimes asked: "Is preserving chastity easy?"
translations.idiomatic: Village women sometimes asked her: "Is it easy to keep your chastity?"

translations.literal: She said: "Easy."
translations.idiomatic: She answered: "Easy."

sentences.zh: 「如無夫何？」

translations.literal: What about having no husband?"
translations.idiomatic: What about having no husband?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「如未嫁。」

translations.literal: She said: "As if never married."
translations.idiomatic: She said: "As if I had never married."

sentences.zh: 「如無子何？」

translations.literal: What about having no son?"
translations.idiomatic: What about having no son?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「如有子而死若不孝。」

translations.literal: She said: "As if having a son who died would be unfilial."
translations.idiomatic: She said: "As if I had a son who died—what would unfilial conduct matter then?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「何以製此心？」

translations.literal: How do you restrain this heart?"
translations.idiomatic: How do you restrain your heart?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「飢而食，倦而寢，不飢不倦，必有事焉，毋坐而嬉。

translations.literal: She said: "When hungry, eat; when weary, sleep; when neither hungry nor weary, there must be work—do not sit idle in play.
translations.idiomatic: She said: "When hungry, eat; when tired, sleep; when neither hungry nor tired, keep busy—never sit idle.

sentences.zh: 吾嘗為人傭，治女紅，必求其工。

translations.literal: I once worked as a hired hand at needlework and always demanded excellence in the craft.
translations.idiomatic: I once worked for others at needlework and always demanded the finest workmanship.

sentences.zh: 求工，則心專；

translations.literal: Seek excellence, and the heart is focused;
translations.idiomatic: Demand excellence, and the mind concentrates;

sentences.zh: 心專，則力勤；

translations.literal: when the heart is focused, strength is diligent;
translations.idiomatic: concentrate the mind, and the body works hard;

sentences.zh: 力勤，則勞而易倦。

translations.literal: when strength is diligent, one labors and grows weary easily.
translations.idiomatic: work hard, and weariness comes easily.

sentences.zh: 倦即寢，寤即興，毋使一息閒，久之則習慣矣。」

translations.literal: When weary, sleep; when awake, rise; allow not a moment's idleness—in time it becomes habit."
translations.idiomatic: Sleep when weary, rise when awake, never let a moment go idle—in time it becomes second nature."

sentences.zh: 林國奎妻鄭，閩人。

translations.literal: Zheng, wife of Lin Guokui, was from Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng, the wife of Lin Guokui, came from Fujian.

sentences.zh: 國奎卒，有子二。

translations.literal: Guokui died, leaving two sons.
translations.idiomatic: When Guokui died he left two sons.

sentences.zh: 鄭將殉，姑誡以存孤，乃已。

translations.literal: Zheng was about to follow him in death; her mother-in-law admonished her to preserve the orphans, and she desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng was ready to die with him, but her mother-in-law urged her to live for the orphans, and she desisted.

sentences.zh: 一子殤，遂自沉於江，漁者拯以還。

translations.literal: When one son died young, she threw herself into the river; fishermen rescued and brought her back.
translations.idiomatic: When one son died in infancy she drowned herself in the river; fishermen pulled her out and brought her back.

sentences.zh: 姑疾，刲肝雜糜進，疾良已。

translations.literal: When her mother-in-law fell ill, she cut out part of her liver, mixed it with gruel, and fed her; the illness was soon cured.
translations.idiomatic: When her mother-in-law fell ill she cut a piece of her own liver, mixed it into gruel, and fed it to her; the illness soon passed.

sentences.zh: 族有亡賴子嘗中夜至，告族人杖於宗祠。

translations.literal: A ruffian kinsman once came in the middle of the night; she reported him to the clan, who beat him in the ancestral hall.
translations.idiomatic: A worthless kinsman once came at midnight; she reported him to the clan, who flogged him in the ancestral hall.

sentences.zh: 亡賴子為嫚書汙鄭，鄭恚，取刀斷左耳，訟於縣，縣笞亡賴子。

translations.literal: The ruffian wrote an obscene letter defiling Zheng; enraged, Zheng took a knife and severed her left ear, sued at the county, and the county flogged the ruffian.
translations.idiomatic: The ruffian wrote a lewd letter slandering her; furious, Zheng cut off her own left ear and brought suit at the county yamen; the magistrate had the man flogged.

sentences.zh: 亡賴子出，益妄語，鄭复割右耳。

translations.literal: When the ruffian was released he spoke even more wildly; Zheng again cut off her right ear.
translations.idiomatic: When the man was released he slandered her all the more; Zheng cut off her right ear as well.

sentences.zh: 巡撫卞永譽聞其事，坐轅門讞其獄，令隸以兩耳示觀者，械亡賴子至，閱嫚書一行，輒撻其面，復重榜荷校論戍邊。

translations.literal: Governor Bian Yongyu heard of the affair, sat at the yamen gate to try the case, had an attendant show Zheng's two ears to the onlookers, brought the ruffian in shackles, and for each line of the obscene letter struck his face, then sentenced him to heavy flogging, cangue, and exile to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Bian Yongyu heard of the case, held court at the yamen gate, had a clerk display Zheng's severed ears to the crowd, brought the ruffian in chains, and for each line of the lewd letter struck his face, then sentenced him to heavy flogging, the cangue, and exile to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 居數月，鄭兩耳復生，永譽复坐轅門，召而察之，左耳完且晰，右耳赤如血，下廓乃微赬而短於左。

translations.literal: After several months Zheng's two ears grew back; Yongyu again sat at the yamen gate, summoned her and examined them—the left ear was whole and clear, the right ear red as blood, its lower rim slightly flushed and shorter than the left.
translations.idiomatic: Months later both of Zheng's ears had grown back; Yongyu again held court at the gate, summoned her, and inspected them—the left was whole and clear, the right red as blood, its lower rim slightly flushed and shorter than the left.

sentences.zh: 文武吏及諸觀者皆驚嘆，一時稱異事雲。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials and all onlookers marveled; for a time it was called a wonder.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials and all who looked on were astonished; for a time the story was hailed as a marvel.

sentences.zh: 陳仁道妻龐，博白人。

translations.literal: Pang, wife of Chen Rendao, was from Bobai.
translations.idiomatic: Pang, the wife of Chen Rendao, came from Bobai.

sentences.zh: 康熙十九年，吳三桂將程可任掠博白，仁道將與鄰人拒之，為所殺。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Kangxi, Wu Sangui's general Cheng Keren raided Bobai; Rendao was about to resist with neighbors and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 19 Wu Sangui's general Cheng Keren raided Bobai; Rendao was about to resist with his neighbors and was killed.

sentences.zh: 龐自經，家人救之，甦，乃斥產購得殺仁道者，殺諸仁道墓前。

translations.literal: Pang hanged herself; her family saved her and she revived, then sold property to buy the man who had killed Rendao and executed him before Rendao's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Pang hanged herself; her family revived her. She sold her property, bought the man who had killed her husband, and had him executed before Rendao's grave.

sentences.zh: 張某妻秦，三原人。

translations.literal: Qin, wife of a man surnamed Zhang, was from Sanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Qin, the wife of a man surnamed Zhang, came from Sanyuan.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十一年，仍歲大祲，縣民多流亡。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year of Kangxi, famine struck year after year and many in the county fled.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 31 famine struck year after year and many in the county fled as refugees.

sentences.zh: 秦內外無所依，至龍橋河北，河岸坼有隙，自匿​​其中，有老人憫之，遺以食。

translations.literal: Qin had no kin to rely on within or without; she came to the north bank of Longqiao River, where a crack in the riverbank offered a hiding place; she hid herself there; an old man pitied her and left her food.
translations.idiomatic: With no kin to turn to, she went to the north bank of Longqiao River, hid in a crack in the bank, and an old man took pity on her and left her food.

sentences.zh: 明日復往，則昨所遺故在，勸之食，且問故，秦曰：「謝翁厚，然不可為常，先後等死耳，我坐岸隙，令死不至暴露足矣。」

translations.literal: The next day he came again; the food left yesterday was still there; he urged her to eat and asked why; Qin said: "I thank you, sir, for your kindness, but this cannot be constant—sooner or later we die alike; I sit in the riverbank crack so that when I die my body will not lie exposed—that is enough."
translations.idiomatic: The next day he returned; the food he had left was untouched. He urged her to eat and asked why. Qin said: "I thank you for your kindness, sir, but I cannot live on charity—we all die sooner or later. I sit in this crack in the bank so that when I die I will not lie exposed in the open; that is enough."

sentences.zh: 遂餓而死，年二十餘。

translations.literal: She then starved to death at a little over twenty.
translations.idiomatic: She starved to death at a little over twenty.

sentences.zh: 老人為封焉。

translations.literal: The old man buried her.
translations.idiomatic: The old man gave her a burial.

sentences.zh: 同時李氏女，從父母逐食至漢口，父母皆疫死。

translations.literal: At the same time a daughter of the Li family followed her parents in search of food to Hankou; both parents died of plague.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time a daughter of the Li clan followed her parents in search of food to Hankou; both parents died of plague.

sentences.zh: 女年十六，美，儈聘焉，將鬻使為妓，女得其情，力求死。

translations.literal: The girl was sixteen and beautiful; a broker engaged her, intending to sell her as a prostitute; learning this, she strove to die.
translations.idiomatic: The girl was sixteen and beautiful; a broker had engaged her intending to sell her into prostitution; when she learned of it she begged for death.

sentences.zh: 三原人賈漢口者群詰儈，儈陰殺之。

translations.literal: Merchants from Sanyuan at Hankou questioned the broker in a group; the broker secretly killed her.
translations.idiomatic: Sanyuan merchants trading at Hankou questioned the broker in a body; the broker secretly killed her.

sentences.zh: 何某妻韓，張榮妻吳，張萬寶妻李，皆濰縣人。

translations.literal: Han, wife of a man surnamed He; Wu, wife of Zhang Rong; Li, wife of Zhang Wanbao—all were from Weixian.
translations.idiomatic: Han, wife of a man surnamed He; Wu, wife of Zhang Rong; Li, wife of Zhang Wanbao—all came from Weixian.

sentences.zh: 韓早寡，求疏屬子為後。

translations.literal: Han was widowed early and sought a distant kinsman's son as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Han was widowed young and adopted a distant kinsman's son as heir.

sentences.zh: 康熙四十三年，濰大饑，韓晝抱子拾薪，夜則紡績，日一食。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year of Kangxi, Weixian suffered great famine; by day Han carried her son gathering firewood, by night she spun, eating once a day.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 43 Weixian suffered a great famine; by day Han carried her son while gathering firewood, by night she spun, and ate once a day.

sentences.zh: 久之，有所蓄，非甚飢則不食。

translations.literal: After a long time she had some savings and would not eat unless very hungry.
translations.idiomatic: In time she saved a little and would not eat unless she was very hungry.

sentences.zh: 卒買宅娶婦生孫，年七十三卒。

translations.literal: In the end she bought a house, married a wife for her son, and had grandsons; she died at seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the end she bought a house, found a wife for her son, and had grandsons; she died at seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 吳嫁三日，夫死，貧甚，轉役自活，夜必歸其室。

translations.literal: Wu had been married three days when her husband died; extremely poor, she took odd jobs to live but always returned to her room at night.
translations.idiomatic: Wu had been married three days when her husband died. Utterly poor, she took day labor to live but always returned to her own room at night.

sentences.zh: 得米雜糠粃樹葉為食，贏一日食，則一日閉戶。

translations.literal: When she got rice she mixed it with chaff, bran, and leaves for food; if she earned a day's food, she shut her door for a day.
translations.idiomatic: When she had rice she mixed it with chaff, bran, and leaves; if she earned enough for a day she shut her door for that day.

sentences.zh: 年九十二，病將死，呼其侄，謂曰：「我有銀紉衣帶，猶昔吾夫物。

translations.literal: At ninety-two, gravely ill, she called her nephew and said: "I have a silver-threaded belt and sash—still my late husband's things.
translations.idiomatic: At ninety-two, on her deathbed, she called her nephew and said: "I have a silver-threaded belt and sash—still my late husband's things.

sentences.zh: 我死，以此市棺埋我夫墓側。」

translations.literal: When I die, use these to buy a coffin and bury me beside my husband's tomb."
translations.idiomatic: When I die, sell them for a coffin and bury me beside my husband's grave."

sentences.zh: 李嫁生子，方晬，而喪夫。

translations.literal: Li married and bore a son still at the breast when her husband died.
translations.idiomatic: Li married and bore a son still in swaddling clothes when her husband died.

sentences.zh: 舅、姑謂曰：「汝不幸，我曹老，子幼，汝當如何？」

translations.literal: Her father-in-law and mother-in-law said: "You are unfortunate; we are old, the child is young—what will you do?"
translations.idiomatic: Her parents-in-law said: "You are unlucky; we are old and the child is young—what will you do?"

sentences.zh: 李泣曰：「婦非為舅姑老子幼，夫死何所不得？

translations.literal: Li wept and said: "It is not for my parents-in-law's sake or the child's that I live—when a husband dies, what may a wife not do?
translations.idiomatic: Li wept and said: "It is not for you or the child that I stay—when one's husband dies, what may a wife not do?

sentences.zh: 猶忍活至此，婦自審已決，原舅姑無疑。」

translations.literal: Yet I have endured life to this point; I have examined myself and my resolve is firm—I pray my parents-in-law harbor no doubt."
translations.idiomatic: Yet I have endured until now; I have examined my heart and my resolve is firm—please do not doubt me."

sentences.zh: 舅賣漿，暮出戶，聞鐸聲，必趨往代其擔。

translations.literal: Her father-in-law sold gruel; when he went out at dusk and she heard the bell, she always hurried to take his load.
translations.idiomatic: Her father-in-law sold gruel; when he went out at dusk and she heard his bell, she always ran to carry his load for him.

sentences.zh: 抱子力作，人未嘗見其啟齒。

translations.literal: Carrying her son she labored hard; people never saw her show her teeth in a smile.
translations.idiomatic: She labored with her child in her arms; no one ever saw her smile.

sentences.zh: 既喪舅、姑，娶婦生孫乃卒。

translations.literal: After her parents-in-law died, she married a wife for her son and had grandsons before she died.
translations.idiomatic: After her parents-in-law died she found a wife for her son and had grandsons before she passed away.

sentences.zh: 疾革，謂其子曰：「我死得見汝父，我甚喜，汝勿悲也！」

translations.literal: On her deathbed she told her son: "In death I shall see your father—I am very glad; do not grieve!"
translations.idiomatic: On her deathbed she told her son: "In death I shall see your father—I am glad; do not grieve!"

sentences.zh: 韓居縣東南草廟村，吳居縣西張家村，李居縣北長甿村。

translations.literal: Han lived in Caomiao village southeast of the county, Wu in Zhangjia village west of the county, Li in Changmeng village north of the county.
translations.idiomatic: Han lived in Caomiao village in the county's southeast, Wu in Zhangjia village in the west, and Li in Changmeng village in the north.

sentences.zh: 沈學顏妻尤，仁和人。

translations.literal: You, wife of Shen Xueyan, was from Renhe.
translations.idiomatic: You, the wife of Shen Xueyan, came from Renhe.

sentences.zh: 學顏卒，無子，以從子時吉為後。

translations.literal: Xueyan died without sons; they made his nephew Shiji heir.
translations.idiomatic: When Xueyan died without sons, they made his nephew Shiji the heir.

sentences.zh: 時吉生子大震，又卒。

translations.literal: Shiji bore a son Dazhen, then died again.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji fathered a son named Dazhen, then died in turn.

sentences.zh: 尤撫孤孫，其兄侮之。

translations.literal: You raised the orphaned grandson; her elder brother bullied her.
translations.idiomatic: You raised the orphaned grandson while her elder brother bullied her.

sentences.zh: 秋將穫，以眾刈其禾，尤置針於髻末，外向踴而號，兄提其發，針創手乃去。

translations.literal: When autumn harvest neared, he brought a crowd to reap her grain; You placed needles at the end of her hair bun pointing outward and leaped about wailing; her brother seized her hair, was wounded by the needles, and left.
translations.idiomatic: At harvest time her brother brought men to reap her grain; You stuck needles in her hair bun pointing outward and leaped about wailing; her brother seized her hair, cut his hand on the needles, and left.

sentences.zh: 常恨其孫弱，曰：「我安得見曾孫，見曾孫，死不恨。」

translations.literal: She often grieved that her grandson was frail and said: "How might I live to see a great-grandson? If I see a great-grandson, I shall die without regret."
translations.idiomatic: She often lamented that her grandson was frail and said: "How can I live to see a great-grandson? If I see one, I shall die content."

sentences.zh: 大震娶婦舉子，尤乃卒。

translations.literal: Dazhen married and had a son; then You died.
translations.idiomatic: Dazhen married and had a son; then You died.

sentences.zh: 既卒，大震复舉子近思，自有傳。

translations.literal: After she died, Dazhen again had a son Jinsi, who has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: After her death Dazhen had another son, Jinsi, who has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 王賜紱妻時，黃平人。

translations.literal: Shi, wife of Wang Cifu, was from Huangping.
translations.idiomatic: Shi, the wife of Wang Cifu, came from Huangping.

sentences.zh: 賜紱出行，宿於翁丙，為苗所殺，棄屍箐中。

translations.literal: Cifu went on a journey and lodged at Wengbing; Miao killed him and cast his body in a ravine.
translations.idiomatic: Cifu was traveling and lodged at Wengbing; Miao tribesmen killed him and threw his body into a ravine.

sentences.zh: 時行求得之，告官，得苗五，俱伏罪，時年二十一。

translations.literal: Shi went and found the body, reported to the authorities, and five Miao were seized, all confessing guilt; Shi was twenty-one.
translations.idiomatic: Shi found the body, reported to the authorities, and five Miao were captured and confessed; she was twenty-one.

sentences.zh: 母欲令更嫁，剪髮、烙左頰，毀容矢不行。

translations.literal: Her mother wished her to remarry; she cut her hair, branded her left cheek, disfigured herself, and swore never to marry.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother wanted her to remarry; she cut her hair, branded her left cheek, disfigured her face, and swore never to marry again.

sentences.zh: 王某妻張，灤州人。

translations.literal: Zhang, wife of a man surnamed Wang, was from Luanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang, the wife of a man surnamed Wang, came from Luanzhou.

sentences.zh: 早寡，無子。

translations.literal: Widowed early, without sons.
translations.idiomatic: She was widowed young and had no sons.

sentences.zh: 以族子曰琦後，亦早卒，妻魏，亦州人。

translations.literal: She made a clansman's son Ziqi heir; he too died young; his wife Wei was also from the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: She adopted a clansman's son, Ziqi, as heir; he too died young. His wife Wei was also from the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 所居村曰柳河，地卑濕，食不足，掇草根木葉，拾蘋藻，雜糠粃以食其孤，复殤。

translations.literal: Their village was called Liuhe; the land was low and damp, food scarce; they gathered roots, leaves, and duckweed, mixed chaff and bran to feed the orphan, who again died young.
translations.idiomatic: They lived in Liuhe village, where the land was low and damp and food was scarce; they gathered roots, leaves, and duckweed and mixed chaff and bran to feed the orphan, who again died in infancy.

sentences.zh: 復以族子後。

translations.literal: Again they made a clansman's son heir.
translations.idiomatic: Again they adopted a clansman's son as heir.

sentences.zh: 張卒，族人諷魏嫁，魏不可。

translations.literal: When Zhang died, clansmen hinted that Wei should remarry; Wei would not.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang died, clansmen suggested Wei remarry; she refused.

sentences.zh: 居十餘年，為所後子娶婦，乃語所親曰：「吾乃今志始遂，使嫁，不過溫飽死耳。

translations.literal: After more than ten years she found a wife for the adopted son, then told those close to her: "Only now is my purpose fulfilled; had I remarried, I would only have died fed and clothed.
translations.idiomatic: After more than ten years she found a wife for the adopted son, then told her intimates: "Only now is my purpose fulfilled; had I remarried I would merely have died fed and clothed.

sentences.zh: 人恆苦貧，吾獨不自覺。

translations.literal: People always suffer from poverty; I alone am unaware of it.
translations.idiomatic: Others always complain of poverty; I alone never feel it.

sentences.zh: 苦皆自樂生，吾生不知為樂，又焉知有苦？」

translations.literal: Suffering all springs from taking pleasure in life; my life knows no pleasure—how then could I know suffering?"
translations.idiomatic: Suffering comes from taking pleasure in life; my life knows no pleasure—how then could I know suffering?"

sentences.zh: 州又有李學詩妻趙，學書妻高，娣姒以節著。

translations.literal: In the prefecture were also Zhao, wife of Li Xueshi, and Gao, wife of Li Xueshu—sisters-in-law famed for their chastity.
translations.idiomatic: In the same prefecture Zhao, wife of Li Xueshi, and Gao, wife of Li Xueshu—sisters-in-law—were likewise renowned for their virtue.

sentences.zh: 學詩、學書生友愛，行涉水，學書誤就深，學詩拯之，相抱持俱死。

translations.literal: The wives of Li Xueshi and Li Xueshu were deeply affectionate; walking and wading through water, Xueshu's wife by mistake entered the deep, Xueshi's wife rescued her, and embracing each other they both died.
translations.idiomatic: The wives of the brothers Li Xueshi and Li Xueshu were devoted friends. Once, wading through a stream, Xueshu's wife stumbled into deep water; Xueshi's wife rushed to save her, and the two clung to each other until both drowned.

sentences.zh: 趙生二女，高無出，食貧堅守，年皆逾八十。

translations.literal: Zhao bore two daughters; Gao had no offspring; eating in poverty they steadfastly kept their chastity, and both passed eighty years of age.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao bore two daughters, while Gao had no children; though they lived in bitter poverty, both remained faithful widows and lived past eighty.

sentences.zh: 高明妻劉，秦安人，早寡，子步雲幼。

translations.literal: Liu, wife of Gao Ming, was a native of Qin'an; widowed early, her son Buyun was young.
translations.idiomatic: Liu, the wife of Gao Ming of Qin'an, was widowed while still young, with a small son named Buyun.

sentences.zh: 貧甚，嘗伺鄰家炊，乞餘熱為兒煁餅。

translations.literal: Extremely poor, she would watch a neighbor's cooking and beg leftover heat to bake cakes for her son.
translations.idiomatic: They were desperately poor; she would wait until a neighbor's fire had nearly gone out, then beg the embers' warmth to bake a little cake for the boy.

sentences.zh: 步雲稍長，就學歸，則燃燈讀。

translations.literal: When Buyun grew somewhat, returning from school she would light a lamp for him to read.
translations.idiomatic: As Buyun grew older and came home from his studies, Liu would light a lamp so he could read at night.

sentences.zh: 劉縫紉，夜必盡數線。

translations.literal: Liu sewed and stitched; every night she had to use up several skeins of thread.
translations.idiomatic: Liu sewed for a living and never went to bed until she had used up every skein of thread she had set out for the night.

sentences.zh: 一夕，線未盡，步雲倦臥，撫之有淚跡，問曰：「兒耶病？」

translations.literal: One evening the thread was not finished; Buyun, weary, lay down to sleep; feeling him she found tear traces and asked, "Son, are you ill?"
translations.idiomatic: One night, before she had finished her thread, Buyun fell asleep from exhaustion; when she touched his face she found it wet with tears and asked, "Are you sick, my son?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「無之，但飢耳！」

translations.literal: He said, "No; only hungry!"
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "No—I'm just hungry!"

sentences.zh: 劉泫然曰：「兒不慣餓，我則常耳！」

translations.literal: Liu, tears falling, said, "You are not used to hunger; for me it is ordinary!"
translations.idiomatic: Liu wept and said, "You aren't used to going hungry—but I am!"

sentences.zh: 步雲為賈，家漸起。

translations.literal: Buyun became a merchant, and the family gradually prospered.
translations.idiomatic: Buyun later went into trade, and the household slowly recovered its fortunes.

sentences.zh: 鄧汝明妻劉，崇善人。

translations.literal: Liu, wife of Deng Ruming, was a native of Chongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu, the wife of Deng Ruming, came from Chongshan.

sentences.zh: 康熙四十一年，歲大無，官煮粥食饑民，劉不食五日。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year of Kangxi there was a great famine; the government cooked porridge to feed the hungry, and Liu did not eat for five days.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year of the Kangxi reign, famine struck the land; though the authorities served gruel to the starving, Liu went five days without food.

sentences.zh: 鄰家招偕赴，劉恥之，三出三返，終不行。

translations.literal: A neighbor invited her to go together; Liu was ashamed, went out three times and returned three times, and in the end did not go.
translations.idiomatic: A neighbor urged her to go to the relief kitchen with her, but Liu was too ashamed; three times she set out and three times turned back, and she never went.

sentences.zh: 因投水，漁人拯之，坐岸側，漁人去，復入水死。

translations.literal: Thereupon she threw herself into the water; a fisherman saved her, and she sat on the bank; when the fisherman left, she entered the water again and died.
translations.idiomatic: She then threw herself into the river. A fisherman pulled her out, but once he had gone and she was sitting alone on the bank, she went back into the water and drowned.

sentences.zh: 魏國棟妻龐，蠡縣龐家莊人。

translations.literal: Pang, wife of Wei Guodong, was from Pangjiazhuang in Li County.
translations.idiomatic: Pang, the wife of Wei Guodong, came from Pangjiazhuang in Li County.

sentences.zh: 祖姑徐、姑董，皆節婦。

translations.literal: Her husband's grandmother Xu and her aunt Dong were both chaste widows.
translations.idiomatic: Both her husband's grandmother, née Xu, and her aunt, née Dong, had been exemplary chaste widows.

sentences.zh: 國棟卒，無子，龐力女紅以養。

translations.literal: Guodong died without a son; Pang labored at women's needlework to support the household.
translations.idiomatic: When Guodong died leaving no son, Pang supported the family through her own weaving and sewing.

sentences.zh: 織日一疋，或授以纑，織成必增重，曰：「糨所滋也。」

translations.literal: She wove one bolt a day; or if given hemp waste to weave, when finished the cloth was always heavier, and she said, "That is from the starch sizing."
translations.idiomatic: She wove a full bolt of cloth every day. When given coarse hemp to work with, the finished cloth always weighed more than expected; she would explain, "That's just the starch sizing."

sentences.zh: 或與值多一錢，不受。

translations.literal: If offered one extra cash in payment, she would not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: If a customer tried to pay her an extra cash, she refused it.

sentences.zh: 祖姑八十餘，目昏，向曝、如廁，躬負以出入。

translations.literal: Her husband's grandmother was over eighty, her eyes dim; for sunning and going to the privy, Pang personally carried her in and out.
translations.idiomatic: Her husband's grandmother was in her eighties and nearly blind; Pang personally carried her outside to sun herself and to the privy.

sentences.zh: 姑亦至八十，負出入如之。

translations.literal: Her aunt also reached eighty, and Pang carried her in and out in the same way.
translations.idiomatic: When her aunt too reached eighty, Pang cared for her in just the same way.

sentences.zh: 再居喪，有周之者，龐曰：「吾貧，幸相貸，然必償。

translations.literal: During a second period of mourning, when someone gave her relief, Pang said, "I am poor and am fortunate that you lend to me, but I must repay.
translations.idiomatic: During a second mourning period, when neighbors offered her aid, Pang said, "I am poor and grateful for your help, but I must pay you back.

sentences.zh: 如不使我償，是視我非人也。」

translations.literal: If you do not let me repay, that is treating me as not a proper person."
translations.idiomatic: If you won't let me repay you, you're treating me as though I weren't a person of honor."

sentences.zh: 日夜織，不期月皆償。

translations.literal: Day and night she wove, and within less than a month all was repaid.
translations.idiomatic: She wove day and night and repaid every debt within the month.

sentences.zh: 當葬，衰而前柩，或請代，龐曰：「我祖姑、我姑無子孫，我在，即其子孫也，可代乎？」

translations.literal: At the funeral she walked before the coffin in mourning dress; when someone offered to take her place, Pang said, "My husband's grandmother and my aunt have no other descendants—as long as I live, I am their child. How could anyone stand in for me?"
translations.idiomatic: At the funeral she walked before the coffin in mourning dress; when someone offered to take her place, Pang said, "My husband's grandmother and my aunt have no other descendants—as long as I live, I am their child. How could anyone stand in for me?"

sentences.zh: 姑葬以夏，方雨，龐涉潦號踴，見者皆流涕。

translations.literal: Her aunt was buried in summer, just as it was raining; Pang waded through the floodwater wailing and lamenting, and all who saw it wept.
translations.idiomatic: Her aunt was buried in summer during a downpour; Pang waded through the flooded ground, wailing as she walked, and everyone who watched wept.

sentences.zh: 雍正三年，縣大水，歲無。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongzheng the county suffered great flooding and crop failure.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Yongzheng reign, catastrophic floods left the county without a harvest.

sentences.zh: 有縣治賑役自戶外呼告之，龐曰：「婦固飢，然食朝廷米，償否？」

translations.literal: A county relief worker called to her from outside; Pang asked, "I am hungry, yes—but if I eat the government's grain, will I have to repay it?"
translations.idiomatic: A county relief worker called to her from outside; Pang asked, "I am hungry, yes—but if I eat the government's grain, will I have to repay it?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「賑也，何償？」

translations.literal: He replied, "It's famine relief—why would you repay it?"
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "It's famine relief—why would you repay it?"

sentences.zh: 龐曰：「償則食，不償，則我孱婦何功報朝廷而徒食乎？

translations.literal: Pang said, "If it must be repaid then I will eat; if not, what merit has this frail woman to repay the court, that she should eat for nothing?
translations.idiomatic: Pang said, "If I can repay it, I'll eat; if not, what have I ever done for the state that I should eat its grain for free?

sentences.zh: 不可！」

translations.literal: I cannot!"
translations.idiomatic: I won't do it!"

sentences.zh: 遂鍵戶，复呼之，不應。

translations.literal: Thereupon she bolted the door; he called again, and she did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: She bolted the door. When he called again, she would not respond.

sentences.zh: 縣使役具刺歸之米一石，龐复辭。

translations.literal: The county sent the worker with a letter and one shi of rice as a return gift; Pang again declined.
translations.idiomatic: The county then sent the worker back with an official letter and a gift of one shi of rice, but Pang refused that too.

sentences.zh: 役曰：「此喬令君所以旌節義，毋辭！」

translations.literal: The worker said, "This is how Magistrate Qiao honors your chastity and righteousness—do not decline!"
translations.idiomatic: The worker said, "Magistrate Qiao is sending this to honor your virtue—please accept it!"

sentences.zh: 乃拜而受。

translations.literal: Thereupon she bowed and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did she bow and accept the gift.

sentences.zh: 縣上其事，得旌，族人為立後。

translations.literal: The county reported the matter; she received commendation, and the clan established an heir for her.
translations.idiomatic: The county reported her conduct to the throne; she received an official commendation, and her clan arranged for an heir to carry on the line.

sentences.zh: 呂才智妻王，博興人。

translations.literal: Wang, wife of Lü Caizhi, was a native of Boxing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang, the wife of Lü Caizhi, came from Boxing.

sentences.zh: 才智病傴僂，杖而行，鬻餅於市。

translations.literal: Caizhi was sick with a hunchback, walked with a cane, and sold cakes in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Caizhi was crippled by a hunchback, hobbled with a cane, and sold cakes in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 歲祲，才智將鬻王，王曰：「汝病廢，我去，汝不得生！

translations.literal: In a famine year Caizhi was about to sell Wang; Wang said, "You are sick and crippled; if I leave, you cannot survive!
translations.idiomatic: During a famine Caizhi planned to sell her; Wang said, "You're sick and helpless—if I leave, you won't survive!

sentences.zh: 且我身值幾何？

translations.literal: Moreover, what is my body worth?
translations.idiomatic: Besides, what would my body even fetch?

sentences.zh: 汝不過得數日飽。

translations.literal: You would only get a few days' full stomach.
translations.idiomatic: You'd only buy yourself a few days of full meals.

sentences.zh: 食盡，終當死。

translations.literal: When the food is gone, in the end you must still die.
translations.idiomatic: Once that food runs out, you'll starve anyway.

sentences.zh: 等死，不如相依死也。」

translations.literal: If we're going to die either way, we'd be better off dying together."
translations.idiomatic: If we're going to die either way, we'd be better off dying together."

sentences.zh: 乃令才智守舍，而出行乞。

translations.literal: Thereupon she had Caizhi guard the house while she went out begging.
translations.idiomatic: She made Caizhi stay home and went out to beg for food herself.

sentences.zh: 生一子，才智死，終不嫁。

translations.literal: She bore one son; when Caizhi died, she never remarried.
translations.idiomatic: She bore a son; after Caizhi died, she never remarried.

sentences.zh: 許爾臣妻駱，肅寧人。

translations.literal: Luo, wife of Xu Erchen, was a native of Suining.
translations.idiomatic: Luo, the wife of Xu Erchen, came from Suining.

sentences.zh: 家奇貧。

translations.literal: The family was extremely poor.
translations.idiomatic: The household was desperately poor.

sentences.zh: 爾臣及其父母相繼卒，駱號於市，得柳棺瘞焉。

translations.literal: Erchen and his parents died in succession; Luo cried out in the market, obtained willow coffins, and buried them.
translations.idiomatic: Erchen and his parents died one after another; Luo wailed in the marketplace until she scraped together willow-wood coffins and buried them all.

sentences.zh: 或勸：「盍嫁？」

translations.literal: People urged her, "Why not remarry?"
translations.idiomatic: People urged her, "Why not remarry?"

sentences.zh: 駱曰：「乞食雖辱，猶勝於再嫁！」

translations.literal: Luo said, "Begging for food, though shameful, is still better than remarrying!"
translations.idiomatic: Luo replied, "Begging is humiliating, but it's still better than taking another husband!"

sentences.zh: 卒以窮餓死。

translations.literal: In the end she died of poverty and starvation.
translations.idiomatic: In the end she died of hunger and want.

sentences.zh: 原某妻馬，河津人。

translations.literal: Ma, wife of a man surnamed Yuan, was a native of Hejin.
translations.idiomatic: Ma, the wife of a man surnamed Yuan, came from Hejin.

sentences.zh: 康熙六十年，飢，行乞食。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year of Kangxi there was famine; she went begging for food.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixtieth year of the Kangxi reign, famine drove her to beg for food.

sentences.zh: 泣語人曰：「乞食至辱，不如死，顧安得死所無累人耶？」

translations.literal: In tears she told people, "Begging is the deepest humiliation—I'd rather die, but where can I die without becoming a burden to anyone?"
translations.idiomatic: In tears she told people, "Begging is the deepest humiliation—I'd rather die, but where can I die without becoming a burden to anyone?"

sentences.zh: 或漫應曰：「去此十餘裡，有紅石崖，死此，可無累。」

translations.literal: Someone answered casually, "Ten-odd li from here is Red Stone Cliff; die there and you will not burden anyone."
translations.idiomatic: Someone answered offhandedly, "There's a Red Stone Cliff about ten li from here—die there and you won't burden anyone."

sentences.zh: 馬明日徑至其所，脫耳環易餅，遲鄰人過者，囑以畀其母，曰：「為我語母，無復望我，我今死此矣！」

translations.literal: The next day Ma went straight there, removed her earrings to exchange for cakes, waited for a passing neighbor, and entrusted a message to give to her mother, saying, "Tell my mother for me: do not hope for me anymore—I die here now!"
translations.idiomatic: The next day Ma went straight there, traded her earrings for a cake, stopped a passing neighbor, and asked him to tell her mother, "Tell Mother not to wait for me anymore—I am dying here today!"

sentences.zh: 即投崖下死。

translations.literal: Thereupon she threw herself off the cliff and died.
translations.idiomatic: Then she leapt from the cliff to her death.

sentences.zh: 張揚名妻彭，臨江人。

translations.literal: Peng, wife of Zhang Yangming, was a native of Linjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Peng, the wife of Zhang Yangming, came from Linjiang.

sentences.zh: 早寡，貧，或謂行乞可得食，彭唾之，曰：「我亦書生婦，有餓死張氏舍耳​​，安能為丐？」

translations.literal: Widowed young and left destitute, when someone suggested she could survive by begging, Peng spat in disgust and said, "I am a scholar's wife. I'd rather starve in the Zhang household than become a beggar!"
translations.idiomatic: Widowed young and left destitute, when someone suggested she could survive by begging, Peng spat in disgust and said, "I am a scholar's wife. I'd rather starve in the Zhang household than become a beggar!"

sentences.zh: 日夜操作，立後，娶婦，持門戶。

translations.literal: Day and night she worked; she established an heir, his wife was taken, and she maintained the household.
translations.idiomatic: She worked day and night, arranged for an heir, saw him married, and kept the household together.

sentences.zh: 沈萬裕妻王，浙江山陰人。

translations.literal: Wang, wife of Shen Wanyu, was a native of Shanyin in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang, the wife of Shen Wanyu, came from Shanyin in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 萬裕早失母，王事後姑謹。

translations.literal: Wanyu lost his mother early; Wang served her stepmother-in-law carefully.
translations.idiomatic: Wanyu had lost his mother young; Wang served her stepmother-in-law with scrupulous care.

sentences.zh: 萬裕卒，子幼，後姑虐使之。

translations.literal: Wanyu died, the son was young, and the stepmother-in-law abused and worked her.
translations.idiomatic: After Wanyu died, leaving a small son, her stepmother-in-law mistreated her and worked her mercilessly.

sentences.zh: 舅予田數畝，使別居。

translations.literal: Her maternal uncle gave her several mu of fields and had her live separately.
translations.idiomatic: Her maternal uncle gave her a few mu of land and set her up in a separate household.

sentences.zh: 後姑使嫁，王不可。

translations.literal: The stepmother-in-law urged her to remarry; Wang would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Her stepmother-in-law pressed her to remarry, but Wang refused.

sentences.zh: 後姑陰取犬子胞擲王室，陽出之，曰：「寡婦室，何乃有此？」

translations.literal: Her stepmother-in-law secretly placed a dog's afterbirth in Wang's room, then 'discovered' it and cried, "How could such a thing be found in a chaste widow's quarters?"
translations.idiomatic: Her stepmother-in-law secretly placed a dog's afterbirth in Wang's room, then 'discovered' it and cried, "How could such a thing be found in a chaste widow's quarters?"

sentences.zh: 迫嫁益厲。

translations.literal: She pressed remarriage all the more harshly.
translations.idiomatic: She then pressed Wang to remarry even more fiercely.

sentences.zh: 或語王：「當以死自明。」

translations.literal: Someone advised Wang, "You should die to prove your innocence."
translations.idiomatic: Someone advised Wang, "You should die to prove your innocence."

sentences.zh: 王曰：「吾當死。

translations.literal: Wang said, "I ought to die.
translations.idiomatic: Wang replied, "I am willing to die.

sentences.zh: 吾死孤不得生，夫且無祀，事終當白。

translations.literal: If I die the orphan cannot live, and my husband will have no sacrifices; the matter will eventually be cleared.
translations.idiomatic: But if I die, my son won't survive and my husband's line will go unserved—yet the truth will come out in time.

sentences.zh: 吾死，又誰吾明也？」

translations.literal: If I die now, who will be left to vindicate me?"
translations.idiomatic: If I die now, who will be left to vindicate me?"

sentences.zh: 藏其胞，事後姑愈謹。

translations.literal: She hid the afterbirth and served her stepmother-in-law even more carefully.
translations.idiomatic: She hid the afterbirth and continued serving her stepmother-in-law with even greater devotion.

sentences.zh: 後姑有少子訟於縣，知縣姚仁昌察胞非人，杖少子，而表王節。

translations.literal: The stepmother-in-law's younger son sued at the county; Magistrate Yao Renchang examined the afterbirth and saw it was not human; he beat the younger son and commended Wang's chastity.
translations.idiomatic: When the stepmother-in-law's younger son brought a case to the county court, Magistrate Yao Renchang examined the afterbirth and found it was not human; he had the younger son beaten and publicly honored Wang's virtue.

sentences.zh: 其後少子死，王收其孤，為娶婦。

translations.literal: Afterward the younger son died; Wang took in his orphan and found a wife for him.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the younger son died, Wang took in his orphaned child and arranged a marriage for him.

sentences.zh: 盧廷華妻沈，永定人。

translations.literal: Shen, wife of Lu Tinghua, was a native of Yongding.
translations.idiomatic: Shen, the wife of Lu Tinghua, came from Yongding.

sentences.zh: 廷華好狹邪遊，擯沈異居。

translations.literal: Tinghua was fond of dissolute pleasures and drove Shen to live separately.
translations.idiomatic: Tinghua loved the brothels and cast Shen out to live apart from him.

sentences.zh: 姑溺愛，亦惡沈。

translations.literal: His mother doted on him and also hated Shen.
translations.idiomatic: His mother indulged him and turned against Shen as well.

sentences.zh: 沈晨必謁姑，為理井臼。

translations.literal: Every morning Shen had to visit her mother-in-law and attend to the well and mortar.
translations.idiomatic: Every morning Shen had to call on her mother-in-law and do the grinding and chores.

sentences.zh: 或私具甘旨，姑不善也。

translations.literal: Sometimes she privately prepared delicacies, but her mother-in-law disliked them.
translations.idiomatic: When she brought special foods she had prepared, her mother-in-law rejected them.

sentences.zh: 施鞭撻，無懟。

translations.literal: She was whipped and lashed, yet offered no resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother-in-law beat her, yet she never talked back.

sentences.zh: 廷華得惡疾，沈乃歸侍。

translations.literal: Tinghua contracted a vicious illness; Shen then returned to nurse him.
translations.idiomatic: When Tinghua fell gravely ill, Shen came back to care for him.

sentences.zh: 廷華死，以節終。

translations.literal: Tinghua died, and she lived chaste to the end.
translations.idiomatic: After Tinghua died, she remained a faithful widow for the rest of her life.

sentences.zh: 李豁然妻楊，永年人。

translations.literal: Yang, wife of Li Huoran, was a native of Yongnian.
translations.idiomatic: Yang, the wife of Li Huoran, came from Yongnian.

sentences.zh: 康熙十五年，豁然卒，楊年二十一。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Kangxi Huoran died; Yang was twenty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of the Kangxi reign, Huoran died; Yang was twenty-one.

sentences.zh: 事舅姑孝。

translations.literal: She served her parents-in-law filially.
translations.idiomatic: She cared for her in-laws with devoted filial piety.

sentences.zh: 撫子尊賢，娶婦王，生子而尊賢卒，姑、婦共撫孤孫至成立。

translations.literal: She raised her son Zunxian; he took a wife Wang and had a son, then Zunxian died; the mother-in-law and daughter-in-law together raised the orphaned grandson to maturity.
translations.idiomatic: She raised her son Zunxian, who married a woman named Wang and had a child before dying young; Yang and her daughter-in-law then reared the orphaned grandson together until he came of age.

sentences.zh: 楊以乾隆四十二年卒，壽百二十，守節百有一年。

translations.literal: Yang died in the forty-second year of Qianlong, aged one hundred twenty, having kept her chastity for one hundred one years.
translations.idiomatic: Yang died in the forty-second year of the Qianlong reign at the age of one hundred twenty, having remained a chaste widow for one hundred and one years.

sentences.zh: 王前一年卒，年亦九十八。

translations.literal: Wang died the year before, also aged ninety-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Wang had died the year before, also at the age of ninety-eight.

sentences.zh: 曾經佑妻林，惠安人。

translations.literal: Lin, wife of Zeng Jingyou, was a native of Huian.
translations.idiomatic: Lin, the wife of Zeng Jingyou, came from Huian.

sentences.zh: 早寡。

translations.literal: Widowed early.
translations.idiomatic: She was widowed while still young.

sentences.zh: 所居濱海，為漁家補網，夜無燈，隨月升落為作輟。

translations.literal: She lived by the sea and mended nets for fishing families; at night there was no lamp, and she worked and rested according to the moon's rising and setting.
translations.idiomatic: She lived on the coast and mended fishermen's nets; without a lamp at night, she timed her work and rest to the moon's rise and fall.

sentences.zh: 積數十年，目因以盲，而手甚習，操作如故。

translations.literal: Accumulating over several decades, her eyes thereby went blind, but her hands were very skilled and she worked as before.
translations.idiomatic: After decades of this labor her eyes went blind, yet her hands remained so skilled that she worked as capably as ever.

sentences.zh: 舅姑資以老，復為夫立後。

translations.literal: She supported her parents-in-law into old age and also established an heir for her husband.
translations.idiomatic: She supported her in-laws into their old age and also arranged for an heir to continue her husband's line.

sentences.zh: 梁曇妻李，臨汾人。
