translations.literal: Li, wife of Liang Tan, was a native of Linfen.
translations.idiomatic: Li, the wife of Liang Tan, came from Linfen.

sentences.zh: 曇卒，時子生方兩月，貧，啖野菜以活。

translations.literal: Tan died when their son was just two months old; poor, they ate wild vegetables to survive.
translations.idiomatic: When Tan died their son was only two months old; destitute, mother and child lived on wild greens.

sentences.zh: 曇嘗蒔槐於庭，李日紡其下，護之甚謹。

translations.literal: Tan had once planted a locust tree in the courtyard; Li daily spun beneath it and guarded it very carefully.
translations.idiomatic: Tan had once planted a locust tree in the courtyard; Li spun beneath it every day and tended it with great care.

sentences.zh: 曰：「此吾夫手植，見之如見吾夫矣！」

translations.literal: She said, "My husband planted this with his own hands—when I look at it, it's as though I see him again!"
translations.idiomatic: She said, "My husband planted this with his own hands—when I look at it, it's as though I see him again!"

sentences.zh: 鄉人因稱「節婦槐」。

translations.literal: The villagers therefore called it the "Chaste Widow Locust."
translations.idiomatic: The villagers came to call it the "Chaste Widow Tree."

sentences.zh: 姜吉生妻木，東川人。

translations.literal: Mu, wife of Jiang Jisheng, was a native of Dongchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Mu, the wife of Jiang Jisheng, came from Dongchuan.

sentences.zh: 雍正八年，東川屬夷叛，從吉生逃山中。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yongzheng the Yi of Dongchuan rebelled; she fled into the mountains with Jisheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of the Yongzheng reign, when the tribal peoples of Dongchuan rose in rebellion, she fled into the mountains with Jisheng.

sentences.zh: 賊至，殺吉生及其子，木忍哭伏林間。

translations.literal: The bandits arrived, killed Jisheng and his son, and Mu wept and lay hidden in the forest.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits came they killed Jisheng and his son; Mu wept and hid herself in the woods.

sentences.zh: 師至，賊降，木躡賊至城西，手搏殺吉生賊以告官，請得手刃之。

translations.literal: The army arrived, the bandits surrendered; Mu tracked the bandits to the west of the city, seized with her hands the bandit who had killed Jisheng, reported to the authorities, and asked to be allowed to finish him off with her own hand.
translations.idiomatic: When government troops arrived and the bandits surrendered, Mu followed them to the west gate of the city, seized the man who had killed Jisheng, reported him to the officials, and asked permission to dispatch him with her own hand.

sentences.zh: 提督張耀愍而許焉，遂磔賊以祭吉生。

translations.literal: Governor-General Zhang Yao took pity and granted it; they then dismembered the bandit as a sacrifice to Jisheng.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Zhang Yao was moved and consented; the bandit was then torn apart as an offering to Jisheng.

sentences.zh: 曹某妻王，興縣人。

translations.literal: Wang, wife of a man surnamed Cao, was a native of Xing County.
translations.idiomatic: Wang, the wife of a man surnamed Cao, came from Xing County.

sentences.zh: 早寡，子喑，鄰婦亦早寡，相與約不嫁。

translations.literal: Widowed early, with a mute son; a neighboring woman was also widowed early, and together they pledged not to remarry.
translations.idiomatic: She was widowed young and had a mute son; a neighbor had also lost her husband early, and the two women pledged never to marry again.

sentences.zh: 居十五年，王詣其戚，或自外至，曰：「鄰婦嫁矣！」

translations.literal: After fifteen years Wang went to visit a kinsman; someone arriving from outside said, "Your neighbor has remarried!"
translations.idiomatic: After fifteen years Wang went to visit a kinsman; someone arriving from outside said, "Your neighbor has remarried!"

sentences.zh: 王曰：「信有之乎？」

translations.literal: Wang asked, "Can that really be true?"
translations.idiomatic: Wang asked, "Can that really be true?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「信，我所目見也！」

translations.literal: The visitor replied, "It is true—I saw it with my own eyes!"
translations.idiomatic: The visitor replied, "It is true—I saw it with my own eyes!"

sentences.zh: 王乃大慟，曰：「不意此婦，乃有此事！」

translations.literal: Wang was stricken with grief and said, "I never dreamed this woman would do such a thing!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang was stricken with grief and said, "I never dreamed this woman would do such a thing!"

sentences.zh: 遂絕。

translations.literal: She then broke off the relationship.
translations.idiomatic: She broke off all contact with her.

sentences.zh: 潘思週妻傅，名五芳，會稽人。

translations.literal: Fu, wife of Pan Sizhou, named Wufang, was a native of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Fu, the wife of Pan Sizhou—her given name was Wufang—came from Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 思週父為田州吏目，傅氏亦僑居廣西。

translations.literal: Sizhou's father was a clerk in Tianzhou; the Fu clan also sojourned in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhou's father served as a clerk in Tianzhou, and the Fu family had also taken up residence in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 嫁年餘，生一女，思週卒。

translations.literal: A little over a year after marriage she bore a daughter; Sizhou died.
translations.idiomatic: A little more than a year after she married, she gave birth to a daughter; then Sizhou died.

sentences.zh: 或欲聘焉，傅截發矢曰：「所不終於潘者，如此發！」

translations.literal: When suitors came forward, Fu cut off her hair and vowed, "Anything that does not end with the Pan family shall be like this hair!"
translations.idiomatic: When suitors came forward, Fu cut off her hair and vowed, "Anything that does not end with the Pan family shall be like this hair!"

sentences.zh: 未幾，母與兄死，兄公及娣又死，舅亦死，傅持六喪還。

translations.literal: Before long her mother and elder brother died, her elder brother's father-in-law and sister-in-law also died, and her uncle-in-law died as well; Fu conducted six funerals and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Not long afterward her mother and elder brother died, then her brother's father-in-law and sister-in-law, and then her husband's uncle; Fu presided over six funerals before returning home.

sentences.zh: 出郭門，身衰絰，徒步號泣以從。

translations.literal: Leaving the city gate, she wore mourning hemp and walked on foot, wailing as she followed.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the city gate she wore the coarse hemp of mourning and walked on foot, wailing as she followed the coffins.

sentences.zh: 僮民皆感嘆，稱孝婦。

translations.literal: The local people were all moved and called her a filial daughter-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: The local people were deeply moved and hailed her as a filial daughter-in-law.

sentences.zh: 歸營葬，撫叔及其女畢婚嫁。

translations.literal: After returning she arranged burials, raised her husband's uncle, and saw her daughter through marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Back home she arranged the burials, cared for her husband's uncle, and saw her daughter married.

sentences.zh: 倪存謨二妾方、硃，富順人。

translations.literal: Fang and Zhu, the two concubines of Ni Cunmo, were from Fushun.
translations.idiomatic: Fang and Zhu, the two concubines of Ni Cunmo, were natives of Fushun.

sentences.zh: 存謨為英山知縣，坐事戍伊犁，方、硃皆從。

translations.literal: Cunmo was magistrate of Yingshan; convicted of an offense he was banished to Yili; Fang and Zhu both followed.
translations.idiomatic: Cunmo served as magistrate of Yingshan; after he was convicted and exiled to Yili, both Fang and Zhu accompanied him.

sentences.zh: 存謨死，方、硃慟不食。

translations.literal: When Cunmo died, Fang and Zhu grieved and refused to eat.
translations.idiomatic: When Cunmo died, Fang and Zhu mourned so bitterly that they stopped eating.

sentences.zh: 伊犁將軍為徵賻，俾持喪歸。

translations.literal: The Yili general collected burial funds and had them bring the coffin home.
translations.idiomatic: The general at Yili raised funeral expenses and sent them home with the coffin.

sentences.zh: 至富順，嫡子出郭迎，方、硃相謂曰：「我二人不死者，懼主人骨不歸。

translations.literal: At Fushun the legitimate son came out to meet them at the city gate; Fang and Zhu said to each other, "The reason we two did not die was that we feared our master's bones would not return home.
translations.idiomatic: At Fushun the legitimate son came out to greet them at the city gate; Fang and Zhu said to each other, "The only reason we stayed alive was our fear that our master's bones would never come home.

sentences.zh: 今歸矣，請死。」

translations.literal: Now that we are home, we ask to die."
translations.idiomatic: Now that we are home, we ask to die."

sentences.zh: 相攜躍入江，救不死，嫡子及孫死，撫曾孫二成立。

translations.literal: They took each other's hands and leaped into the river; they were rescued and did not die. The legitimate son and grandson had died; they raised two great-grandsons to maturity.
translations.idiomatic: Hand in hand they threw themselves into the river, but were pulled out alive. The legitimate son and grandson had already died; the two women then raised two great-grandsons to adulthood.

sentences.zh: 楊震甲妻楊，楊三德妻馬，張壺裝妻牛，皆秦州人。

translations.literal: Yang Zhenjia's wife Yang, Yang Sande's wife Ma, and Zhang Huzhuang's wife Niu were all from Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang, wife of Yang Zhenjia; Ma, wife of Yang Sande; and Niu, wife of Zhang Huzhuang—all three were from Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 夫皆出客遊，久不歸。

translations.literal: Their husbands all went away as traveling guests and did not return for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: All three husbands had gone away on long journeys and did not return for many years.

sentences.zh: 皆善事孀姑。

translations.literal: All dutifully served their widowed mothers-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Each dutifully cared for her widowed mother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 馬姑尤嚴，日被箠楚，奉之愈謹。

translations.literal: Ma's mother-in-law was especially strict; she was beaten with whips daily yet served her all the more carefully.
translations.idiomatic: Ma's mother-in-law was especially harsh; Ma was whipped nearly every day, yet she served her all the more devotedly.

sentences.zh: 楊撫子女成立。

translations.literal: Yang raised the children to maturity.
translations.idiomatic: Yang raised her children to adulthood.

sentences.zh: 馬、牛皆無子，立後。

translations.literal: Ma and Niu both had no sons and established heirs.
translations.idiomatic: Ma and Niu had no sons of their own and each arranged for an heir.

sentences.zh: 州人為之語曰：「馬牛羊，立人綱。

translations.literal: The people of the prefecture made a rhyme about them: "Horse, ox, and sheep uphold human bonds.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the prefecture made up a rhyme about them: "Horse, ox, and sheep uphold the bonds of humanity.

sentences.zh: 夫遠客，姑在堂。

translations.literal: Husbands far away as guests, mothers-in-law in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Husbands far from home, mothers-in-law still in the hall.

sentences.zh: 胸中冰，頭上霜。」

translations.literal: Ice in the heart, frost upon the brow."
translations.idiomatic: Ice in the heart, frost upon the brow."

sentences.zh: 蓋借「羊」目楊也。

translations.literal: This used the word "sheep" to refer to Yang by homophone.
translations.idiomatic: The rhyme used the word for "sheep" as a homophone for the Yang surname.

sentences.zh: 陳大成妻林，連江人。

translations.literal: Lin, wife of Chen Dacheng, was from Lianjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Lin, the wife of Chen Dacheng, came from Lianjiang.

sentences.zh: 大成坐事戍黑龍江。

translations.literal: Dacheng was convicted and banished to Heilongjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Dacheng was convicted of an offense and exiled to Heilongjiang.

sentences.zh: 將行，遣林別嫁，林不可，從大成戍所。

translations.literal: About to depart, he sent Lin away to remarry; Lin refused and followed Dacheng to the place of exile.
translations.idiomatic: Before he left he urged Lin to remarry, but she refused and followed him to his place of exile.

sentences.zh: 居二十八年，大成死，林裹其骨，襁兒女，乞食跣行萬餘裡，還故鄉。

translations.literal: After twenty-eight years Dacheng died; Lin wrapped his bones, carrying her infant son and daughter, begged for food and went barefoot more than ten thousand li, returning to her homeland.
translations.idiomatic: After twenty-eight years Dacheng died; Lin wrapped his bones, took her infant son and daughter in her arms, and walked barefoot more than ten thousand li, begging for food all the way home.

sentences.zh: 灌園自給，葬大成祖墓側。

translations.literal: She irrigated gardens to support herself and buried Dacheng beside his ancestral tomb.
translations.idiomatic: She tended gardens to support herself and buried Dacheng beside his family's ancestral graves.

sentences.zh: 溫得珠妻李，永清人。

translations.literal: Li, wife of Wen Dezhu, was from Yongqing.
translations.idiomatic: Li, the wife of Wen Dezhu, came from Yongqing.

sentences.zh: 得珠早喪母，父娶後妻，生二子，遂惡得珠，並憎李。

translations.literal: Dezhu lost his mother early; his father took a second wife and had two sons, then came to despise Dezhu and hate Li as well.
translations.idiomatic: Dezhu lost his mother while still young; his father remarried and had two more sons, then turned against Dezhu and came to despise Li as well.

sentences.zh: 得珠病狂易，一日逃其叔杖，投井死。

translations.literal: Dezhu developed mental illness; one day he fled his uncle's beating and threw himself into a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: Dezhu fell into madness; one day he fled his uncle's beating, threw himself into a well, and died.

sentences.zh: 父母聞，不哭，李力請，乃得斂。

translations.literal: When his parents heard, they did not weep; only after Li strongly pleaded were they allowed to bury him.
translations.idiomatic: When his parents heard the news they did not weep; only after Li pleaded insistently were they persuaded to give him a proper burial.

sentences.zh: 遺腹生子經元，舅姑迫李嫁，謂李嫁，則田廬皆二少子產也，因虐之百端。

translations.literal: She bore posthumously a son Jingyuan; her parents-in-law forced Li to remarry, saying that if Li remarried, the fields and house would all become property of the two younger sons, and so they abused her in every way.
translations.idiomatic: She bore a posthumous son, Jingyuan; her in-laws pressed her to remarry, declaring that if she did the fields and house would pass to their two younger sons, and they tormented her in every conceivable way.

sentences.zh: 李度終不可留，抱經元辭舅姑還母家，賃地以耕，勞苦自食力。

translations.literal: Li judged she could not stay, took Jingyuan and bade farewell to her parents-in-law and returned to her mother's home, rented land to farm, and supported herself by hard labor.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing she could not remain, Li took Jingyuan, bade farewell to her in-laws, and returned to her mother's home, where she rented land to farm and supported herself by hard work.

sentences.zh: 經元娶婦生孫，而舅及二少子皆死，遺田亦殆盡，姑衰病無所依。

translations.literal: Jingyuan married and had a grandson; then her father-in-law and the two younger sons all died, the inherited fields were nearly exhausted, and her mother-in-law was old, ill, and had nowhere to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyuan married and had a son of his own; then his grandfather and the two younger uncles died, the family lands were nearly gone, and his grandmother, old and sick, had no one to depend on.

sentences.zh: 李乃率子婦還，起居床下。

translations.literal: Li then led her son and daughter-in-law back and attended to her day and night at bedside.
translations.idiomatic: Li then brought her son and daughter-in-law back and waited on her mother-in-law day and night at her bedside.

sentences.zh: 姑執手流涕，道其悔也；

translations.literal: Her mother-in-law took her hand with tears streaming and spoke of her regret;
translations.idiomatic: Her mother-in-law took her hand, weeping, and spoke of her remorse;

sentences.zh: 而得珠叔故助虐者，亦前死，其嫠仰食於經元。

translations.literal: Dezhu's uncle, who had formerly aided in the abuse, had also died earlier; his widow depended on Jingyuan for food.
translations.idiomatic: Dezhu's uncle, who had once joined in the abuse, had also died; his widow now depended on Jingyuan for her livelihood.

sentences.zh: 經元有四子，皆力田，能孝養。

translations.literal: Jingyuan had four sons, all worked the fields and were able to filially support them.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyuan had four sons, all hardworking farmers who dutifully supported their elders.

sentences.zh: 賈國林妻韓，國林，扶溝人；

translations.literal: Han, wife of Jia Guolin; Guolin was from Fugou;
translations.idiomatic: Han was the wife of Jia Guolin, who came from Fugou;

sentences.zh: 韓，淮寧人。

translations.literal: Han was from Huaining.
translations.idiomatic: Han herself was from Huaining.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五十一年，大饑，民為盜。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year of Qianlong there was a great famine and the people turned to banditry.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-first year of the Qianlong reign a great famine drove people to robbery.

sentences.zh: 國林有族子二，行無賴，執國林及韓，綁於庭之槐，而盡取其室所有，已乃斫綁釋之。

translations.literal: Guolin had two clansmen who were thuggish; they seized Guolin and Han, bound them to the courtyard locust tree, and took everything in the house; only then did they chop the bonds and release them.
translations.idiomatic: Guolin had two clansmen, both ruffians, who seized him and Han, tied them to the locust tree in the courtyard, stripped the house of everything they owned, and only then cut their bonds and let them go.

sentences.zh: 國林將指傷，越三日死。

translations.literal: Guolin's finger was injured; after three days he died.
translations.idiomatic: Guolin's finger was wounded; three days later he died.

sentences.zh: 韓欲告官，無人焉為之佐。

translations.literal: Han wished to report to the authorities but had no one to assist her.
translations.idiomatic: Han wanted to bring charges but had no one to help her.

sentences.zh: 有子二，皆幼。

translations.literal: She had two sons, both young.
translations.idiomatic: She had two young sons.

sentences.zh: 其弟日負薪米贍姊，夜執梃伺門戶。

translations.literal: Her younger brother daily carried firewood and rice to support his sister; at night he held a club and guarded the door.
translations.idiomatic: Her younger brother brought firewood and rice every day to support her, and at night stood guard at the door with a club.

sentences.zh: 居數年，無賴又至，徹其屋茅，擲大磚中韓手，遂奪田伐樹，一不與較。

translations.literal: After several years the ruffians came again, stripped the thatch from her roof, threw a large brick that struck Han's hand, then seized fields and cut trees—she did not contend with them at all.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later the ruffians returned, tore the thatch from her roof, threw a large brick that struck Han's hand, then seized her fields and cut down her trees—she never resisted them.

sentences.zh: 二人者死，乃稍稍得安。

translations.literal: When the two men died, she gradually obtained peace.
translations.idiomatic: When the two men died she was at last able to live in some peace.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶二十三年，又大饑，無賴有子鬻其嫂，夜出走，韓為召其夫婦之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Jiaqing there was again a great famine; a ruffian's son sold his sister-in-law and fled by night; Han summoned the husband and wife back.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year of the Jiaqing reign famine struck again; a ruffian's son sold his sister-in-law and fled by night, but Han brought the couple back together.

sentences.zh: 因泣告其子曰：「害爾父者，某也。

translations.literal: She wept and told his son, "The one who harmed your father was such-and-such a person.
translations.idiomatic: Weeping, she told the man's son, "The one who killed your father was so-and-so.

sentences.zh: 今其子又鬻嫂，不仁哉此父子也！

translations.literal: Now his son has sold his sister-in-law—how unkind are this father and son!
translations.idiomatic: Now his son has sold his own sister-in-law—what cruel men, father and son!

sentences.zh: 顧為賈氏婦，即餓死，豈可失清白，汝曹當死守之！」

translations.literal: Remember—you are women of the Jia clan; even if you starve, you must not lose your honor; you must defend it with your lives!"
translations.idiomatic: Remember—you are women of the Jia clan; even if you starve, you must not lose your honor; you must defend it with your lives!"

sentences.zh: 此婦竟得免。

translations.literal: This woman was indeed spared.
translations.idiomatic: That woman was spared after all.

sentences.zh: 孫雲妻白，興縣人。

translations.literal: Bai, wife of Sun Yun, was from Xing County.
translations.idiomatic: Bai, the wife of Sun Yun, came from Xing County.

sentences.zh: 生十四年而嫁，嫁十三年而雲卒。

translations.literal: At fourteen she married; after thirteen years of marriage Yun died.
translations.idiomatic: She married at fourteen; thirteen years later Yun died.

sentences.zh: 又二十年，子長娶婦，白挈以拜雲墓，指而言曰：「此君子也，此君婦也，吾事畢，可以從君矣！」

translations.literal: Twenty years later, when their son had grown and taken a wife, Bai brought the daughter-in-law to bow at Yun's tomb and said, pointing, "This is the gentleman; this is his wife; my duty is done—I may follow my husband now!"
translations.idiomatic: Twenty years later, when their son had grown and taken a wife, Bai brought the daughter-in-law to bow at Yun's tomb and said, pointing, "This is the gentleman; this is his wife; my duty is done—I may follow my husband now!"

sentences.zh: 慟而僕，遂絕。

translations.literal: Grieving she collapsed and then stopped eating, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Overcome with grief she collapsed, stopped eating, and died.

sentences.zh: 圖斡恰納妻王依氏，滿洲人，乍浦駐防。

translations.literal: Wang Yishi, wife of Tuwohqiana, was a Manchu stationed at the Zhapu garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yishi, wife of Tuwohqiana, was a Manchu woman of the garrison at Zhapu.

sentences.zh: 圖斡恰納，瓜爾佳氏，早喪母，尋亦卒，無子，嗣絕矣。

translations.literal: Tuwohqiana, of the Guwalgiya clan, lost his mother early and soon also died without a son—the line was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Tuwohqiana of the Guwalgiya clan lost his mother while young and soon died himself, leaving no son—the line was broken.

sentences.zh: 父查郎阿謀為立後，王依氏曰：「子他人子，終非骨肉，不足奉大宗，原翁娶繼室。」

translations.literal: His father Qialang'a planned to adopt an heir; Wang Yishi said, "Another man's son can never truly be one's own flesh and blood and is not fit to carry on the main line—I beg you, Father, to take a second wife."
translations.idiomatic: His father Qialang'a planned to adopt an heir; Wang Yishi said, "Another man's son can never truly be one's own flesh and blood and is not fit to carry on the main line—I beg you, Father, to take a second wife."

sentences.zh: 查郎阿感其意，娶於邵，生子觀成。

translations.literal: Qialang'a was moved by her intent and married a woman from the Shao clan, who bore a son Guancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by her words, Qialang'a married a woman of the Shao clan, who bore a son named Guancheng.

sentences.zh: 觀成生七月，而查郎阿卒，王依氏哀姑少寡，奉養甚謹，躬操作助姑撫孤。

translations.literal: When Guancheng was seven months old Qialang'a died; Wang Yishi grieved for her young widowed mother-in-law, served her very carefully, and personally worked to help her mother-in-law raise the orphan.
translations.idiomatic: When Guancheng was seven months old Qialang'a died; Wang Yishi pitied her young widowed mother-in-law, served her devotedly, and worked with her own hands to help raise the orphan.

sentences.zh: 既遘疾，猶不自逸，事輒代其姑。

translations.literal: Even when she fell ill she still did not indulge herself; she always performed tasks in place of her mother-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Even when she fell ill she would not rest, always taking over her mother-in-law's chores herself.

sentences.zh: 卒時觀成已舉鄉試，以子鳳瑞為兄嗣，未百年而子孫繁衍至百餘人。

translations.literal: When she died Guancheng had already passed the provincial examinations; she made her son Fengrui heir to her elder brother-in-law's line; within a century descendants flourished to more than a hundred people.
translations.idiomatic: By the time she died Guancheng had passed the provincial examinations; she had made her son Fengrui heir to her brother-in-law's line, and within a century their descendants numbered more than a hundred.

sentences.zh: 吳先榜妻鄭，陝西山陽人。

translations.literal: Zheng, wife of Wu Xianbang, was from Shanyang in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng, the wife of Wu Xianbang, came from Shanyang in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 先榜卒，鄭誓殉。

translations.literal: When Xianbang died, Zheng swore to die with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianbang died, Zheng vowed to follow him in death.

sentences.zh: 家人慰喻之，曰：「兩兄公皆無子，若方有身，男也，吳氏幸有後。」

translations.literal: Her family comforted her, saying, "Both elder uncles are without sons; if you are pregnant and the child is a boy, the Wu line will be saved."
translations.idiomatic: Her family comforted her, saying, "Both elder uncles are without sons; if you are pregnant and the child is a boy, the Wu line will be saved."

sentences.zh: 逾數月生男，撫以成立，吳氏得有後。

translations.literal: After several months she bore a boy, raised him to maturity, and the Wu line obtained an heir.
translations.idiomatic: A few months later she gave birth to a son, raised him to adulthood, and the Wu clan had an heir.

sentences.zh: 王元龍妻李，嘉興人。

translations.literal: Li, wife of Wang Yuanlong, was from Jiaxing.
translations.idiomatic: Li, the wife of Wang Yuanlong, came from Jiaxing.

sentences.zh: 元龍悍，嗜酒，稍拂意，輒呵斥。

translations.literal: Yuanlong was fierce and fond of wine; if slightly displeased he would scold and shout.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanlong was violent and addicted to drink; the slightest provocation would set him shouting abuse.

sentences.zh: 既，傷於酒而病，李斥嫁時所媵田供藥餌。

translations.literal: Later, injured by drink and falling ill, Li sold the dowry fields from her marriage to supply medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Later he fell ill from drink; Li sold the fields she had brought as dowry to pay for his medicine.

sentences.zh: 元龍病，益悍，稍間，則日夜博。

translations.literal: When Yuanlong was ill he grew fiercer; in any interval of relief he gambled day and night.
translations.idiomatic: As his illness wore on Yuanlong grew even more violent; whenever he felt a little better he gambled day and night.

sentences.zh: 怒李，故以非禮虐使，或加以鞭楚，李安之，無幾微忤也。

translations.literal: Angry at Li, he deliberately abused her with improper demands, sometimes adding whippings; Li accepted it without the slightest sign of disobedience.
translations.idiomatic: Angry at Li, he deliberately mistreated her and sometimes whipped her; Li endured it all without the slightest complaint.

sentences.zh: 元龍病三年而死，李朝夕上食，輒號慟。

translations.literal: Yuanlong was ill three years and died; Li morning and evening offered food at his grave and always wailed in grief.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanlong was ill for three years and died; Li visited his grave morning and evening with offerings, wailing each time.

sentences.zh: 服除，會兄公之官福建，姑老不能赴，李往奉姑，七年而姑卒。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, her elder brother-in-law took an official post in Fujian; the mother-in-law was old and could not go; Li went to serve her, and after seven years the mother-in-law died.
translations.idiomatic: When her mourning period ended, her brother-in-law took a post in Fujian; the mother-in-law was too old to travel, so Li went in her stead and served her for seven years until she died.

sentences.zh: 李泣謂諸從子曰：「我當從汝叔於地下矣！」

translations.literal: Li wept and told her nephews, "It is time for me to join your uncle in the grave!"
translations.idiomatic: Li wept and told her nephews, "It is time for me to join your uncle in the grave!"

sentences.zh: 會火發，李整衣坐樓上，有梯而援者，李戒毋上樓，燼死焉。

translations.literal: A fire broke out; Li dressed neatly and sat upstairs; there was a ladder and people who came to rescue her, but Li warned them not to come upstairs, and she burned to death.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward a fire broke out; Li dressed herself neatly and sat upstairs; rescuers came with a ladder, but she warned them not to come up, and she perished in the flames.

sentences.zh: 蔡庚妻吳，合肥人。

translations.literal: Wu, wife of Cai Geng, was from Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: Wu, the wife of Cai Geng, came from Hefei.

sentences.zh: 早寡，立從子為後，以事姑。

translations.literal: Widowed early, she established a younger clansman's son as heir in order to serve her mother-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Widowed young, she adopted a younger clansman's son as heir so she could continue caring for her mother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 嘗為辭自序曰：「父母生我時，惟原得其所。

translations.literal: She once composed a poem self-narrative: "When my parents bore me, they only wished I might find my proper place.
translations.idiomatic: She once composed a verse about her own life: "When my parents gave me life, they only prayed I might find my proper place.

sentences.zh: 十六歸君子，同心祀先祖。

translations.literal: At sixteen I married a gentleman; with one heart we sacrificed to our ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen I married a good man; together we honored our ancestors.

sentences.zh: 歸時舅已歿，姑老誰為主？

translations.literal: When I married, my father-in-law had already died—who would be mistress for my old mother-in-law?
translations.idiomatic: When I came to this house my father-in-law was already gone—who would care for my aged mother-in-law?

sentences.zh: 嗟嗟夫質弱，終朝抱疾處。

translations.literal: Alas, my nature is weak; all day I lie sick in my chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Alas, my frail body kept me sick in bed all day long.

sentences.zh: 十八幸生男，朝夕姑欣睹。

translations.literal: At eighteen I fortunately bore a son; morning and evening my mother-in-law rejoiced to see him.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen I was blessed with a son; my mother-in-law delighted in him every day.

sentences.zh: 無端因痘殤，姑泣淚如雨。

translations.literal: Without cause he died of smallpox; my mother-in-law wept tears like rain.
translations.idiomatic: Then he died suddenly of smallpox, and my mother-in-law wept as though the sky itself were falling.

sentences.zh: 堂上節姑哀，入幔痛肝腑。

translations.literal: In the hall the chaste mother-in-law grieved; entering the curtain I felt pain to my inmost organs.
translations.idiomatic: In the hall my chaste mother-in-law mourned; behind the curtain my heart was torn apart.

sentences.zh: 二十再生男，視若擎天柱。

translations.literal: At twenty I again bore a son, regarding him as the pillar that holds up the sky.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty I bore another son and looked on him as the pillar holding up heaven itself.

sentences.zh: 兒生甫一載，忽然夫命殂。

translations.literal: The son had lived barely one year when suddenly her husband's life ended.
translations.idiomatic: Her son was barely a year old when her husband suddenly died.

sentences.zh: 始婦並時啼，眷屬群相撫。

translations.literal: At first the daughter-in-law and mother-in-law wept together; relatives gathered to comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: At first she and her mother-in-law wept together while kinsmen gathered to comfort them.

sentences.zh: 死者不復生，弱息堪承父。

translations.literal: The dead do not return to life; the weak child can carry on for the father.
translations.idiomatic: The dead cannot be restored, but the infant son could still carry on his father's line.

sentences.zh: 那知天奪兒，骨肉又歸土。

translations.literal: Who knew Heaven would take the son—flesh and bone returned again to earth.
translations.idiomatic: But Heaven took the child too, and her flesh and blood returned to the earth.

sentences.zh: 姑祗有哭時，我豈無死所！

translations.literal: My mother-in-law has only times to weep—have I no place to die!
translations.idiomatic: My mother-in-law had only her tears—did I not have a place to die as well?

sentences.zh: 還念朽姑存，我死誰為哺？

translations.literal: Yet thinking of my aged mother-in-law still living—if I die, who will feed her?
translations.idiomatic: Yet I thought of my frail mother-in-law still alive—if I died, who would care for her?

sentences.zh: 隱痛斂深閨，衰顏原長護。

translations.literal: She hid her pain within the inner chambers and with a worn face continued long to protect her.
translations.idiomatic: She hid her grief in the inner rooms and with a weary face went on caring for her.

sentences.zh: 奇災偏遇火，焦爛姑肌膚。

translations.literal: A strange calamity chanced to be fire; her mother-in-law's flesh was scorched and ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Then a terrible fire struck, scorching her mother-in-law's flesh.

sentences.zh: 和血以丸藥，年餘乃如故。

translations.literal: She mixed blood into pills of medicine; after more than a year she was as before.
translations.idiomatic: She mixed her own blood into medicinal pills; after more than a year her mother-in-law recovered.

sentences.zh: 災退宜多壽，云何复病殂！

translations.literal: When calamity receded she ought to live long—why again did illness take her life!
translations.idiomatic: After the disaster she should have lived long—why did illness take her again!

sentences.zh: 送姑歸黃泉，夫缺我今補。

translations.literal: Sending my mother-in-law back to the Yellow Springs—my husband's place I now fill.
translations.idiomatic: I sent my mother-in-law to the grave; now I would fill the place my husband left empty.

sentences.zh: 我今補夫缺，一死何所顧？

translations.literal: I now fill my husband's place—what is there to consider in one death?
translations.idiomatic: Having fulfilled my husband's duty, what did I have left to live for?

sentences.zh: 哀哀我父母，惸惸將泣訴！」

translations.literal: Alas, my poor parents—bereft and alone, they will weep in grief!"
translations.idiomatic: Alas, my poor parents—bereft and alone, they will weep in grief!"

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十有八。

translations.literal: She died at the age of eighty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: She died at the age of eighty-eight.

sentences.zh: 韓某妻馬，萊蕪人。

translations.literal: Ma, wife of a man surnamed Han, was from Laigwu.
translations.idiomatic: Ma, the wife of a man surnamed Han, came from Laigwu.

sentences.zh: 貧，夫商於遼陽，馬出為傭。

translations.literal: Poor, her husband traded in Liaoyang; Ma went out to work as a hired laborer.
translations.idiomatic: They were poor; her husband went to trade in Liaoyang while Ma hired herself out as a laborer.

sentences.zh: 聞夫死，其父欲嫁之，馬曰：「歸夫骨其可。」

translations.literal: When she heard her husband had died, her father wanted to remarry her; Ma said, "At least let me bring back my husband's bones."
translations.idiomatic: When she heard her husband had died, her father wanted to remarry her; Ma said, "At least let me bring back my husband's bones."

sentences.zh: 乃乞食行五千里，得夫骨，負以歸。

translations.literal: She then begged for food and traveled five thousand li, obtained her husband's bones, and carried them back.
translations.idiomatic: She begged for food along the way and walked five thousand li, found her husband's remains, and carried them home on her back.

sentences.zh: 日行一二十里，夜或露宿，犯風雪，行歲餘，乃至家。

translations.literal: Daily she traveled ten or twenty li; at night she sometimes slept in the open, braving wind and snow; after traveling more than a year she reached home.
translations.idiomatic: She walked ten or twenty li a day, sometimes sleeping in the open at night through wind and snow; after more than a year she reached home.

sentences.zh: 既葬，其父終欲嫁之，馬執白刃自誓，乃已。

translations.literal: After the burial her father still wished to marry her off; Ma grasped a bare blade and swore an oath, and only then did he stop.
translations.idiomatic: After the burial her father still pressed her to remarry; Ma seized a bare blade and swore she would die rather than comply, and he gave up.

sentences.zh: 李鳴鑾妻黃，騰越人。

translations.literal: Huang, wife of Li Mingluan, was from Tengyue.
translations.idiomatic: Huang, the wife of Li Mingluan, came from Tengyue.

sentences.zh: 咸豐間，雲南迴亂，鳴鑾以千總戰，負傷卒。

translations.literal: During the Xianfeng era the Hui of Yunnan rebelled; Mingluan fought as a battalion commander, was wounded, and died.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianfeng reign the Hui rebellion broke out in Yunnan; Mingluan fought as a battalion commander, was wounded in battle, and died.

sentences.zh: 黃截發，撫二子。

translations.literal: Huang cut off her hair and raised two sons.
translations.idiomatic: Huang cut off her hair in mourning and raised their two sons.

sentences.zh: 同治初，寇至，轉徙為人縫紉浣濯，日率一粥，仍督子讀不輟。

translations.literal: In the early Tongzhi era bandits arrived; she moved about sewing and washing for others, daily eating only one bowl of gruel, yet still supervised her sons' reading without pause.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Tongzhi years, when bandits came, she moved from place to place sewing and washing for others, living on a single bowl of gruel a day while still making her sons study without fail.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「人不讀書，與禽獸何異？」

translations.literal: She once said, "If a person does not read books, how is he different from birds and beasts?"
translations.idiomatic: She often said, "A person who does not read—how is he any different from a beast?"

sentences.zh: 金光炳妻倪，金華人。

translations.literal: Ni, wife of Jin Guangbing, was from Jinhua.
translations.idiomatic: Ni, the wife of Jin Guangbing, came from Jinhua.

sentences.zh: 光炳卒，倪殉，救免。

translations.literal: When Guangbing died, Ni sought to die with him but was rescued and spared.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangbing died, Ni tried to follow him in death but was saved.

sentences.zh: 洪秀全兵至，攜二子竄山谷。

translations.literal: When Hong Xiuquan's troops arrived, she took her two sons and fled into the mountain valleys.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong Xiuquan's army came, she fled into the mountains with her two sons.

sentences.zh: 亂定，力作自給。

translations.literal: When the turmoil settled, she worked hard labor to support herself.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebellion ended she supported herself by hard labor.

sentences.zh: 貧甚，督子讀，不少假。

translations.literal: Extremely poor, she supervised her sons' reading and granted no leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Though desperately poor, she kept her sons at their books and never relaxed her demands.

sentences.zh: 徐嘉賢妻劉，嘉賢，天津人；

translations.literal: Liu, wife of Xu Jiaxian; Jiaxian was from Tianjin;
translations.idiomatic: Liu was the wife of Xu Jiaxian, who came from Tianjin;

sentences.zh: 劉，桐城人。

translations.literal: Liu was from Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu herself was from Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 嘉賢少從軍河南，嘗單騎入賊壘，拔陷賊婦女數百人出。

translations.literal: Jiaxian in youth followed the army in Henan; once riding alone he entered the bandit camp and rescued several hundred women trapped by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaxian had served in the army in Henan as a young man; once he rode alone into a bandit camp and rescued several hundred captive women.

sentences.zh: 旋卒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 劉貧，輒數日不舉火，嚴督其子讀。

translations.literal: Liu was poor and often went several days without lighting a fire; she strictly supervised her son's reading.
translations.idiomatic: Liu was so poor she often went days without cooking, yet she still kept her son at his books.

sentences.zh: 族有為令者招使往，劉曰：「今不自立，而託於人，懼吾子之不振也！」

translations.literal: When a clansman who had become a magistrate invited her to come live with him, Liu said, "If I cannot stand on my own feet now but depend on others, I fear my son will never make anything of himself!"
translations.idiomatic: When a clansman who had become a magistrate invited her to come live with him, Liu said, "If I cannot stand on my own feet now but depend on others, I fear my son will never make anything of himself!"

sentences.zh: 謝不往。

translations.literal: She declined and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: She declined and stayed away.

sentences.zh: 冒樹楷妻週，樹楷，如皋人；

translations.literal: Zhou, wife of Mao Shukai; Shukai was from Rugao;
translations.idiomatic: Zhou was the wife of Mao Shukai, who came from Rugao;

sentences.zh: 週，祥符人。

translations.literal: Zhou was from Xiangfu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou herself was from Xiangfu.

sentences.zh: 樹楷以知縣待缺福建，早卒。

translations.literal: Shukai was a magistrate awaiting appointment in Fujian and died early.
translations.idiomatic: Shukai had been a magistrate awaiting appointment in Fujian when he died young.

sentences.zh: 週挈子女從舅廣州，舅亦卒。

translations.literal: Zhou took her children and followed her uncle-in-law to Guangzhou; the uncle also died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou took her children and followed her husband's uncle to Guangzhou, where the uncle also died.

sentences.zh: 僑居，日食率百錢，翼子女以長。

translations.literal: Living as sojourners, daily food cost about a hundred cash; she nurtured her children to grow up.
translations.idiomatic: Living as exiles, she spent about a hundred cash a day on food and raised her children to adulthood.

sentences.zh: 子得官，將請旌，週拒之曰：「婦節常耳，人子於其母，奈何欲假以為名哉？」

translations.literal: When her son gained an official post and wanted to petition for an imperial commendation, Zhou refused, saying, "A woman's chastity is nothing extraordinary—how could a son use his mother's virtue to make a name for himself?"
translations.idiomatic: When her son gained an official post and wanted to petition for an imperial commendation, Zhou refused, saying, "A woman's chastity is nothing extraordinary—how could a son use his mother's virtue to make a name for himself?"

sentences.zh: 父星詒，諸父星譼、星虓，並有文行，週刻其遺著，為父營葬，置墓田焉。

translations.literal: Her father Xingyi, uncles Xingxi and Xingxiao, all had literary accomplishments; Zhou engraved their posthumous writings, arranged burial for her father, and set aside grave fields.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Xingyi and her uncles Xingxi and Xingxiao had all been men of letters; Zhou published their posthumous writings, arranged her father's burial, and set aside land for the family graves.

sentences.zh: 曾廣垕妻劉，衡陽人。

translations.literal: Liu, wife of Zeng Guanghou, was from Hengyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu, the wife of Zeng Guanghou, came from Hengyang.

sentences.zh: 歸廣垕，舅老，姑前卒。

translations.literal: After marrying Guanghou, her father-in-law was old and her mother-in-law had died earlier.
translations.idiomatic: When she married Guanghou, her father-in-law was elderly and her mother-in-law had already died.

sentences.zh: 兄公初喪，舅痛子，幾失明，出入需人。

translations.literal: When her elder brother-in-law first died, her father-in-law grieved for his son and nearly went blind, needing someone for going in and out.
translations.idiomatic: When her brother-in-law died, her father-in-law grieved so deeply for his son that he nearly lost his sight and needed help whenever he went out.

sentences.zh: 劉侍舅謹，日執炊，一飯三起視舅起居衣食。

translations.literal: Liu attended her father-in-law carefully; daily she cooked, rising three times during one meal to check his comings and goings, clothing and food.
translations.idiomatic: Liu waited on her father-in-law devotedly, cooking for him every day and rising three times during a single meal to attend to his needs.

sentences.zh: 雖貧，必具酒肉。

translations.literal: Though poor, she always provided wine and meat.
translations.idiomatic: Though they were poor, she always saw that he had wine and meat.

sentences.zh: 舅病，奉侍七晝夜不就枕。

translations.literal: When her father-in-law fell ill, she attended him for seven days and nights without lying down on a pillow.
translations.idiomatic: When her father-in-law fell ill, she nursed him for seven days and nights without resting her head on a pillow.

sentences.zh: 舅卒，棄田廬治喪。

translations.literal: When her father-in-law died, she abandoned fields and house to conduct the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: When her father-in-law died, she sold their fields and house to pay for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 劉方產，徙陋巷，艱苦冰雪中。

translations.literal: Liu had just given birth and moved to a humble lane, enduring hardship in ice and snow.
translations.idiomatic: Liu had just given birth when they moved to a poor alley and endured bitter hardship through the winter snows.

sentences.zh: 廣垕又卒，乃與姒李同居，以子為之後。

translations.literal: Guanghou also died; she then lived together with her sister-in-law Li and made her son heir to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Guanghou also died, she lived with her sister-in-law Li and made her son the heir to his line.

sentences.zh: 李亦苦節，劉事之如姑。

translations.literal: Li also endured hardship in chastity; Liu served her as a mother-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Li was also a woman of steadfast virtue; Liu treated her as she would a mother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 晝治針黹，夜則紡績，節衣食，命子熙就學，卒成進士。

translations.literal: By day she did needlework, by night she spun; she economized on clothing and food, ordered her son Xi to pursue learning, and he ultimately became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: She sewed by day and spun by night, lived frugally, and sent her son Xi to school; he eventually passed the jinshi examinations.

sentences.zh: 方極困，老稚或乞食，必分食與之。

translations.literal: When most destitute, if old or young came begging for food, she always shared food with them.
translations.idiomatic: Even in their worst poverty, whenever old or young beggars came, she always shared what food she had.

sentences.zh: 晚少豐，年飢，必出穀以賑貧者。

translations.literal: In later years she was somewhat better off; in years of famine she always brought out grain to relieve the poor.
translations.idiomatic: In later life she was somewhat better off, and in famine years she always gave grain to the poor.

sentences.zh: 馮丙煐妻俞，丙煐，大興人；

translations.literal: Yu, wife of Feng Bingying; Bingying was from Daxing;
translations.idiomatic: Yu was the wife of Feng Bingying, who came from Daxing;

sentences.zh: 俞，婺源人。

translations.literal: Yu was from Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu herself was from Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 丙煐為世父後，俞事兩姑，維護調和。

translations.literal: Bingying was heir to his father's elder brother; Yu served two mothers-in-law, maintaining and harmonizing relations.
translations.idiomatic: Bingying had been adopted as heir to his uncle's line; Yu served both mothers-in-law and kept harmony in the household.

sentences.zh: 迭遘諸喪，丙煐亦卒，喪葬皆盡禮。

translations.literal: They successively encountered many deaths; Bingying also died, and funerals and burials were all conducted with full propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Death followed death in the family; when Bingying died as well, Yu saw that every funeral was conducted with full propriety.

sentences.zh: 光緒二十六年，京師被兵，俞市米數十石與貧者，戚友相依者六十餘家，衣食之，亂定始去。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Guangxu the capital was overrun by troops; Yu bought several tens of shi of rice for the poor; more than sixty families of kin and friends who depended on her she clothed and fed, leaving only when the turmoil settled.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year of the Guangxu reign, when Beijing was overrun by soldiers, Yu bought dozens of shi of rice for the poor and fed and clothed more than sixty families of kinsmen and friends who had taken refuge with her, staying until order was restored.

sentences.zh: 亂後多暴骨，募貲為收斂。

translations.literal: After the turmoil there were many exposed bones; she raised funds to gather and bury them.
translations.idiomatic: After the chaos many corpses lay unburied; she raised money to collect and inter them.

sentences.zh: 死難者，求其姓名為請旌卹。

translations.literal: For those who died in the calamity, she sought their names and petitioned for commendation and relief.
translations.idiomatic: For those who had died in the disaster she traced their names and petitioned for imperial commendation and relief.

sentences.zh: 獄囚衣糧主者不能給，斥銀米畀之。

translations.literal: The officials in charge could not supply clothing and grain for prisoners; she spent silver and rice and gave it to them.
translations.idiomatic: When the authorities could not supply prisoners with food and clothing, she paid out silver and grain from her own funds.

sentences.zh: 其後直隸、安徽災，輒募貲至鉅萬。

translations.literal: Afterward when Zhili and Anhui suffered disasters, she always raised funds amounting to tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when disasters struck Zhili and Anhui, she repeatedly raised tens of thousands in relief funds.

sentences.zh: 京師卹嫠會、八旗工廠，皆輸金以助其成。

translations.literal: The Beijing Widows' Relief Society and the Eight Banners workshops all received her contributions of gold to help them succeed.
translations.idiomatic: She contributed funds to the Beijing Widows' Relief Society and the Eight Banners workshops to help establish them.

sentences.zh: 袁績懋妻左，績懋見忠義傳。

translations.literal: Zuo, wife of Yuan Jimao; Jimao is treated in the Biographies of the Loyal and Righteous.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo was the wife of Yuan Jimao, whose biography appears among the Loyal and Righteous.

sentences.zh: 左名錫璇，字芙江，陽湖人。

translations.literal: Zuo's given name was Xixuan, style name Fujiang, a native of Yanghu.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo's given name was Xixuan, her style name Fujiang, and she came from Yanghu.

sentences.zh: 事親孝，父病，刲臂和藥進。

translations.literal: Filial in serving her parents; when her father was ill, she cut her arm and mixed the flesh into medicine and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: She was filial toward her parents; when her father fell ill, she cut flesh from her arm and mixed it into his medicine.

sentences.zh: 工詩善畫，書法尤精，著有捲葹閣詩集。

translations.literal: Skilled at poetry and painting, especially accomplished in calligraphy; she authored the Juanwei Pavilion Poetry Collection.
translations.idiomatic: She was accomplished in poetry and painting and especially skilled in calligraphy; her collected poems were published as the Juanwei Pavilion Poetry Collection.

sentences.zh: 績懋子學昌妻曾，名懿，字伯淵，華陽人。

translations.literal: Zeng, wife of Jimao's son Xuechang, named Yi, style name Boyuan, a native of Huayang.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng, wife of Jimao's son Xuechang—her given name was Yi, her style name Boyuan—came from Huayang.

sentences.zh: 通書史，善課子，著有古歡室詩集、醫學篇、女學篇、中饋錄。

translations.literal: Well versed in books and history, skilled at instructing her son; she authored the Guhuan Studio Poetry Collection, Medical Learning, Women's Learning, and Records of the Kitchen.
translations.idiomatic: She was well read in history and literature and skilled at teaching her son; she wrote the Guhuan Studio Poetry Collection, Medical Learning, Women's Learning, and Records of the Kitchen.

sentences.zh: 俞振鸞妻傅，振鸞，餘杭人；

translations.literal: Fu, wife of Yu Zhenluan; Zhenluan was from Yuhang;
translations.idiomatic: Fu was the wife of Yu Zhenluan, who came from Yuhang;

sentences.zh: 傅名宛，號青泉，大興人，以禮女。

translations.literal: Fu's given name was Wan, style name Qingquan, a native of Daxing, renowned as a woman of propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Fu's given name was Wan, her style name Qingquan; she came from Daxing and was known as a woman of exemplary propriety.

sentences.zh: 能承父學，工詩，著有山青雲白軒詩集。

translations.literal: Able to inherit her father's learning, skilled at poetry; she authored the Shanyun Yunbai Studio Poetry Collection.
translations.idiomatic: She inherited her father's scholarship, was accomplished in poetry, and published the Shanyun Yunbai Studio Poetry Collection.

sentences.zh: 教子嚴，建宗祠，立條教，示子孫。

translations.literal: Strict in teaching her sons, she built an ancestral hall, established rules and teachings, and showed them to descendants.
translations.idiomatic: She was strict in raising her sons, built a family ancestral hall, and set down rules of conduct for future generations.

sentences.zh: 光、宣間，江、浙遇災，屢蠲金賑之。

translations.literal: Between the Guangxu and Xuantong eras, when Jiangsu and Zhejiang encountered disasters, she repeatedly contributed gold to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guangxu and Xuantong reigns, when disasters struck Jiangsu and Zhejiang, she repeatedly donated large sums for relief.

sentences.zh: 周懷伯妻邊，懷伯，餘杭人；

translations.literal: Bian, wife of Zhou Huaibo; Huaibo was from Yuhang;
translations.idiomatic: Bian was the wife of Zhou Huaibo, who came from Yuhang;

sentences.zh: 邊，諸暨人。

translations.literal: Bian was from Zhuji.
translations.idiomatic: Bian herself came from Zhuji.

sentences.zh: 邊事姑孝，懷伯卒，有女子子三。

translations.literal: Bian was filial in serving her mother-in-law; when Huaibo died, she had three daughters.
translations.idiomatic: Bian was devoted to her mother-in-law; when Huaibo died she was left with three daughters.

sentences.zh: 邊恃女紅養姑，營喪葬，嫁三女，貸於人以舉。

translations.literal: Bian relied on women's needlework to support her mother-in-law, arranged funerals and burials, married off three daughters, and borrowed from others to accomplish it.
translations.idiomatic: Bian supported her mother-in-law with needlework, arranged the funeral, and married off all three daughters, borrowing money to pay for it all.

sentences.zh: 節衣縮食，數十年乃畢償。

translations.literal: Economizing on clothing and food, only after several decades did she finish repaying.
translations.idiomatic: She lived frugally for decades before she finally paid off the debts.

sentences.zh: 年六十九，知將死，辭親族，啟夫墓右生壙，坐臥其中，遂死。

translations.literal: At sixty-nine, knowing she would die, she bade farewell to kin, opened the living tomb beside her husband's grave, sat and lay within it, and died.
translations.idiomatic: At sixty-nine, sensing death was near, she said farewell to her kin, opened the prepared tomb beside her husband's grave, sat down inside it, and died.

sentences.zh: 堅囑毋具棺，重以累人。

translations.literal: She firmly instructed that no coffin be prepared, lest it burden others.
translations.idiomatic: She firmly instructed that no coffin be made, not wanting to burden anyone.

sentences.zh: 親族哀其志，樏梩而掩之。

translations.literal: Kin grieved for her resolve and buried her with a coffin of plain boards.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by her resolve, her kin buried her in a simple plank coffin.

sentences.zh: 吉山妻瓜爾佳氏，名惠興，滿洲人，杭州駐防。

translations.literal: Huixing of the Guwalgiya clan, wife of Jishan, a Manchu stationed at the Hangzhou garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Huixing of the Guwalgiya clan, wife of Jishan, was a Manchu woman of the garrison at Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 早寡，事姑謹，嘗刲肱療姑疾。

translations.literal: Widowed early, she served her mother-in-law carefully and once cut flesh from her arm to treat her mother-in-law's illness.
translations.idiomatic: Widowed young, she dutifully cared for her mother-in-law and once cut flesh from her arm to treat her illness.

sentences.zh: 光緒季年，創立女學。

translations.literal: In the late Guangxu era she founded a school for girls.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Guangxu years she founded a school for girls.

sentences.zh: 逾年，貲不足，校將散，乃飲毒具牘上將軍，自陳以身殉校。

translations.literal: After a year funds were insufficient and the school was about to disband; she then drank poison and submitted a memorial to the general, declaring she would give her life for the school.
translations.idiomatic: A year later, when funds ran short and the school was about to close, she drank poison and sent a memorial to the general declaring she would give her life for the school.

sentences.zh: 且言曰：「雁過留聲，人過留名，我非樂死，不得已耳！」

translations.literal: She wrote, "Wild geese leave their call as they pass; people leave their names—I do not seek death for its own sake; I had no other choice!"
translations.idiomatic: She wrote, "Wild geese leave their call as they pass; people leave their names—I do not seek death for its own sake; I had no other choice!"

sentences.zh: 既死，將軍瑞興與巡撫張曾敭奏聞，賜「貞心毅力」額，眾為集貲擴校，以「惠興」名焉。

translations.literal: After her death General Ruixing and Governor Zhang Cengyi memorialized the throne; she was granted the plaque "Steadfast Heart and Resolute Will"; the people collected funds to expand the school, naming it "Huixing."
translations.idiomatic: After her death General Ruixing and Governor Zhang Cengyi reported the matter to the throne; she was granted a plaque reading "Steadfast Heart and Resolute Will," and the public raised funds to expand the school, which was named Huixing in her honor.

sentences.zh: 張某妻錢，嘉興人。

translations.literal: Qian, wife of a man surnamed Zhang, was from Jiaxing.
translations.idiomatic: Qian, the wife of a man surnamed Zhang, came from Jiaxing.

sentences.zh: 生一女而嫠，還依父母居。

translations.literal: She bore one daughter and was widowed; she returned to live depending on her parents.
translations.idiomatic: She had borne one daughter when she was widowed and returned to live with her parents.

sentences.zh: 姑貧，計鬻之，度錢剛，言無益，陽攜以省戚。

translations.literal: Her mother-in-law was poor and planned to sell her; judging that Qian's words would be useless, she pretended to take her to visit relatives.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother-in-law was poor and planned to sell her; knowing Qian's protests would be useless, she pretended to take her to visit relatives.

sentences.zh: 先期告鬻婦家，待郭外，舟出郭，別有舟來並艤，則鬻婦家人也。

translations.literal: She had beforehand informed the buyer's family and waited outside the city gate; when the boat left the gate, another boat came alongside—it was the buyer's family.
translations.idiomatic: She had secretly arranged with the buyer's family to wait outside the city gate; when their boat left the gate, another boat pulled alongside—it was the buyer's party.

sentences.zh: 姑乃告錢，錢即起，躍入水。

translations.literal: The mother-in-law then told Qian; Qian immediately rose and leaped into the water.
translations.idiomatic: The mother-in-law then told Qian what was happening; Qian at once jumped into the water.

sentences.zh: 鬻婦家人大驚，而姑已得錢，強婦往，趣舟行。

translations.literal: The buyer's family was greatly alarmed, but the mother-in-law had already received the money and forced the woman to go, urging the boat to depart.
translations.idiomatic: The buyer's family was horrified, but the mother-in-law had already taken the money and forced Qian aboard, ordering the boat to leave.

sentences.zh: 錢屢躍入水，持之不能止，至三。

translations.literal: Qian repeatedly leaped into the water; those holding her could not stop her, up to three times.
translations.idiomatic: Qian threw herself into the water again and again; those who held her could not restrain her, and she did so three times.

sentences.zh: 眾皆懼，乃送還父母家，而錢為救者搤胸傷，咯血，數月卒。

translations.literal: All were afraid and sent her back to her parents' home; Qian's chest was bruised by those who rescued her, she coughed blood, and died after several months.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, they sent her back to her parents' home; Qian's chest had been crushed by her rescuers, she coughed blood, and died a few months later.

sentences.zh: 戚成勳妻廖，江津人。

translations.literal: Liao, wife of Qi Chengxun, was from Jiangjin.
translations.idiomatic: Liao, the wife of Qi Chengxun, came from Jiangjin.

sentences.zh: 成勳家萬山中，張獻忠之亂，成勳出避寇，廖弱不能從，閉重門獨居。

translations.literal: Chengxun's family lived deep in the ten-thousand mountains; during Zhang Xianzhong's rebellion Chengxun went out to flee the bandits; Liao was weak and could not follow, so she shut the heavy doors and lived alone.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxun's family lived deep in the mountains; when Zhang Xianzhong's rebellion broke out Chengxun fled to escape the bandits, but Liao was too frail to follow and shut herself inside their home alone.

sentences.zh: 家故有餘粟，粟將盡，就池畔種稻以食。

translations.literal: The household originally had surplus grain; when the grain was nearly gone, she planted rice beside the pond to eat.
translations.idiomatic: When the household grain ran low she planted rice beside a pond to feed herself.

sentences.zh: 衣敝，綴草自蔽。

translations.literal: Her clothes were worn; she patched grass to cover herself.
translations.idiomatic: Her clothes wore out, so she patched together grass to cover herself.

sentences.zh: 居四十餘年，山徑塞，與世隔絕。

translations.literal: She lived more than forty years; mountain paths were blocked and she was cut off from the world.
translations.idiomatic: She lived there more than forty years, the mountain paths overgrown, completely cut off from the outside world.

sentences.zh: 成勳竄黔中，聞亂定，乃還，行求故山，斧竹木得道，見其宅盡圮，隱隱起炊煙。

translations.literal: Chengxun fled into Qianzhong; hearing the turmoil had settled, he returned, traveled seeking his old mountain, cut through bamboo and trees to find a path, saw his dwelling entirely collapsed, yet faint cooking smoke rose.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxun had fled into Guizhou; when he heard the rebellion was over he returned, hacked his way through bamboo and trees to find the old mountain path, found their house in ruins, yet saw faint smoke rising from cooking fires.

sentences.zh: 呼且入，廖自樓上問誰何，成勳道姓名，廖乃泣曰：「我夫今得還耶？

translations.literal: He called out and entered; Liao from upstairs asked who it was; Chengxun gave his name; Liao then wept and said, "Has my husband now been able to return?
translations.idiomatic: He called out and went in; Liao called from upstairs to ask who was there; when Chengxun gave his name she wept and said, "Has my husband truly come home?

sentences.zh: 我無衣，君以餘衣畀我，乃得下相見。」

translations.literal: I have no clothes—throw me something to wear so I can come down to meet you."
translations.idiomatic: I have no clothes—throw me something to wear so I can come down to meet you."

sentences.zh: 成勳解衣擲樓上，廖衣以下，面目黧黑，發如蓬，相持大慟。

translations.literal: Chengxun removed his clothes and threw them upstairs; Liao dressed and came down—her face was dark, her hair like a tangled thicket; they embraced and wailed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxun stripped off his spare clothes and threw them up; Liao dressed and came down—her face was blackened, her hair a tangled mess—and they embraced and wept bitterly.

sentences.zh: 其居又十餘年，年各至九十餘。

translations.literal: They lived together more than ten years further; each reached more than ninety years of age.
translations.idiomatic: They lived together another dozen years, each reaching more than ninety years of age.

sentences.zh: 曾惟庸妻譚，衡陽人。

translations.literal: Tan, wife of Zeng Weiyong, was from Hengyang.
translations.idiomatic: Tan, the wife of Zeng Weiyong, came from Hengyang.

sentences.zh: 順治五年，譚歸惟庸，方四閱月，惟庸為遊騎掠去。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Shunzhi Tan married Weiyong; after only four months Weiyong was seized by roaming cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Shunzhi reign Tan married Weiyong; only four months later roaming cavalry carried him off.

sentences.zh: 亂定，有言惟庸死者，譚召族人，分授以田宅。

translations.literal: When the turmoil settled, some said Weiyong had died; Tan summoned clansmen and distributed fields and houses among them.
translations.idiomatic: When order was restored and word came that Weiyong had died, Tan gathered the clan and divided the fields and houses among them.

sentences.zh: 康熙二年，惟庸還，詐稱行賈，過譚，音容已盡變，譚不能識。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kangxi Weiyong returned, falsely claiming to be a traveling merchant; passing Tan, his voice and appearance had completely changed and Tan could not recognize him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Kangxi reign Weiyong returned, posing as a traveling merchant; his voice and appearance had changed so completely that Tan did not recognize him.

sentences.zh: 求食，與之；

translations.literal: He asked for food and she gave it to him;
translations.idiomatic: He asked for food and she gave him some;

sentences.zh: 求借宿，不可。

translations.literal: he asked to stay the night and she refused.
translations.idiomatic: he asked to stay the night and she refused.

sentences.zh: 越日再至，乃自名惟庸，譚未敢信，問臨別時事，嘗授三鑰，鐵奇銅偶，語皆驗。

translations.literal: The next day he came again and then gave his name as Weiyong; Tan did not dare believe it; she asked about matters at their parting—he had once given three keys, one iron, one strange, one copper—and all his words were verified.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he returned and revealed his name; Tan still could not believe it until she tested him with details from their parting—he had once given her three keys, iron, copper, and an odd one—and everything he said checked out.

sentences.zh: 譚乃泣而言曰：「君別十六年，謂物故久，今幸生還，當告諸宗族。」

translations.literal: Tan wept and said, "You have been gone sixteen years; I thought you dead long ago. Now that you have returned alive, I must tell the clan."
translations.idiomatic: Tan wept and said, "You have been gone sixteen years; I thought you dead long ago. Now that you have returned alive, I must tell the clan."

sentences.zh: 惟庸召族人，置酒，具白其事，為夫婦如初。

translations.literal: Weiyong summoned clansmen, set out wine, fully explained the matter, and they were husband and wife as before.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyong gathered the clan, set out wine, explained everything, and they lived as husband and wife again.

sentences.zh: 謝萬程妻李，唐縣人。

translations.literal: Li, wife of Xie Wancheng, was from Tang County.
translations.idiomatic: Li, the wife of Xie Wancheng, came from Tang County.

sentences.zh: 萬程父儀，順治間諸生，貧，卒無棺，萬程將鬻妻以為斂，不忍言。

translations.literal: Wancheng's father Yi, a licentiate during Shunzhi, was poor; when he died there was no coffin; Wancheng planned to sell his wife to pay for the burial but could not bear to speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: Wancheng's father Yi had been a licentiate during the Shunzhi reign; when he died penniless without even a coffin, Wancheng planned to sell his wife to pay for the funeral but could not bring himself to say so.

sentences.zh: 李知萬程意，哭請行。

translations.literal: Li knew Wancheng's intent and weeping asked to go.
translations.idiomatic: Li understood what Wancheng was thinking and, weeping, volunteered to go.

sentences.zh: 南陽民王全以二十四金鬻李歸，將以為妾。

translations.literal: Wang Quan, a commoner of Nanyang, bought Li for twenty-four taels of gold and intended to make her his concubine.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Quan, a man of Nanyang, bought Li for twenty-four taels of silver and intended to take her as a concubine.

sentences.zh: 李至全家，日涕泣，但原供織紝，不肯侍全，全亦聽，不強。

translations.literal: When Li reached Wang's home she wept daily, only wishing to supply weaving and sewing, refusing to attend Quan; Quan also listened and did not force her.
translations.idiomatic: At Wang's house Li wept every day, offering only to weave and sew and refusing to serve him as a wife; Wang did not force her.

sentences.zh: 居一年所，全兄大有與全隙，詣南汝道告全匿逃人。

translations.literal: After about a year Quan's elder brother Dayou had a rift with Quan and went to the Nannu Circuit to report that Quan was hiding a fugitive.
translations.idiomatic: After about a year Quan's elder brother Dayou, who had a grudge against him, reported to the Nannu Circuit that Quan was harboring a fugitive.

sentences.zh: 事下南陽府同知張三異，三異漢陽人，嘗為陝西延長知縣，有惠政。

translations.literal: The case went down to Vice Magistrate Zhang Sanyi of Nanyang Prefecture; Sanyi was from Hanyang and had once been magistrate of Yanchang in Shaanxi, with benevolent administration.
translations.idiomatic: The case went to Vice Magistrate Zhang Sanyi of Nanyang Prefecture, a native of Hanyang who had once served as magistrate of Yanchang in Shaanxi with a reputation for benevolent rule.

sentences.zh: 詰大有，辭遁。

translations.literal: He interrogated Dayou, who evaded with excuses.
translations.idiomatic: He questioned Dayou, who evaded with excuses.

sentences.zh: 召全，並​​以李至，問何為匿逃人，全目李妾，因言：「妾至日涕泣，但原供織紝，居一年所，不我從也。」

translations.literal: He summoned Quan and brought Li as well; when asked why he was hiding a fugitive, Quan gestured at Li and said, "From the day she arrived she wept constantly, offering only to weave and sew; after a full year she still would not be my wife."
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Quan and brought Li as well; when asked why he was hiding a fugitive, Quan gestured at Li and said, "From the day she arrived she wept constantly, offering only to weave and sew; after a full year she still would not be my wife."

sentences.zh: 問得自何所，乃復召萬程，具得賣妻葬父狀。

translations.literal: Asked where he had obtained her, he then summoned Wancheng again and fully learned the circumstances of selling his wife to bury his father.
translations.idiomatic: Asked where he had gotten her, he summoned Wancheng and learned the full story of how he had sold his wife to bury his father.

sentences.zh: 三異驚嘆，問萬程：「欲復合否？」

translations.literal: Sanyi was deeply moved and asked Wancheng, "Do you want to be reunited with your wife?"
translations.idiomatic: Sanyi was deeply moved and asked Wancheng, "Do you want to be reunited with your wife?"

sentences.zh: 萬程言：「妻故無失德，聞其至王氏日涕泣，但原供織紝，居一年所，艱難以守身。

translations.literal: Wancheng said, "My wife originally had no moral failing; I heard that from the day she reached the Wang household she wept daily, only wishing to supply weaving and sewing; after about a year she arduously preserved her chastity.
translations.idiomatic: Wancheng said, "My wife has done nothing wrong; I hear that at the Wang household she wept every day, offering only to weave and sew, and after a full year managed with great difficulty to preserve her virtue.

sentences.zh: 我豈不欲合，而無其貲，則奈何？」

translations.literal: Of course I want to reunite with her, but without the money to redeem her, what can I do?"
translations.idiomatic: Of course I want to reunite with her, but without the money to redeem her, what can I do?"

sentences.zh: 三異出俸二十四金償全，而使吏以金幣送萬程夫婦還。

translations.literal: Sanyi paid out twenty-four taels from his salary to compensate Quan and had an official escort Wancheng and his wife home with gold and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Sanyi paid twenty-four taels from his own salary to compensate Wang Quan and sent an official to escort the Wanchengs home.

sentences.zh: 李殿機妻王，名素貞，亳州人。

translations.literal: Wang, wife of Li Dianji, named Suzhen, was from Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang, the wife of Li Dianji—her given name was Suzhen—came from Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 幼喪母，父以字殿機，殿機父範同，順治初坐法，妻張及殿機沒入象房，殿機方三歲。

translations.literal: She lost her mother in youth; her father had betrothed her to Dianji; Dianji's father Fan Tong, convicted under the law in early Shunzhi, had his wife Zhang and Dianji confiscated into the elephant quarters; Dianji was just three years old.
translations.idiomatic: She lost her mother as a child; her father had betrothed her to Dianji, whose father Fan Tong was convicted in the early Shunzhi reign and sent with his wife Zhang and young Dianji, then only three, to serve in the imperial elephant stables.

sentences.zh: 稍長，自鬻於鑲紅旗護軍厄爾庫為奴，厄爾庫妻以婢蕭。

translations.literal: When somewhat grown, he sold himself as a slave to the Bordered Red Banner guardsman E'erku; E'erku's wife was given the maid Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew older Dianji sold himself as a slave to E'erku, a guardsman of the Bordered Red Banner; E'erku's wife was given a maid named Xiao.

sentences.zh: 王從其父居二十餘年，其父病且死，以簪珥授女，泣曰：「此李氏物也！」

translations.literal: Wang lived with her father for more than twenty years; on his deathbed he gave her hairpins and earrings, weeping, "These belong to the Li family!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang lived with her father for more than twenty years; on his deathbed he gave her hairpins and earrings, weeping, "These belong to the Li family!"

sentences.zh: 又數年，或傳殿機死，王氏諸父兄迫女別嫁，女原為殿機死。

translations.literal: Several years later, some reported Dianji had died; Wang's uncles and elder brothers forced the daughter to remarry; the daughter wished to die for Dianji.
translations.idiomatic: Some years later word came that Dianji had died; her uncles and brothers pressed her to marry another, but she declared she would rather die for Dianji.

sentences.zh: 久之，诇殿機猶在，欲走京師求殿機。

translations.literal: After a long time she learned Dianji was still alive and wished to run to the capital to seek Dianji.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually she learned Dianji was still alive and resolved to go to Beijing to find him.

sentences.zh: 鄰有範一魁者，其父友也，王乞為導，諸父兄不欲，令處於樓，去其梯。

translations.literal: Among the neighbors was Fan Yikui, her father's friend; Wang begged him to guide her; her uncles and elder brothers did not wish it and had her kept on an upper floor, removing the ladder.
translations.idiomatic: A neighbor named Fan Yikui, her father's old friend, agreed to guide her; her uncles and brothers objected and locked her on an upper floor, removing the ladder.

sentences.zh: 王以夜縋而下，從一魁至京師，求諸象房，有知者導至厄爾庫家，殿機荷畚拾馬通自厩出。

translations.literal: Wang lowered herself by rope at night, followed Yikui to the capital, inquired at the elephant quarters; someone who knew the way guided them to E'erku's home; Dianji carrying a basket, gathering horse dung, came out from the stable.
translations.idiomatic: Wang lowered herself by rope at night and traveled with Yikui to Beijing; guided to the elephant stables and then to E'erku's home, she found Dianji coming out of the stables carrying a basket, shoveling horse dung.

sentences.zh: 一魁前與語，王出父故所授簪珥，相向哭，行路聚觀，皆流涕。

translations.literal: Yikui went forward and spoke with him; Wang produced the hairpins and earrings her father had formerly given; facing each other they wept; passersby gathered to watch and all shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: Yikui spoke to him first; Wang produced the hairpins and earrings her father had given her; they faced each other and wept while passersby gathered, all in tears.

sentences.zh: 厄爾庫義之，許放殿機及蕭，不督自鬻值。

translations.literal: E'erku considered it righteous and agreed to release Dianji and Xiao, not demanding the price of self-sale.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by their story, E'erku agreed to release Dianji and Xiao without demanding repayment of the purchase price.

sentences.zh: 巡視南城御史阿爾賽疏聞，下禮部。

translations.literal: Censor A'ersai, inspector of the Southern City, memorialized the throne; the case went down to the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Censor A'ersai, inspector of the Southern City, reported the matter to the throne, and the case was referred to the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 禮部議：「八旗家奴不得復為民，惟王氏守節求夫，有裨風化，應如所題。」

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites ruled: "Banner slaves may not ordinarily be restored to commoner status, but Wang's steadfast virtue in seeking her betrothed serves the cause of moral instruction and the petition should be granted."
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites ruled: "Banner slaves may not ordinarily be restored to commoner status, but Wang's steadfast virtue in seeking her betrothed serves the cause of moral instruction and the petition should be granted."

sentences.zh: 康熙二十八年四月乙未，疏上，聖祖可其議，王年已三十有四，猶處女也。

translations.literal: On the yimwei day of the fourth month of the twenty-eighth year of Kangxi the memorial went up; the Sage Ancestor approved the deliberation; Wang was already thirty-four years old and still a maiden.
translations.idiomatic: On the yimwei day of the fourth month of the twenty-eighth year of the Kangxi reign the memorial was approved by the Emperor; Wang was thirty-four years old and still a virgin.

sentences.zh: 長清婦王氏，父王三，農也。

translations.literal: A woman Wang of Changqing—her father Wang San was a farmer.
translations.idiomatic: A woman surnamed Wang of Changqing—her father Wang San was a farmer.

sentences.zh: 未行，歲祲，父母舅姑議鬻之，而均其值。

translations.literal: Before the marriage ceremony, in a year of famine, parents and parents-in-law discussed selling her and dividing the proceeds equally.
translations.idiomatic: Before the wedding, during a famine year, her parents and in-laws agreed to sell her and split the proceeds.

sentences.zh: 販挾以去，至饒陽，入妓家，矢死不肯汙。

translations.literal: A trafficker took her away; reaching Raoyang she was placed in a brothel; she swore to die rather than be defiled.
translations.idiomatic: A trafficker took her away; at Raoyang she was sold into a brothel, but she vowed she would die rather than be defiled.

sentences.zh: 轉至孔店村，村諸生孔繼禹、繼淳兄弟好義，愍其志，以五十金贖焉。

translations.literal: She was transferred to Kongdian Village; the village licentiates Kong Jiyu and Jichun, brothers who loved righteousness, pitied her resolve and redeemed her for fifty taels of gold.
translations.idiomatic: She was taken to Kongdian Village, where the licentiate brothers Kong Jiyu and Jichun, men of generous spirit, took pity on her and redeemed her for fifty taels.

sentences.zh: 問所居地，曰焦家台。

translations.literal: Asked where she lived, she said Jiajiatai.
translations.idiomatic: Asked where she was from, she said Jiajiatai.

sentences.zh: 問戚屬，以父王三對。

translations.literal: Asked about kin, she answered with her father Wang San.
translations.idiomatic: Asked about her family, she named her father Wang San.

sentences.zh: 當春，村民祠泰山，具榜書女始末畀行者，誡使入長清界則揭榜。

translations.literal: That spring when villagers worshipped at Mount Tai, they prepared a placard recording the woman's entire story and gave it to travelers, instructing them to post it when entering Changqing territory.
translations.idiomatic: That spring, when villagers made the pilgrimage to Mount Tai, they wrote out her whole story on a placard and gave it to travelers with instructions to post it when they entered Changqing territory.

sentences.zh: 焦家台農有見者，以告王三，詣孔氏以女歸，復歸所字壻。

translations.literal: A farmer at Jiajiatai who saw it told Wang San; he went to the Kong clan to bring his daughter home and restored her to her betrothed husband.
translations.idiomatic: A farmer at Jiajiatai who saw the placard told Wang San; he went to the Kong brothers, brought his daughter home, and restored her to her betrothed.

sentences.zh: 程允元妻劉，名秀石，允元，江南山陽山；

translations.literal: Liu, wife of Cheng Yun'yuan, named Xiushi; Yun'yuan was from Shanyang in Jiangnan;
translations.idiomatic: Liu, betrothed to Cheng Yun'yuan—her given name was Xiushi; Yun'yuan came from Shanyang in Jiangnan;

sentences.zh: 秀石，平谷人也。

translations.literal: Xiushi was from Pinggu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiushi came from Pinggu.

sentences.zh: 秀石父登庸，康熙間為山西蒲州知府。

translations.literal: Xiushi's father Dengyong during Kangxi served as prefect of Puzhou in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiushi's father Dengyong had served as prefect of Puzhou in Shanxi during the Kangxi reign.

sentences.zh: 初謁選，允元父舉人光奎，亦在京師。

translations.literal: When first awaiting appointment, Yun'yuan's father the juren Guangkui was also in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Dengyong first went to the capital to await appointment, Yun'yuan's father Guangkui, a juren degree holder, was also in Beijing.

sentences.zh: 相與友，申之以婚姻。

translations.literal: They became friends with each other and pledged marriage between their children.
translations.idiomatic: They became friends and pledged their children to each other in marriage.

sentences.zh: 時允元二歲，秀石生未期也。

translations.literal: At the time Yun'yuan was two years old and Xiushi was not yet one year old.
translations.idiomatic: Yun'yuan was two years old and Xiushi was not yet one.

sentences.zh: 光奎歸，尋​​卒。

translations.literal: Guangkui returned home and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Guangkui returned home and soon died.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，登庸罷官，居天津北倉，亦卒。

translations.literal: In early Qianlong Dengyong was dismissed from office, lived at Beicang in Tianjin, and also died.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Qianlong years Dengyong was dismissed from office, settled at Beicang near Tianjin, and died there as well.

sentences.zh: 秀石年二十二，母前卒，諸兄奔走衣食，弟崇善為童子師，徙廢宅。

translations.literal: Xiushi was twenty-two; her mother had died earlier; elder brothers scurried for food and clothing; younger brother Chongshan was a village schoolteacher and moved to an abandoned house.
translations.idiomatic: Xiushi was twenty-two; her mother had died; her elder brothers struggled to find food while her younger brother Chongshan taught village schoolchildren from a ruined house.

sentences.zh: 姊妹姑侄猶五六人，食不得飽，寒無衣，相倚坐取暖。

translations.literal: Sisters, sisters-in-law, and nephews still numbered five or six; they could not eat their fill, had no clothes against the cold, and sat leaning on each other for warmth.
translations.idiomatic: Five or six sisters, in-laws, and nephews still depended on them; they went hungry and had no warm clothes, huddling together for warmth.

sentences.zh: 崇善死，益貧，恆數日不得食。

translations.literal: Chongshan died and they grew poorer; often several days passed without food.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongshan died they grew even poorer, often going days without food.

sentences.zh: 屋破，群僵坐雨中，乃徙依比丘尼照震。

translations.literal: The house collapsed; the group sat stiff in the rain and then moved to depend on the Buddhist nun Zhaozhen.
