translations.idiomatic: When their house collapsed they sat huddled in the rain and then moved in with the Buddhist nun Zhaozhen.

sentences.zh: 無何，家人相繼死，惟秀石存，力針黹自活。

translations.literal: Before long family members died one after another; only Xiushi survived, supporting herself by strenuous needlework.
translations.idiomatic: Soon her family members died one after another; only Xiushi survived, supporting herself by needlework.

sentences.zh: 照震徙天津，秀石從。

translations.literal: Zhaozhen moved to Tianjin and Xiushi followed.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaozhen moved to Tianjin, Xiushi went with her.

sentences.zh: 嘗有求婚者，介照震道意，秀石恚，不食，照震力謝乃已。

translations.literal: Once there was a suitor; through Zhaozhen he conveyed his intent; Xiushi was angry and refused to eat; only after Zhaozhen firmly declined did it stop.
translations.idiomatic: When suitors came, Zhaozhen conveyed their proposals; Xiushi was furious and refused to eat until Zhaozhen firmly turned them away.

sentences.zh: 允元既喪父，亦中落，聞登庸卒，家且散，顧不知女存亡。

translations.literal: Yun'yuan having lost his father also declined in fortune; hearing Dengyong had died and the family was dispersing, he did not know whether the daughter lived or died.
translations.idiomatic: Yun'yuan had also fallen on hard times after his father's death; when he heard Dengyong had died and the family was breaking up, he had no idea whether Xiushi was alive or dead.

sentences.zh: 或傳女死，勸別娶，允元不可，且曰：「女即死，必酹其墓乃別娶。」

translations.literal: When word came that Xiushi had died, people urged him to marry someone else; Yun'yuan refused, saying, "Even if she is dead, I must pour libations at her grave before I marry again."
translations.idiomatic: When word came that Xiushi had died, people urged him to marry someone else; Yun'yuan refused, saying, "Even if she is dead, I must pour libations at her grave before I marry again."

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十二年，附運漕舟至北倉求劉氏，有舟人為言：「劉氏家已散，其孥殆盡死，惟第四女存，是嘗字淮安程氏，傳程氏子已死，而女矢不他適。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year of Qianlong he attached himself to a grain-transport boat to Beicang to seek the Liu clan; a boatman told him, "The Liu family has dispersed; their dependents are nearly all dead; only the fourth daughter survives—she was once betrothed to the Cheng clan of Huai'an; it was reported the Cheng son had died, yet the daughter swore not to marry another.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-second year of the Qianlong reign he traveled by grain boat to Beicang to find the Liu family; a boatman told him, "The Liu family is scattered and nearly all dead; only the fourth daughter survives—she was betrothed to the Cheng clan of Huai'an; though told the Cheng son had died, she vowed never to marry another.

sentences.zh: 昔居準提菴，今徙天津，不知菴何名也。」

translations.literal: She once lived at the Zhunti Nunnery and has now moved to Tianjin, though I do not know which temple she is at."
translations.idiomatic: She once lived at the Zhunti Nunnery and has now moved to Tianjin, though I do not know which temple she is at."

sentences.zh: 允元因言己即程氏子，舟人又言：「劉氏有故僕，瘖而義，歲時必問女起居。」

translations.literal: Yun'yuan said he was the Cheng son; the boatman added, "The Liu family has an old servant, mute but loyal, who inquires after the daughter's welfare every year."
translations.idiomatic: Yun'yuan said he was the Cheng son; the boatman added, "The Liu family has an old servant, mute but loyal, who inquires after the daughter's welfare every year."

sentences.zh: 允元求得僕，偕詣照震，言始末，照震疑，且憚秀石，未敢以通。

translations.literal: Yun'yuan found the servant and together went to Zhaozhen, explaining the whole story; Zhaozhen was doubtful and also feared Xiushi, not daring to convey it.
translations.idiomatic: Yun'yuan found the servant and together they went to Zhaozhen and told the whole story; Zhaozhen was skeptical and feared Xiushi's reaction, and did not dare tell her.

sentences.zh: 允元言於監漕吏，牒天津縣知縣金之忠，之忠召允元問之，信。

translations.literal: Yun'yuan spoke to the grain-transport supervisor, who sent a dispatch to Magistrate Jin Zhizhong of Tianjin County; Zhizhong summoned Yun'yuan and questioned him, and believed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yun'yuan appealed to the grain transport official, who wrote to Magistrate Jin Zhizhong of Tianjin County; Jin summoned Yun'yuan, questioned him, and found his story credible.

sentences.zh: 使告女，且勉之嫁，女猶辭。

translations.literal: He had the daughter told and urged her to marry; the daughter still declined.
translations.idiomatic: He sent word to Xiushi and urged her to marry; she still refused.

sentences.zh: 復使謂曰：「女不字五十七年，豈非為程郎？

translations.literal: He again had someone say to her, "The daughter has not been betrothed for fifty-seven years—is it not for Master Cheng?
translations.idiomatic: He sent word again: "You have remained unmarried for fifty-seven years—was it not for Cheng?

sentences.zh: 程郎至，天也，復何辭？」

translations.literal: Cheng has come—it is Heaven's will; what more is there to refuse?"
translations.idiomatic: Cheng has come—it is Heaven's will; what more is there to refuse?"

sentences.zh: 乃成婚。

translations.literal: They then married.
translations.idiomatic: At last they were married.

sentences.zh: 大學士兩江總督高晉以其事上聞，下禮部，禮部議：「義夫貞婦，例得旌表。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary and Governor-General of the Two Jiangs Gao Jin reported the matter to the throne; the Ministry of Rites ruled: "Righteous husbands and chaste wives are by precedent entitled to imperial commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary and Governor-General of the Two Jiangs Gao Jin reported the matter to the throne; the Ministry of Rites ruled: "Righteous husbands and chaste wives are by precedent entitled to imperial commendation.

sentences.zh: 至幼年聘定，彼此隔絕，經數十年之久，守義懷貞，各矢前盟，卒償所原，實從來所未有，應旌表以獎節義。」

translations.literal: But a betrothal made in childhood, followed by decades of separation during which both kept faith with their pledge and at last fulfilled their original vow—this was truly unprecedented and deserves commendation to reward their steadfast virtue."
translations.idiomatic: But a betrothal made in childhood, followed by decades of separation during which both kept faith with their pledge and at last fulfilled their original vow—this was truly unprecedented and deserves commendation to reward their steadfast virtue."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 楊某妻樊，字正，撫寧人。

translations.literal: Fan, wife of a man surnamed Yang, style name Zheng, was from Funing.
translations.idiomatic: Fan, betrothed to a man surnamed Yang—her style name was Zheng—came from Funing.

sentences.zh: 既字而楊氏子病且廢，使辭於樊，樊母乃為正改字。

translations.literal: Already betrothed, the Yang son fell ill and was crippled; he sent word to break the engagement with Fan; Fan's mother then changed Zheng's betrothal.
translations.idiomatic: After the betrothal the Yang son fell ill and was crippled; he sent word to break the engagement, and Fan's mother arranged a new match for her.

sentences.zh: 行有日，正請於母曰：「兒奚嫁？」

translations.literal: When the wedding day approached, Zheng asked her mother, "Whom am I to marry?"
translations.idiomatic: When the wedding day approached, Zheng asked her mother, "Whom am I to marry?"

sentences.zh: 母曰：「嫁某氏。」

translations.literal: Her mother said, "You are to marry so-and-so."
translations.idiomatic: Her mother said, "You are to marry so-and-so."

sentences.zh: 正曰：「兒幼非受楊氏聘乎？」

translations.literal: Zheng said, "Was I not betrothed to the Yang clan from childhood?"
translations.idiomatic: Zheng said, "Was I not betrothed to the Yang clan from childhood?"

sentences.zh: 母曰：「然，楊氏子病且廢，使辭於我。

translations.literal: Her mother said, "Yes, but the Yang son is ill and crippled; he sent word to break it with me.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother said, "Yes, but the Yang son is ill and crippled; he asked to be released from the engagement.

sentences.zh: 我憐兒，故為兒改字也。」

translations.literal: I felt sorry for you, so I arranged a new match."
translations.idiomatic: I felt sorry for you, so I arranged a new match."

sentences.zh: 正不語，夜潛出，度山林數十里，晨至楊氏。

translations.literal: Zheng said nothing; at night she stole out, crossed mountains and forests for several tens of li, and by morning reached the Yang household.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng said nothing; that night she slipped out, crossed miles of mountain wilderness, and by morning reached the Yang household.

sentences.zh: 翁姑未即許，父母亦至，相與慰勉。

translations.literal: Her parents-in-law did not immediately consent; her parents also arrived and together they comforted and encouraged her.
translations.idiomatic: Her future in-laws did not immediately agree; her parents arrived as well and all tried to reason with her.

sentences.zh: 正曰：「夫病，天也，我為病夫婦，亦天也，違天不祥。

translations.literal: Zheng said, "My husband's illness is Heaven's doing; that I should be wife to an ill man is also Heaven's doing; to defy Heaven is inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng said, "His illness is Heaven's will; that I should be wife to a sick man is also Heaven's will; to defy Heaven brings misfortune.

sentences.zh: 欲別嫁，我請死。」

translations.literal: If you want me to marry someone else, I ask only to die."
translations.idiomatic: If you want me to marry someone else, I ask only to die."

sentences.zh: 乃卒歸於楊，楊氏子病良已。

translations.literal: She then ultimately returned to the Yang clan; the Yang son's illness fully recovered.
translations.idiomatic: She was at last accepted into the Yang household, and the Yang son's illness fully recovered.

sentences.zh: 同縣又有劉柱兒妻魯，字春。

translations.literal: In the same county there was also Lu, wife of Liu Zhu'er, style name Chun.
translations.idiomatic: In the same county there was also Lu, betrothed to Liu Zhu'er—her style name was Chun.

sentences.zh: 柱兒先為李氏義子，聘於魯，既復還劉氏。

translations.literal: Zhu'er was first an adopted son of the Li clan and was betrothed to Lu; afterward he was returned to the Liu clan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu'er had first been adopted by the Li clan and betrothed to Lu, but was later returned to the Liu clan.

sentences.zh: 李富而劉貧，於是李氏之人，嗾魯使罷婚，劉不敢爭也。

translations.literal: The Li were rich and the Liu poor; therefore people of the Li clan incited Lu to break the engagement; Liu did not dare contend.
translations.idiomatic: The Li were wealthy and the Liu poor; the Li clan pressured Lu to break the engagement, and the Liu family did not dare object.

sentences.zh: 春聞，亡之劉氏，魯氏劫春歸。

translations.literal: When Chun heard, she fled to the Liu clan; the Lu clan seized Chun and brought her back.
translations.idiomatic: When Chun heard of this she fled to the Liu household, but the Lu clan seized her and brought her back.

sentences.zh: 訟於縣，縣判歸劉氏。

translations.literal: They sued at the county; the county magistrate ruled she should return to the Liu clan.
translations.idiomatic: The case went to the county magistrate, who ruled that Chun belonged to the Liu clan.

sentences.zh: 時乾隆十九年，先樊氏女事一歲。

translations.literal: This was in the nineteenth year of Qianlong, one year after the affair of Fan the woman.
translations.idiomatic: This occurred in the nineteenth year of the Qianlong reign, one year after the case of Fan Zheng.

sentences.zh: 李國郎妻蘇，南安人。

translations.literal: Su, wife of Li Guolang, was from Nan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Su, the wife of Li Guolang, came from Nan'an.

sentences.zh: 未行，父以國郎貧，為女別字富家子，焚李氏書幣。

translations.literal: Before the marriage ceremony, her father because Guolang was poor betrothed his daughter to a rich man's son and burned the Li family's betrothal letters and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Before the wedding her father, finding Guolang too poor, betrothed her to a wealthy man's son and burned the Li family's betrothal gifts.

sentences.zh: 蘇縊，未絕，父招富家子贅於家，以死拒，撻之不悔。

translations.literal: Su hanged herself but was not yet dead; her father invited the rich man's son to marry into the household; she refused with death, was beaten and did not repent.
translations.idiomatic: Su tried to hang herself but was cut down in time; her father brought the rich man's son to marry into the household, but she refused even under threat of death and did not yield despite being beaten.

sentences.zh: 富家子自去。

translations.literal: The rich man's son left on his own.
translations.idiomatic: The wealthy suitor left of his own accord.

sentences.zh: 國郎聞，訟於官，乃歸於李。

translations.literal: When Guolang heard, he sued at the authorities and she was returned to the Li clan.
translations.idiomatic: When Guolang heard, he brought the case to the authorities, and Su was restored to the Li family.

sentences.zh: 婚夕，泣曰：「吾父以吾故在系，何得遽言婚！」

translations.literal: On the wedding night she wept and said, "My father is in prison because of me—how can we speak of marriage now!"
translations.idiomatic: On the wedding night she wept and said, "My father is in prison because of me—how can we speak of marriage now!"

sentences.zh: 國郎為請於有司，出其父。

translations.literal: Guolang pleaded with the authorities and had her father released.
translations.idiomatic: Guolang appealed to the authorities and secured her father's release.

sentences.zh: 同縣蔡登龍妻林，其父母亦以婿貧欲別字，不從，令別居。

translations.literal: In the same county Lin, wife of Cai Denglong—her parents also because the son-in-law was poor wished to change the betrothal; she would not agree and was made to live separately.
translations.idiomatic: In the same county, Lin, betrothed to Cai Denglong, also faced pressure from her parents to break the engagement because he was poor; when she refused they made her live apart from the family.

sentences.zh: 積女紅得十五金，使以遺登龍佐聘錢，父母少之。

translations.literal: Accumulating needlework she obtained fifteen taels of gold and sent them to Denglong to help with betrothal money; her parents thought it too little.
translations.idiomatic: She saved fifteen taels from her needlework and sent them to Denglong to help pay the betrothal fee, but her parents considered it insufficient.

sentences.zh: 乃日減餐，治女紅益勤，逾年又得十餘金，卒歸登龍。

translations.literal: She then daily reduced her meals, worked at needlework all the more diligently, and after more than a year obtained more than ten taels further; she ultimately returned to Denglong.
translations.idiomatic: She ate less each day, worked harder at her needlework, and after another year saved more than ten taels more; at last she was married to Denglong.

sentences.zh: 父母既喪，孤弟貧無依，乃收撫之。

translations.literal: After her parents died her orphaned younger brother was poor with no one to rely on; she then took him in and raised him.
translations.idiomatic: After her parents died she took in her orphaned younger brother, who had no one else to depend on.

sentences.zh: 又有黃元河妻戴，吳恆妻陳，婿皆有廢疾，父母議毀盟，力請行。

translations.literal: There were also Dai, wife of Huang Yuanhe, and Chen, wife of Wu Heng—their betrothed husbands all had crippling illnesses; parents discussed breaking the engagements, but they strongly pleaded to proceed.
translations.idiomatic: There were also Dai, betrothed to Huang Yuanhe, and Chen, betrothed to Wu Heng—both fiances were crippled by illness and both sets of parents wanted to break the engagements, but the women insisted on going through with the marriages.

sentences.zh: 戴勤儉起其家，吳以節終。

translations.literal: Dai through diligence and thrift raised up the household; Wu ended her life in chastity.
translations.idiomatic: Dai through hard work and thrift restored the family fortunes; Chen lived out her life in chaste widowhood.

sentences.zh: 趙維石妻張，小字瑤娃，寧羌人。

translations.literal: Zhang, wife of Zhao Weishi, childhood name Yaowa, was from Ningqiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang, the wife of Zhao Weishi—her childhood name was Yaowa—came from Ningqiang.

sentences.zh: 年十七，未行。

translations.literal: At seventeen she had not yet undergone the marriage ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: She was seventeen and not yet married.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶初，教匪掠州，賊渠得之，以畀其妻。

translations.literal: In early Jiaqing the teaching-bandits plundered the prefecture; the bandit chief obtained her and gave her to his wife.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Jiaqing years rebel sectarians raided the prefecture; the bandit chief captured her and handed her over to his wife.

sentences.zh: 其妻以瑤娃慧，畜為女，渠累欲汙之，賴其妻以免。

translations.literal: His wife because Yaowa was clever kept her as a daughter; the chief repeatedly wished to defile her and she was spared thanks to his wife.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, finding Yaowa intelligent, kept her as a foster daughter; the chief repeatedly tried to violate her, but his wife protected her each time.

sentences.zh: 尋竄徽縣，一夕渠醉，召瑤娃，瑤娃拒之力，渠使其下將出殺之。

translations.literal: Soon they fled to Huixian; one night the chief was drunk and summoned Yaowa; Yaowa resisted forcefully; the chief had his subordinates take her out to kill her.
translations.idiomatic: They soon fled to Huixian; one night the chief, drunk, summoned Yaowa; when she resisted fiercely he ordered his men to take her out and kill her.

sentences.zh: 其妻知不可救，戒勿過創，棄諸野，而以死告。

translations.literal: His wife knew she could not be saved and warned them not to wound her too severely; they abandoned her in the wild and reported her dead.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, knowing she could not be saved, told the men not to inflict fatal wounds; they left her in the wilderness and reported that she was dead.

sentences.zh: 次日賊引去，村婦舁之歸，藥其創良愈，將以為子婦。

translations.literal: The next day the bandits withdrew; village women carried her back, treated her wounds until she recovered well, and intended to make her their son's wife.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the bandits moved on; village women found her and carried her home, nursed her wounds until she recovered, and planned to make her their son's wife.

sentences.zh: 會縣吏過門，瑤娃拔銀釵賄吏，使告縣。

translations.literal: A county clerk happened to pass the door; Yaowa pulled out a silver hairpin to bribe the clerk and had him report to the county.
translations.idiomatic: When a county clerk passed by, Yaowa pulled out a silver hairpin to bribe him into reporting her case to the magistrate.

sentences.zh: 瑤娃至縣庭，陳始末，乃召維石，為合婚，與俱歸。

translations.literal: Yaowa came to the county court, explained the whole story from beginning to end; they then summoned Weishi, performed the marriage, and she returned home with him.
translations.idiomatic: Yaowa appeared before the magistrate and told her whole story; Weishi was summoned, they were married, and she returned home with him.

sentences.zh: 鍾某聘妻吳，武岡人。

translations.literal: Wu, betrothed wife of a man surnamed Zhong, was from Wugang.
translations.idiomatic: Wu, betrothed to a man surnamed Zhong, came from Wugang.

sentences.zh: 待年於鍾氏。

translations.literal: She awaited the proper age at the Zhong household.
translations.idiomatic: She lived at the Zhong household awaiting the proper age for marriage.

sentences.zh: 鍾氏子從父賈四川，久不歸，或傳已死。

translations.literal: The Zhong son followed his father to trade in Sichuan and did not return for a long time; some reported he had died.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhong son had gone with his father to trade in Sichuan and did not return for many years; some said he had died.

sentences.zh: 鍾母卒，吳紡績奉其祖母。

translations.literal: When Zhong's mother died, Wu spun and wove to support his grandmother.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhong mother died, Wu supported the grandmother by spinning and weaving.

sentences.zh: 祖母卒，為營喪葬。

translations.literal: When the grandmother died, she arranged the funeral and burial.
translations.idiomatic: When the grandmother died as well, she arranged the funeral.

sentences.zh: 年四十餘，鍾氏子始歸，欲與婚，吳曰：「君出遊久，安用就木老處子為！」

translations.literal: When she was over forty the Zhong son finally returned and wanted to marry her; Wu said, "You have been away so long—what need is there to marry an old spinster now!"
translations.idiomatic: When she was over forty the Zhong son finally returned and wanted to marry her; Wu said, "You have been away so long—what need is there to marry an old spinster now!"

sentences.zh: 出貲為買妾，而自居別室。

translations.literal: She paid out funds to buy a concubine for him and herself lived in a separate chamber.
translations.idiomatic: She paid for a concubine for him and moved into a separate room herself.

sentences.zh: 鍾氏子以不婦訟於官，吳曰：「若祖母，吾奉之；

translations.literal: The Zhong son sued at the authorities for failure to be a wife; Wu said, "As for your grandmother, I served her;
translations.idiomatic: The Zhong son sued her for refusing to be his wife; Wu said, "I served your grandmother;

sentences.zh: 若妾，吾畜之。

translations.literal: as for your concubine, I provided for her.
translations.idiomatic: I provided for your concubine.

sentences.zh: 吾齒長，不能育子女，請以貞終。」

translations.literal: I am too old to bear children; I ask only to live out my life in chastity."
translations.idiomatic: I am too old to bear children; I ask only to live out my life in chastity."

sentences.zh: 官判從之。

translations.literal: The magistrate ruled in her favor.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate ruled in her favor.

sentences.zh: 岳氏，安平人。

translations.literal: The Yue clan woman was from Anping.
translations.idiomatic: A woman of the Yue clan came from Anping.

sentences.zh: 嫁可仁言，病癇。

translations.literal: She married Ke Renyan, who suffered from epilepsy.
translations.idiomatic: She married Ke Renyan, who suffered from epilepsy.

sentences.zh: 仁言以禮去惡疾，遂大歸。

translations.literal: Renyan according to ritual sent her away because of the bad illness, and she made the great return to her natal home.
translations.idiomatic: Renyan sent her back to her natal home according to ritual because of his illness.

sentences.zh: 居數年，病已，而仁言已別娶。

translations.literal: After several years the illness was cured, but Renyan had already married another.
translations.idiomatic: After several years his illness was cured, but Renyan had already taken another wife.

sentences.zh: 或諷其嫁，岳不應，以針線遍綴衣履投井死。

translations.literal: Some hinted she should remarry; Yue did not respond, sewed all her clothing and shoes together with needle and thread, and threw herself into a well to die.
translations.idiomatic: When people suggested she remarry, Yue did not reply; she stitched all her clothes and shoes together and drowned herself in a well.

sentences.zh: 仁言聞，乞李恭銘其墓。

translations.literal: When Renyan heard, he begged Li Gong to inscribe her tomb.
translations.idiomatic: When Renyan heard the news he asked Li Gong to write the inscription for her grave.

sentences.zh: 姚氏，通州人。

translations.literal: The Yao clan woman was from Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: A woman of the Yao clan came from Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 嫁同州張維垣。

translations.literal: She married Zhang Weiyuan of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: She married Zhang Weiyuan of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 維垣移家湖北，歸既娶，复去。

translations.literal: Weiyuan moved his family to Hubei; he returned, married her, and left again.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyuan moved his family to Hubei, returned to marry her, and then left again.

sentences.zh: 逾年，遺書絕姚，令改嫁。

translations.literal: After a year he sent a letter breaking with Yao and ordering her to remarry.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he sent a letter renouncing her and telling her to remarry.

sentences.zh: 姚持書泣告鄉黨曰：「我無故見絕，死無以自白，原終守以明志。」

translations.literal: Yao wept as she showed the letter to her neighbors, saying, "I have been cast off without cause; only by remaining chaste to the end can I prove my innocence."
translations.idiomatic: Yao wept as she showed the letter to her neighbors, saying, "I have been cast off without cause; only by remaining chaste to the end can I prove my innocence."

sentences.zh: 居五十餘年乃卒。

translations.literal: She lived more than fifty years and then died.
translations.idiomatic: She lived in widowhood for more than fifty years before she died.

sentences.zh: 張氏之族高其義，持喪葬張氏兆，為立後。

translations.literal: The Zhang clan honored her righteousness, conducted mourning and burial at the Zhang ancestral grave, and established an heir.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhang clan honored her virtue, gave her a funeral in the Zhang family graveyard, and established an heir for the line.

sentences.zh: 張氏，江南華亭人。

translations.literal: The Zhang clan woman was from Huating in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: A woman surnamed Zhang came from Huating in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 字金景山。

translations.literal: She was betrothed to Jin Jingshan.
translations.idiomatic: She was betrothed to Jin Jingshan.

sentences.zh: 年十二，喪父母，待年於姑氏。

translations.literal: At twelve she lost her parents and awaited the proper age at her mother-in-law's household.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve she lost both parents and went to live at her future mother-in-law's home awaiting marriage.

sentences.zh: 張莊而無容，景山憎焉。

translations.literal: Zhang was plain and without beauty; Jingshan detested her.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang was plain and unattractive, and Jingshan despised her.

sentences.zh: 稍長，當婚，景山故遲之。

translations.literal: When somewhat grown and it was time to marry, Jingshan deliberately delayed.
translations.idiomatic: When she came of age Jingshan deliberately put off the wedding.

sentences.zh: 既而病作，張奉湯藥，斥不使近，輒泣而退。

translations.literal: Before long illness set in; Zhang served soup and medicine but was driven away and not allowed near; she would weep and withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill Zhang tried to bring him medicine, but he drove her away; she would withdraw in tears.

sentences.zh: 景山將死，指而語母曰：「彼非吾偶，兒死必嫁之。」

translations.literal: On his deathbed Jingshan pointed at her and told his mother, "She is not my match; when I die you must marry her to someone else."
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed Jingshan pointed at her and told his mother, "She is not my match; when I die you must marry her to someone else."

sentences.zh: 景山死，張矢不嫁。

translations.literal: When Jingshan died, Zhang swore not to remarry.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingshan died, Zhang vowed never to marry again.

sentences.zh: 或以夫不見答勸，曰：「我知夫死婦節而已，不知其他。

translations.literal: Some because the husband had not treated her well urged her; she said, "I know only that when the husband dies the wife keeps chastity—I know nothing else.
translations.idiomatic: When people urged her to remarry because her betrothed had never loved her, she said, "I know only that when a husband dies the wife must remain chaste—that is all I know.

sentences.zh: 且祖姑及姑誰為養者？

translations.literal: Moreover, who will support the grandmother-in-law and mother-in-law?
translations.idiomatic: Besides, who will care for his grandmother and mother?

sentences.zh: 若必強我，我請死。」

translations.literal: If you force me, I ask only to die."
translations.idiomatic: If you force me, I ask only to die."

sentences.zh: 是歲姑卒，越八年，祖姑卒，張為營葬。

translations.literal: That year the mother-in-law died; after eight years the grandmother-in-law died; Zhang arranged their burials.
translations.idiomatic: That year her mother-in-law died; eight years later the grandmother-in-law died as well, and Zhang arranged both funerals.

sentences.zh: 日夕紡績，足不喻閾，又三十餘年乃卒。

translations.literal: Morning and evening she spun; her feet never crossed the threshold; after more than thirty years further she died.
translations.idiomatic: She spun morning and evening and never stepped outside the door; more than thirty years later she died.

sentences.zh: 袁氏，名機，字素文，仁和人。

translations.literal: The Yuan clan woman, named Ji, style name Suwen, was from Renhe.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ji, style name Suwen, came from Renhe.

sentences.zh: 兄枚，見文苑傳。

translations.literal: Her elder brother Mei is treated in the Literary Garden Biography.
translations.idiomatic: Her elder brother Yuan Mei is the subject of a biography in the Literary Garden section.

sentences.zh: 機幼字如皋高氏子，高氏子長而有惡疾，其父請離婚，機曰：「女從一者也，疾，我侍之；

translations.literal: Ji in youth was betrothed to the Gao clan son of Rugao; when the Gao son grew up he had a serious illness; his father requested divorce; Ji said, "A woman follows one man—if he is ill, I serve him;
translations.idiomatic: Ji was betrothed in childhood to a son of the Gao clan of Rugao; when he grew up and fell gravely ill, his father asked to dissolve the engagement; Ji said, "A woman belongs to one man—if he is ill, I will care for him;

sentences.zh: 死，我守之。」

translations.literal: if he dies, I will remain faithful to him."
translations.idiomatic: if he dies, I will remain faithful to him."

sentences.zh: 卒歸於高。

translations.literal: She ultimately returned to the Gao clan.
translations.idiomatic: She went through with the marriage to the Gao family.

sentences.zh: 高氏子躁戾佻盪，遊狹邪，傾其奩具；

translations.literal: The Gao son was violent, cruel, and frivolous; he frequented disreputable quarters and squandered her dowry;
translations.idiomatic: The Gao son was violent and dissolute; he frequented brothels and squandered her dowry;

sentences.zh: 不足，抶之，且灼以火。

translations.literal: when it was insufficient he beat her and even burned her with fire.
translations.idiomatic: when that was gone he beat her and even burned her with fire.

sentences.zh: 姑救，則毆母折齒。

translations.literal: When his mother tried to save her, he beat his mother and broke her teeth.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother tried to protect her, he beat his mother and broke her teeth.

sentences.zh: 既，欲鬻機以償博負，乃大歸，齋素奉母。

translations.literal: Afterward he wished to sell Ji to pay gambling debts; she then made the great return, ate vegetarian food, and served her mother.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually he tried to sell her to pay his gambling debts; she returned to her natal home, ate only vegetarian food, and cared for her mother.

sentences.zh: 高氏子死，哭之慟，越一年卒。

translations.literal: When the Gao son died she mourned him bitterly; after a year she died.
translations.idiomatic: When the Gao son died she mourned him deeply; a year later she died herself.

sentences.zh: 楊某妻張，名荷，寧國人。

translations.literal: Zhang, wife of a man surnamed Yang, named He, was from Ningguo.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang, the wife of a man surnamed Yang—her given name was He—came from Ningguo.

sentences.zh: 某貧，無行，令張以非義，不應。

translations.literal: The man was poor and without principle; he ordered Zhang to do improper things and she would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Yang was poor and dissolute; he demanded improper things of Zhang and she refused.

sentences.zh: 樓居，潛去床前板，紿使墮，折足，匍匐歸母家。

translations.literal: Living upstairs, he secretly removed the floorboards before the bed, deceived her into falling, broke her foot, and she crawled back to her mother's home.
translations.idiomatic: They lived upstairs; he secretly removed the floorboards by the bed, tricked her into falling and broke her leg; she crawled back to her mother's home.

sentences.zh: 某鬻子，張積金贖之。

translations.literal: The man sold their son; Zhang accumulated gold to redeem him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang sold their son, Zhang saved money to buy him back.

sentences.zh: 將卒，命子以喪歸楊氏。

translations.literal: About to die, she ordered her son to return with the funeral to the Yang clan.
translations.idiomatic: On her deathbed she told her son to bury her in the Yang family graveyard.

sentences.zh: 周士英聘妻張，泰州人。

translations.literal: Zhang, betrothed wife of Zhou Shiying, was from Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang, betrothed to Zhou Shiying, came from Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 士英喪父母，叔狡，利其有，箠殺之。

translations.literal: Shiying lost his parents; his uncle was cunning and coveting his property beat him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying lost his parents; his uncle, greedy for the inheritance, beat him to death.

sentences.zh: 時順治九年，張年十九，未行，聞其事，哭，不食。

translations.literal: At the time it was the ninth year of Shunzhi; Zhang was nineteen and had not yet married; hearing the affair she wept and refused to eat.
translations.idiomatic: It was the ninth year of the Shunzhi reign; Zhang was nineteen and not yet married; when she heard the news she wept and stopped eating.

sentences.zh: 遂自髡為尼，具牘丐母舅偕訴有司。

translations.literal: She then shaved her head and became a nun, prepared a document and begged her maternal uncle to join her in suing the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: She shaved her head and became a nun, then drafted a petition and asked her maternal uncle to help her bring the case before the authorities.

sentences.zh: 巡按為上其事，誅殺人賊，張乃理士英家財，葬士英及其祖若父，為廬奉佛，祀周氏三世。

translations.literal: The touring censor memorialized the affair upward; the murderous villain was executed; Zhang then settled Shiying's family property, buried Shiying and his grandfather and father, built a hut to worship the Buddha, and sacrificed to three generations of the Zhou clan.
translations.idiomatic: The touring censor reported the case to the throne; the murderous uncle was executed; Zhang then settled Shiying's estate, buried Shiying along with his grandfather and father, built a hut where she worshipped the Buddha, and maintained sacrifices to three generations of the Zhou clan.

sentences.zh: 張既為尼，名曰明貞，表其志也。

translations.literal: Zhang having become a nun took the name Mingzhen to express her resolve.
translations.idiomatic: As a nun she took the name Mingzhen—"Clear Chastity"—to express her purpose.

sentences.zh: 藺壯聘妻宋，名典，蔚州人。

translations.literal: Song, betrothed wife of Lin Zhuang, named Dian, was from Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Song, betrothed to Lin Zhuang—her given name was Dian—came from Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 典家西崖頭，壯居千字村，皆農家也，以羅帕為聘。

translations.literal: Dian's family was at Xiyaitou, Zhuang lived at Qianzicun—both were farming families; a silk handkerchief served as betrothal gift.
translations.idiomatic: Dian's family lived at Xiyaitou and Zhuang's at Qianzicun—both were farming families; a silk handkerchief served as the betrothal gift.

sentences.zh: 壯死，典方從母舂穀，聞，輟舂，慟不食。

translations.literal: When Zhuang died, Dian was just helping her mother pound grain; hearing the news she stopped pounding, grieved, and refused to eat.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuang died, Dian was helping her mother thresh grain; hearing the news she stopped work, grieved bitterly, and refused to eat.

sentences.zh: 父母喻之，意若稍解者，數日，以羅帕自經死。

translations.literal: Her parents reasoned with her and she seemed slightly to understand; several days later she hanged herself with the silk handkerchief.
translations.idiomatic: Her parents tried to comfort her and she seemed to relent; a few days later she hanged herself with the betrothal handkerchief.

sentences.zh: 時康熙四年正月庚辰。

translations.literal: This was on the gengchen day of the first month of the fourth year of Kangxi.
translations.idiomatic: This was on the gengchen day of the first month of the fourth year of the Kangxi reign.

sentences.zh: 沈煜聘妻陳，名三淑，錢塘人。

translations.literal: Chen, betrothed wife of Shen Yu, named Sanshu, was from Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen, betrothed to Shen Yu—her given name was Sanshu—came from Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 幼能詩。

translations.literal: From childhood she could compose poetry.
translations.idiomatic: She wrote poetry from childhood.

sentences.zh: 康熙間，訛言官中閱選，民間女子倉卒嫁娶殆盡，三淑父以許煜。

translations.literal: During Kangxi a false rumor spread that the palace was conducting a selection; commoners' daughters were hastily married off nearly to exhaustion; Sanshu's father betrothed her to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kangxi reign a rumor spread that the palace was selecting girls for the court; families rushed to marry off their daughters, and Sanshu's father betrothed her to Yu.

sentences.zh: 煜故貧，客松江，久不歸，三淑父從軍雲南，戰死。

translations.literal: Yu was originally poor, sojourning in Songjiang and not returning for a long time; Sanshu's father followed the army to Yunnan and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was poor and had gone to work in Songjiang, staying away for years; Sanshu's father joined the army in Yunnan and was killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 其母欲改字富人子，揚言煜已他娶，以絕三淑意。

translations.literal: Her mother wished to change the betrothal to a rich man's son and spread word that Yu had already married another to cut off Sanshu's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother wanted to betroth her to a rich man's son and spread the rumor that Yu had already married someone else, hoping to break Sanshu's resolve.

sentences.zh: 三淑聞，慟哭，自髡其發，矢不字，遂病，時時哭，極悲。

translations.literal: When Sanshu heard she wailed, shaved her own hair, swore not to be betrothed, then fell ill, weeping from time to time in extreme grief.
translations.idiomatic: When Sanshu heard this she wept bitterly, cut off her own hair, vowed never to marry another, fell ill, and wept constantly in deepest grief.

sentences.zh: 鄰生有聞而哀之者，求煜告以故，煜請婚，母持不可。

translations.literal: A neighboring student who heard and pitied her sought out Yu and told him the reason; Yu requested marriage but the mother firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: A neighbor who heard her story and was moved sought out Yu and told him what had happened; Yu asked to marry her, but her mother refused.

sentences.zh: 二十二年春二月，三淑病篤，其母以媒言召煜，煜至，使入省三淑。

translations.literal: In the second month of spring of the twenty-second year Sanshu was gravely ill; her mother through a matchmaker summoned Yu; Yu arrived and was sent in to visit Sanshu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the twenty-second year Sanshu was dying; her mother sent for Yu through a matchmaker; when Yu arrived she let him in to see Sanshu.

sentences.zh: 三淑方寐，告以沈郎至，遽寤，手下帷自蔽。

translations.literal: Sanshu was just asleep; told that Master Shen had arrived, she suddenly awoke and drew the curtain down to hide herself.
translations.idiomatic: Sanshu was sleeping; when told that Shen had come she woke at once and pulled the bed curtain down to hide herself.

sentences.zh: 煜問：「可有言乎？」

translations.literal: Yu asked, "Does she have anything to say?"
translations.idiomatic: Yu asked, "Does she have anything to say?"

sentences.zh: 三淑徐曰：「既有成言，何為又他娶？」

translations.literal: Sanshu said slowly, "We had a pledge—why did you marry someone else?"
translations.idiomatic: Sanshu said slowly, "We had a pledge—why did you marry someone else?"

sentences.zh: 煜辨其誣，三淑都無言，惟以袂掩淚。

translations.literal: Yu argued it was slander; Sanshu had nothing to say, only covering her tears with her sleeve.
translations.idiomatic: Yu protested that it was a lie; Sanshu said nothing, only covered her face with her sleeve and wept.

sentences.zh: 煜辭出，三淑泣不已。

translations.literal: Yu took leave and went out; Sanshu wept without stopping.
translations.idiomatic: Yu left; Sanshu wept without end.

sentences.zh: 已而歎曰：「彼不負我，我死可。」

translations.literal: Later she sighed and said, "He has been faithful to me—I can die content."
translations.idiomatic: Later she sighed and said, "He has been faithful to me—I can die content."

sentences.zh: 遂不飲藥，越日卒。

translations.literal: She then refused to take medicine and died the next day.
translations.idiomatic: She refused her medicine and died the following day.

sentences.zh: 王國隆聘妻餘，懷遠人。

translations.literal: Yu, betrothed wife of Wang Guolong, was from Huaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, betrothed to Wang Guolong, came from Huaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 國隆遊不歸，或言在含山，餘父母挈餘行求不遇，遂僑居焉。

translations.literal: Guolong traveled and did not return; some said he was in Hanshan; Yu's parents took Yu to seek him but did not find him, and so they sojourned there.
translations.idiomatic: Guolong went traveling and never returned; some said he was in Hanshan; Yu's parents took her there to search for him but failed to find him, and they settled there as exiles.

sentences.zh: 餘母死，從父灌園，紡績自活，恆以巾冪首，鄰女罕見其面。

translations.literal: When Yu's mother died she followed her father in irrigating gardens and supported herself by spinning; she always covered her head with a cloth and neighboring girls rarely saw her face.
translations.idiomatic: After Yu's mother died she helped her father tend gardens and supported herself by spinning; she always kept her head covered and neighbors rarely saw her face.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十八年，父死，斂畢，女自經。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year of Kangxi her father died; after the burial was complete the daughter hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year of the Kangxi reign her father died; as soon as the burial was over she hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 韋思誠聘妻宣，廣德人。

translations.literal: Xuan, betrothed wife of Wei Sicheng, was from Guangde.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan, betrothed to Wei Sicheng, came from Guangde.

sentences.zh: 思誠遠行，母以貧，欲令改字，宣不可，遂歸夫家。

translations.literal: Sicheng traveled far; his mother because of poverty wished to have the betrothal changed; Xuan would not agree and returned to her husband's family.
translations.idiomatic: Sicheng went away on a long journey; his mother, citing poverty, wanted to break the engagement, but Xuan refused and went to live at her future husband's home.

sentences.zh: 慮有強暴竊伺，夜懸柝於床，微風柝有聲以警。

translations.literal: Fearing violent men might spy and steal upon her, at night she hung a clapper by the bed so that the slightest breeze would make the clapper sound as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing intruders, she hung a clapper by her bed at night so that even a slight breeze would sound an alarm.

sentences.zh: 一夕，語諸姑、姊，夢夫告以死。

translations.literal: One night she told her sisters-in-law that she dreamed her husband told her he had died.
translations.idiomatic: One night she told her sisters-in-law that she had dreamed her husband telling her he was dead.

sentences.zh: 遂哀泣，不食死。

translations.literal: She then grieved and wept, refused food, and died.
translations.idiomatic: She mourned and wept, stopped eating, and died.

sentences.zh: 於天祥聘妻王，名秀女，祥符人。

translations.literal: Wang, betrothed wife of Yu Tianxiang, named Xiunü, was from Xiangfu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang, betrothed to Yu Tianxiang—her given name was Xiunü—came from Xiangfu.

sentences.zh: 天祥嘗育於陽武王氏，王氏為娶妻，生子，妻死，還於氏。

translations.literal: Tianxiang had been raised in the Yangwu Wang clan; the Wang clan found him a wife, who bore a son; when the wife died he returned to the Yu clan.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxiang had been raised by the Wang clan of Yangwu; they found him a wife who bore a son, and when she died he returned to the Yu family.

sentences.zh: 繼室以王，王未行，而天祥死，王父母秘不使知。

translations.literal: His second wife was to be Wang; Wang had not yet undergone the marriage ceremony when Tianxiang died; Wang's parents kept it secret and did not let her know.
translations.idiomatic: Wang was betrothed as his second wife, but before the wedding Tianxiang died; Wang's parents kept the news from her.

sentences.zh: 久之始聞，力請奔喪，天祥喪已小祥矣。

translations.literal: After a long time she finally heard; she strongly pleaded to rush to the mourning; Tianxiang's mourning had already passed the xiaoxiang rite.
translations.idiomatic: When she finally learned the truth she begged to go mourn him, though the first month of mourning had already passed.

sentences.zh: 王請於陽武王氏，原得子天祥前室子，王氏靳不許。

translations.literal: Wang requested of the Yangwu Wang clan that she might have Tianxiang's son by his former wife; the Wang clan grudgingly refused.
translations.idiomatic: Wang asked the Wang clan of Yangwu to let her raise Tianxiang's son by his first wife, but they refused.

sentences.zh: 及大祥，具奠，即夕自經。

translations.literal: When the daxiang rite came she prepared offerings and that very evening hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the mourning period she made offerings and hanged herself that same evening.

sentences.zh: 於氏故有刈麥刀二，俄失其一，至是得諸王枕下。

translations.literal: The Yu clan originally had two sickles for reaping wheat; soon one was lost; at this time it was found under Wang's pillow.
translations.idiomatic: The Yu family had owned two wheat sickles; one had gone missing and was now found under Wang's pillow.

sentences.zh: 方禮祕聘妻範，名二妹，建水人。

translations.literal: Fan, betrothed wife of Fang Limi, named Ermei, was from Jianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Fan, betrothed to Fang Limi—her given name was Ermei—came from Jianshui.

sentences.zh: 幼事父可望孝，字禮祕，未行。

translations.literal: From youth she served her father Kewang filially; she was betrothed to Limi but had not yet married.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood she was filial to her father Kewang; she was betrothed to Limi but not yet married.

sentences.zh: 禮祕父良佐死，妻改嫁蕭伸，居方氏，禮祕及其兄、妹皆死。

translations.literal: Limi's father Liangzuo died; his wife remarried Xiao Shen and lived at the Fang household; Limi and his elder brother and younger sister all died.
translations.idiomatic: Limi's father Liangzuo died; his widow remarried Xiao Shen and lived in the Fang household, where Limi and his siblings all died.

sentences.zh: 範聞，哭之慟，請於父母歸方氏。

translations.literal: When Fan heard she mourned bitterly and asked her parents to let her return to the Fang clan.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan heard the news she mourned bitterly and asked her parents to let her go to the Fang household.

sentences.zh: 居久之，聞姑詬伸，始知禮祕非良死，以質姑，姑內慚，不復言。

translations.literal: After living there a long time she heard her mother-in-law reviling Shen and first learned Limi had not died a natural death; she confronted her mother-in-law, who was ashamed within and spoke no more.
translations.idiomatic: After living there some time she overheard her mother-in-law cursing Shen and realized Limi had not died naturally; when she confronted her mother-in-law, the woman was too ashamed to reply.

sentences.zh: 範度事無證，禮祕冤不得白，恆時時號痛。

translations.literal: Fan judged there was no evidence for the affair; Limi's injustice could not be cleared and she constantly wailed in pain.
translations.idiomatic: Fan saw there was no proof of the crime; Limi's wrong could never be redressed, and she wailed in grief constantly.

sentences.zh: 伸憚範，欲以妻其從子，百方強之，範不許。

translations.literal: Shen feared Fan and wished to marry her to his younger clansman's son; he tried every means to force her but Fan would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Shen feared Fan and tried every way to marry her off to his nephew; Fan refused.

sentences.zh: 伸怒揮範僕，手點額。

translations.literal: Shen in anger struck Fan's servant; his hand touched her forehead.
translations.idiomatic: Shen flew into a rage and struck Fan's servant, his hand touching her forehead.

sentences.zh: 範怒曰：「奴汙我額！」

translations.literal: Fan cried out in rage, "A slave has defiled my brow!"
translations.idiomatic: Fan cried out in rage, "A slave has defiled my brow!"

sentences.zh: 刀剜伸手所點處，血淋漓被面。

translations.literal: With a knife she gouged out the spot Shen's hand had touched; blood poured down covering her face.
translations.idiomatic: She cut away the flesh where his hand had touched her; blood streamed down her face.

sentences.zh: 其弟訟諸吏，吏笞伸，以其室屬範，使奉方氏祀。

translations.literal: Her younger brother sued before the authorities; the authorities flogged Shen and assigned the household to Fan, having her maintain the Fang clan sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Her brother brought the case to the authorities; Shen was flogged, the household was given to Fan, and she was charged with maintaining the Fang clan sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 姚世治聘妻陳，會稽人。

translations.literal: Chen, betrothed wife of Yao Shizhi, was from Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Chen, betrothed to Yao Shizhi, came from Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 兩家皆居京師。

translations.literal: Both families lived in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Both families lived in Beijing.

sentences.zh: 既定約，世治歸，陳父欲別嫁，陳易服行求世治，遇諸濟寧。

translations.literal: After the engagement was settled Shizhi returned home; Chen's father wished to betroth her elsewhere; Chen changed clothes and traveled seeking Shizhi, meeting him at Jining.
translations.idiomatic: After the betrothal was settled Shizhi returned home; when Chen's father wanted to marry her to someone else, Chen disguised herself and went searching for Shizhi, finding him at Jining.

sentences.zh: 曰：「女違父非孝，得見君子，事畢矣！」

translations.literal: She said, "A daughter who disobeys her father is unfilial, but now that I have seen you, my duty is done!"
translations.idiomatic: She said, "A daughter who disobeys her father is unfilial, but now that I have seen you, my duty is done!"

sentences.zh: 遂入水死。

translations.literal: She then entered the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: She threw herself into the water and died.

sentences.zh: 何秉儀聘妻劉，昆明人，農家女也。

translations.literal: Liu, betrothed wife of He Bingyi, was from Kunming, a farmer's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Liu, betrothed to He Bingyi, was a farmer's daughter from Kunming.

sentences.zh: 秉儀卒，女請於父母，欲奔喪，不許。

translations.literal: When Bingyi died the girl asked her parents, wishing to rush to the mourning; they did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: When Bingyi died she begged her parents to let her go mourn him, but they refused.

sentences.zh: 乃竊出，兄追及之，度金汁河，將赴水，兄力持曳以歸。

translations.literal: She then stole out; her elder brother pursued and caught up; crossing the Jinzhijiang River she was about to enter the water; her brother forcibly held and dragged her back.
translations.idiomatic: She slipped out secretly; her brother caught up with her at the Jinzhijiang River as she was about to throw herself in and forcibly dragged her home.

sentences.zh: 秉儀父使迎女，女哀慟泣血，日夕力作。

translations.literal: Bingyi's father had the girl welcomed; the girl grieved bitterly and wept blood, working hard labor morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: Bingyi's father sent for her; she mourned so bitterly she wept blood and worked hard labor day and night.

sentences.zh: 父母畀田四畝，女為夫弟婚鬻半，喪舅又鬻半。

translations.literal: Her parents gave her four mu of fields; the girl sold half to pay for her husband's younger brother's marriage and sold the other half for her father-in-law's funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Her parents gave her four mu of land; she sold half to pay for her brother-in-law's wedding and the other half for her father-in-law's funeral.

sentences.zh: 父母怒，使告姑，誣女有所私，當遣之嫁。

translations.literal: Her parents were angry and had someone tell her mother-in-law, falsely accusing the girl of having a private affair and that she should be sent to remarry.
translations.idiomatic: Her parents, angry, told her mother-in-law falsely that she had taken a lover and should be sent away to remarry.

sentences.zh: 姑以責女，女不能自白，心疾作，縊死。

translations.literal: Her mother-in-law reproached the girl; the girl could not clear herself; heart illness set in and she hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother-in-law reproached her; unable to defend herself she fell into despair and hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 沈之螽聘妻唐，之螽，普安人；

translations.literal: Tang, betrothed wife of Shen Zhizhong; Zhizhong was from Pu'an;
translations.idiomatic: Tang was betrothed to Shen Zhizhong, who came from Pu'an;

sentences.zh: 唐，武進人。

translations.literal: Tang was from Wujin.
translations.idiomatic: Tang came from Wujin.

sentences.zh: 之螽父文鬱，唐父元聲，康熙季年，同遊高州，相友善，約為婚姻，於是唐生三年矣。

translations.literal: Zhizhong's father Wenyü and Tang's father Yuansheng in the late Kangxi era traveled together to Gaozhou, became friendly, and pledged marriage; at that time Tang was three years old.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhong's father Wenyü and Tang's father Yuansheng became friends while traveling in Gaozhou in the late Kangxi years and pledged their children in marriage when Tang was three.

sentences.zh: 元聲卒，喪歸，文鬱亦還普安。

translations.literal: When Yuansheng died his coffin returned home; Wenyü also returned to Pu'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuansheng died and his coffin was sent home, Wenyü also returned to Pu'an.

sentences.zh: 普安去武進且萬里，而文鬱貧，慮不能為之螽娶，詭言之螽殤，使謝唐，唐矢死。

translations.literal: Pu'an was nearly ten thousand li from Wujin, and Wenyü was poor, fearing he could not marry Zhizhong; he falsely said Zhizhong had died young and sent word to break with Tang; Tang swore to die.
translations.idiomatic: Pu'an was nearly ten thousand li from Wujin, and Wenyü, too poor to arrange the marriage, falsely reported that Zhizhong had died young and broke off the engagement; Tang vowed she would die rather than marry another.

sentences.zh: 久之，文鬱將如京師求官，迂道至常州，唐出拜，涕泣慷慨陳所志。

translations.literal: After a long time Wenyü was about to go to the capital to seek an official post; taking a detour to Changzhou, Tang came out to pay respects, weeping and passionately stating her resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Years later, when Wenyü was traveling to Beijing to seek an official post, he detoured to Changzhou; Tang came out to greet him, weeping as she passionately declared her steadfast resolve.

sentences.zh: 文鬱心悔，則請為養女，期得官迓以歸。

translations.literal: Wenyü's heart repented; he then asked to take her as an adopted daughter, promising when he obtained an office to welcome her home.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyü was filled with remorse and asked to adopt her as a daughter, promising to bring her home once he gained an official post.

sentences.zh: 既，文鬱以病還，唐聞大慟，遂不食，七日竟死。

translations.literal: Afterward Wenyü returned because of illness; when Tang heard she grieved greatly, then refused food, and after seven days died.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenyü returned home ill, Tang was stricken with grief, stopped eating, and died after seven days.

sentences.zh: 後三十餘年，之螽以事過常州，始聞唐死狀，感痛求其墓，已火葬矣。

translations.literal: More than thirty years later Zhizhong passing through Changzhou on business first heard of Tang's death; moved with pain he sought her grave—it had already been cremated.
translations.idiomatic: More than thirty years later, when Zhizhong passed through Changzhou on business, he first learned of Tang's death; grieving, he searched for her grave, but she had already been cremated.

sentences.zh: 唐死時年十六。

translations.literal: When Tang died she was sixteen years old.
translations.idiomatic: Tang was sixteen when she died.

sentences.zh: 貝勒弘暾聘妻富察氏，弘暾，怡親王允祥第三子。

translations.literal: The Fuca clan woman, betrothed wife of Prince Hongdun; Hongdun was the third son of Prince Yi Yunxiang.
translations.idiomatic: A woman of the Fuca clan was betrothed to Prince Hongdun, the third son of Prince Yi Yunxiang.

sentences.zh: 上命指配富察氏，雍正六年，未婚卒。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered her betrothed to the Fuca clan woman; in the sixth year of Yongzheng, unmarried, he died.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had betrothed him to the Fuca woman; in the sixth year of the Yongzheng reign he died before the marriage could take place.

sentences.zh: 富察氏聞，大慟，截發詣王邸，請持服，王不許；

translations.literal: When the Fuca woman heard she grieved greatly, cut off her hair, and went to the princely residence requesting to wear mourning; the prince did not permit it;
translations.idiomatic: When the Fuca woman heard the news she grieved bitterly, cut off her hair, and went to the prince's residence to ask permission to mourn; the prince refused;

sentences.zh: 跪門外，哭，至夕，王終不許，乃還其家持服。

translations.literal: she knelt outside the gate and wept until evening; the prince ultimately did not permit it, and she returned to her home to wear mourning.
translations.idiomatic: she knelt outside the gate and wept until evening, but the prince still refused, so she returned home to mourn on her own.

sentences.zh: 越二年，王薨，复詣王邸請持服，王邸長史奏聞，上命許之。

translations.literal: After two years the prince died; she again went to the princely residence requesting to wear mourning; the chief steward of the princely residence memorialized the throne and the Emperor ordered it permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later, when the prince died, she again went to the residence to request mourning rights; the chief steward reported the matter and the Emperor granted permission.

sentences.zh: 諭王福晉收為子婦，令弘暾祭葬視貝勒例，以從子永喜襲貝勒。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the prince's consort to take her in as a daughter-in-law, directed that Hongdun's sacrifices and burial follow the prince-lieutenant precedent, and had the clansman's son Yongxi inherit the prince-lieutenant title.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered the prince's consort to take her in as a daughter-in-law, directed that Hongdun's funeral rites follow princely precedent, and had the clansman's son Yongxi inherit the beile title.

sentences.zh: 諭謂：「俾富察氏無子而有子，以彰節女之厚報焉。」

translations.literal: The edict stated, "Let the Fuca woman be without a son yet have a son, to manifest the rich reward for a chaste woman."
translations.idiomatic: The edict declared, "Thus the Fuca woman, though without a son, shall have a son—in reward for the virtue of a chaste woman."

sentences.zh: 濰上女子，不知其氏，雍正間，濰田家女也。

translations.literal: A girl of Weishang—her clan name is unknown; during Yongzhi she was a girl of a Weitian farming family.
translations.idiomatic: A girl from Weishang whose surname is unknown was, during the Yongzheng reign, the daughter of a farming family there.

sentences.zh: 未行而夫死，其母往吊，女請從，母止之不可。

translations.literal: Before the marriage ceremony her betrothed died; her mother went to offer condolences; the girl asked to follow but her mother could not stop her.
translations.idiomatic: Before the wedding her betrothed died; when her mother went to offer condolences the girl insisted on going along, and her mother could not stop her.

sentences.zh: 衣紅而襲以素，濰俗婦弔喪不至殯，女陽為如廁，因問得殯室，潛入，去襲，縊柩側。

translations.literal: She wore red beneath covered with white; by Weifang custom women did not attend mourning until the encoffining; the girl pretended to go to the privy, thereby learned where the coffin chamber was, stole in, removed the white covering, and hanged herself beside the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: She wore red beneath a white outer garment; by local custom women did not attend funerals until encoffining; she pretended to need the privy, found the coffin room, slipped in, removed her white covering, and hanged herself beside the coffin.

sentences.zh: 吳某聘妻林，漳浦人。

translations.literal: Lin, betrothed wife of a man surnamed Wu, was from Zhangpu.
translations.idiomatic: Lin, betrothed to a man surnamed Wu, came from Zhangpu.

sentences.zh: 未行，夫坐罪當死，林欲入獄與訣，夫丐獄卒勿納，林晝夜哭不食。

translations.literal: Before the marriage ceremony her betrothed was convicted and sentenced to death; Lin wished to enter the prison for a farewell; her betrothed begged the jailers not to admit her; Lin wept day and night and refused to eat.
translations.idiomatic: Before the wedding her betrothed was convicted and sentenced to death; Lin wanted to visit him in prison for a final farewell, but he begged the jailers not to admit her; she wept day and night and refused to eat.

sentences.zh: 夫使畀以錢三百，且曰：「速擇佳婿，毋自苦！」

translations.literal: He sent her three hundred cash with the message, "Find yourself a good husband quickly—do not suffer for my sake!"
translations.idiomatic: He sent her three hundred cash with the message, "Find yourself a good husband quickly—do not suffer for my sake!"

sentences.zh: 越日，聞夫已決，以所畀錢易絙縊。

translations.literal: The next day, hearing her betrothed had been executed, she exchanged the money given her for a rope and hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, hearing he had been executed, she used the money he sent to buy a rope and hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 雷廷外聘妻侯，南安人。

translations.literal: Hou, betrothed wife of Lei Tingwai, was from Nan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Hou, betrothed to Lei Tingwai, came from Nan'an.

sentences.zh: 廷外母黃，早寡，貧，慮不能娶，乞貧家女撫之，期長以為婦，故侯四歲而育於黃。

translations.literal: Tingwai's mother Huang was widowed early and poor, fearing she could not afford a marriage; she begged a poor family's daughter to raise, planning when grown to make her a daughter-in-law; thus Hou at four years was raised by Huang.
translations.idiomatic: Tingwai's mother Huang was widowed young and too poor to afford a proper marriage; she took in a poor family's daughter to raise, planning to make her his daughter-in-law—Hou had lived with Huang since she was four.

sentences.zh: 十一黃卒，十六廷外卒，死而不瞑，侯慟屢絕。

translations.literal: At eleven Huang died; at sixteen Tingwai died, his eyes not closing in death; Hou grieved until she repeatedly fainted.
translations.idiomatic: Huang died when Hou was eleven; Tingwai died when she was sixteen, his eyes still open; Hou mourned until she repeatedly lost consciousness.

sentences.zh: 廷外有從兄，以其子震

translations.literal: Tingwai had a younger clansman's elder brother who made his son Zhen
translations.idiomatic: Tingwai had a cousin who made his son Zhen

sentences.zh: 為後，侯乃笄，抱以拜祖。

translations.literal: the heir; Hou then put up her hair in the married woman's style and holding him performed obeisance to the ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: the heir to the line; Hou then put up her hair as a married woman and, holding the boy, bowed before the ancestral tablets.

sentences.zh: 侯母欲令別嫁，拒以死。

translations.literal: Hou's mother wished to have her remarry; she refused on pain of death.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou's mother wanted her to remarry, she refused, threatening death.

sentences.zh: 身自耕，跪而耨，十指皆胼。

translations.literal: She personally farmed, kneeling to weed; all ten fingers were calloused.
translations.idiomatic: She farmed herself, weeding on her knees until all ten fingers were calloused.

sentences.zh: 嘗誡震曰：「婦人不可受人憐，況孀乎！」

translations.literal: She once warned Zhen, "A woman must never accept pity from others—especially a widow!"
translations.idiomatic: She once warned Zhen, "A woman must never accept pity from others—especially a widow!"

sentences.zh: 震亦早卒，其妻傅，從姑織蓆以育子。

translations.literal: Zhen also died early; his wife Fu followed her aunt-in-law in weaving mats to raise their son.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen also died young; his wife Fu wove mats alongside her aunt-in-law to raise their son.

sentences.zh: 程樹聘妻宋，名景衛，長洲人。

translations.literal: Song, betrothed wife of Cheng Shu, named Jingwei, was from Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Song, betrothed to Cheng Shu—her given name was Jingwei—came from Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 樹十三補諸生，喪母，复喪大父，旋亦卒。

translations.literal: Shu at thirteen became a licentiate supplement; he lost his mother, then also lost his grandfather, and soon also died.
translations.idiomatic: Shu became a licentiate at thirteen; he lost his mother, then his grandfather, and soon died himself.

sentences.zh: 景衛年二十，請於父，歸程。

translations.literal: Jingwei at twenty asked her father and returned to the Cheng clan.
translations.idiomatic: Jingwei, then twenty, asked her father's permission and went to the Cheng household.

sentences.zh: 以素服拜舅，見於廟；

translations.literal: In plain white garments she bowed to her father-in-law and appeared in the ancestral temple;
translations.idiomatic: Dressed in plain white she bowed to her father-in-law and appeared before the ancestral shrine;

sentences.zh: 謁其大父喪，成孫婦服；

translations.literal: she attended her grandfather-in-law's mourning and completed the garb of a grandson's wife;
translations.idiomatic: she observed mourning for his grandfather as a grandson's wife;

sentences.zh: 謁其母喪，成婦服；

translations.literal: she attended her mother-in-law's mourning and completed the garb of a wife;
translations.idiomatic: she observed mourning for his mother as a wife;

sentences.zh: 乃哭其夫，持服三年；

translations.literal: then she wept for her husband and wore mourning three years;
translations.idiomatic: then she mourned her husband for three years;

sentences.zh: 終，复補行姑服三年。

translations.literal: when that ended she again completed mourning for her mother-in-law for three years.
translations.idiomatic: when that ended she observed another three years of mourning for her mother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 同縣陳氏女淑睿，未行而婿殤，有請婚者，遂自經。

translations.literal: In the same county Chen's daughter Shurui, before the marriage ceremony her betrothed died young; when suitors came she hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: In the same county, Chen's daughter Shurui hanged herself when suitors came after her betrothed died before the wedding.

sentences.zh: 景衛為作詩，於詩共姜用劉向說，於春秋伯姬用何休說，旁採硃彝尊、汪琬、彭定求諸家言，申女子子未嫁守貞之義。

translations.literal: Jingwei composed a poem for her; in the poem on Jiang Gong she used Liu Xiang's interpretation; on Bo Ji in the Spring and Autumn Annals she used He Xiu's interpretation; drawing also on Zhu Yizun, Wang Wan, Peng Dingqiu and various scholars' views, she expounded the principle that an unmarried woman should preserve chastity.
translations.idiomatic: Jingwei wrote a poem for her, citing Liu Xiang on Jiang Gong and He Xiu on Bo Ji in the Spring and Autumn Annals, drawing also on Zhu Yizun, Wang Wan, Peng Dingqiu and others to argue that an unbetrothed woman owes the same duty of chastity.

sentences.zh: 貫​​穿賅洽，八百餘言，以破俗說，白己志。

translations.literal: Penetrating and comprehensive, more than eight hundred words, to break vulgar opinion and clarify her own resolve.
translations.idiomatic: In more than eight hundred tightly argued words she refuted popular opinion and declared her own conviction.

sentences.zh: 景衛通經義，好讀先儒論學書，娣、侄皆從講說。

translations.literal: Jingwei was versed in classical meaning and loved reading the Neo-Confucian books on learning; younger sisters-in-law and nieces all followed her lectures.
translations.idiomatic: Jingwei was well versed in the classics and loved reading Neo-Confucian works; her sisters-in-law and nieces all attended her lectures.

sentences.zh: 病女教不明，乃會通古訓，括聖賢修身盡倫之要，復作詩九百餘言，授娣、侄，令歌習之。

translations.literal: Lamenting that women's teaching was unclear, she synthesized ancient glosses, summarized the essentials of sage self-cultivation and fulfillment of human bonds, and again composed a poem of more than nine hundred words, giving it to younger sisters-in-law and nieces and having them sing and study it.
translations.idiomatic: Distressed that women's education was neglected, she synthesized classical teachings on sage self-cultivation and human bonds into a poem of more than nine hundred lines, which she taught her sisters-in-law and nieces to recite.

sentences.zh: 張氏子聘妻姜，名桂，元和人。

translations.literal: Jiang, betrothed wife of Zhang's son, named Gui, was from Yuanhe.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang, betrothed to the Zhang family's son—her given name was Gui—came from Yuanhe.

sentences.zh: 年十九，婿與舅、姑先後卒，依其母以居，不嫁。

translations.literal: At nineteen her betrothed and father-in-law and mother-in-law died one after another; she lived depending on her mother and did not remarry.
translations.idiomatic: At nineteen her betrothed and his parents died in succession; she lived with her mother and never married.

sentences.zh: 錢氏子聘妻王，吳人，亦年十九而婿卒，女絕食，大父母強起之。

translations.literal: Wang, betrothed wife of Qian's son, a native of Wu, also at nineteen her betrothed died; the girl stopped eating and her grandparents forcibly made her rise.
translations.idiomatic: Wang, betrothed to the Qian family's son and also from Wu, was nineteen when her betrothed died; she stopped eating until her grandparents forced her to take food.

sentences.zh: 居三年，有請婚者，复絕食，死復甦。

translations.literal: After three years when suitors came she again stopped eating, died and revived.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later, when suitors came again, she stopped eating once more and nearly died.

sentences.zh: 母哭之，女曰：「先年兒私吞金環不死，食銀硃又不死，頃复吞金環。

translations.literal: Her mother wept for her; the girl said, "In earlier years I privately swallowed a gold ring and did not die; I ate cinnabar and did not die; just now I again swallowed a gold ring.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother wept over her; the girl said, "Years ago I swallowed a gold ring and did not die; I ate cinnabar and did not die; just now I have swallowed a gold ring again.

sentences.zh: 兒死原得葬錢氏之兆。」

translations.literal: When I die I ask only to be buried in the Qian family graveyard."
translations.idiomatic: When I die I ask only to be buried in the Qian family graveyard."

sentences.zh: 遂卒。

translations.literal: She then died.
translations.idiomatic: She died.

sentences.zh: 王誌曾聘妻張，亦吳人。

translations.literal: Zhang, betrothed wife of Wang Zhiceng, was also from Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang, betrothed to Wang Zhiceng, was also from Wu.

sentences.zh: 年二十，誌曾卒。

translations.literal: At twenty Zhiceng died.
translations.idiomatic: She was twenty when Zhiceng died.

sentences.zh: 居六年，聞姑喪，因歸於王，奉佛以終。

translations.literal: After six years she heard of her mother-in-law's death and therefore returned to the Wang clan, worshipping the Buddha to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Six years later, hearing of her mother-in-law's death, she went to the Wang household and devoted herself to Buddhist practice for the rest of her life.

sentences.zh: 三女皆與景衛同時，而桂能詩善畫，嘗為柏舟圖，賦詩贈景衛。

translations.literal: All three women were contemporaries of Jingwei; Gui could compose poetry and was skilled at painting; she once made a Bo Zhou painting and composed a poem presenting it to Jingwei.
translations.idiomatic: All three women were contemporaries of Jingwei; Gui was accomplished in poetry and painting and once painted the Bo Zhou scene and wrote a poem for Jingwei.

sentences.zh: 景衛有二婢：曰衛喜，字於張，張死，不更字；

translations.literal: Jingwei had two maidservants: one named Weixi, betrothed to Zhang; when Zhang died she did not change the betrothal;
translations.idiomatic: Jingwei had two maidservants: one named Weixi, betrothed to a man surnamed Zhang—when Zhang died she did not accept another match;

sentences.zh: 曰陳壽，嫁硃氏，寡，無子。

translations.literal: The other was named Chen Shou; she married into the Zhu clan, was widowed, and had no son.
translations.idiomatic: The other was named Chen Shou; she had married into the Zhu clan, was widowed, and had no children.

sentences.zh: 皆依景衛以老。

translations.literal: Both depended on Jingwei into old age.
translations.idiomatic: Both lived out their lives under Jingwei's care.

sentences.zh: 李家勳聘妻楊，海寧人。

translations.literal: Yang, betrothed wife of Li Jiaxun, was from Haining.
translations.idiomatic: Yang, betrothed to Li Jiaxun, came from Haining.

sentences.zh: 楊富而李貧，家勳父為楊氏佃。

translations.literal: The Yang were rich and the Li poor; Jiaxun's father was a tenant of the Yang clan.
translations.idiomatic: The Yang family was wealthy and the Li family poor; Jiaxun's father farmed land for the Yang clan.

sentences.zh: 楊父行田，見家勳慧，問之，九歲，使入所立塾，資令讀。

translations.literal: Yang's father while inspecting the fields saw Jiaxun was clever; asked his age—nine years—and had him enter the clan school he had established, providing funds for his study.
translations.idiomatic: While inspecting his fields Yang's father noticed how bright Jiaxun was; learning he was nine, he enrolled him in the clan school he had founded and paid for his education.

sentences.zh: 年十五入學為諸生，家勳父來謝，楊年十四，呼令出拜。

translations.literal: At fifteen he entered school and became a licentiate; Jiaxun's father came to give thanks; Yang was fourteen and was called out to pay respects.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen Jiaxun passed the licentiate examinations; when his father came to give thanks, Yang, then fourteen, was called out to greet him.

sentences.zh: 楊母及兄皆恚曰：「是老顛！

translations.literal: Yang's mother and elder brother were both angry and said, "The old man is senile!
translations.idiomatic: Yang's mother and elder brother were furious and said, "The old fool!

sentences.zh: 豈患女無家，而棄諸佃人子乎？」

translations.literal: Does he think his daughter cannot find a husband, that he would give her to a tenant farmer's son?"
translations.idiomatic: Does he think his daughter cannot find a husband, that he would give her to a tenant farmer's son?"

sentences.zh: 父旋卒，楊氏之人薄家勳。

translations.literal: The father soon died; people of the Yang clan looked down on Jiaxun.
translations.idiomatic: The father soon died, and the Yang clan looked down on Jiaxun.

sentences.zh: 一夕，呼燈，無應者，楊自帷言曰：「丈夫不自處高明，何依人受慢為！」

translations.literal: One evening he called for a lamp and no one answered; Yang spoke from behind her curtain, "A man who will not stand on his own dignity—why live as a dependent and accept their scorn!"
translations.idiomatic: One evening he called for a lamp and no one answered; Yang spoke from behind her curtain, "A man who will not stand on his own dignity—why live as a dependent and accept their scorn!"

sentences.zh: 家勳遂辭楊氏去。

translations.literal: Jiaxun then took leave of the Yang clan and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaxun then left the Yang household.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十五年，舉浙江鄉試，楊氏請婚，家勳以試禮部辭。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Qianlong he passed the Zhejiang provincial examination; the Yang clan requested marriage; Jiaxun declined citing the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of the Qianlong reign he passed the Zhejiang provincial examinations; when the Yang clan proposed marriage he declined, citing the metropolitan examinations ahead.

sentences.zh: 留京師數年，病卒。

translations.literal: He remained in the capital several years and died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed in Beijing for several years and died of illness.

sentences.zh: 楊知母將為議婚他氏，請於母：「原得迎家勳喪，臨奠，然後聽母。」

translations.literal: Learning her mother planned to marry her to someone else, Yang asked, "Let me first receive Jiaxun's coffin and mourn before it; then I will obey you."
translations.idiomatic: Learning her mother planned to marry her to someone else, Yang asked, "Let me first receive Jiaxun's coffin and mourn before it; then I will obey you."

sentences.zh: 母許之。

translations.literal: Her mother consented.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother agreed.

sentences.zh: 楊迎喪於郊，奠竟，要母，遂歸李氏。

translations.literal: Yang welcomed the coffin at the outskirts; when the offerings were complete she pressed her mother and then returned to the Li clan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang met the coffin outside the city, completed the mourning rites, pressed her claim on her mother, and went to live with the Li family.

sentences.zh: 家勳父老而瞽，楊請於姑，為買妾生子。

translations.literal: Jiaxun's father was old and blind; Yang asked her mother-in-law to buy a concubine to bear a son.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaxun's father was old and blind; Yang asked her mother-in-law to take a concubine so the Li line could continue.

sentences.zh: 家勳父八十，目復明，德楊甚，命其子呼「嫂母」也。

translations.literal: When Jiaxun's father reached eighty his eyes recovered sight; he was deeply grateful to Yang and ordered his son to call her "elder-brother's mother."
translations.idiomatic: When Jiaxun's father turned eighty his sight returned; deeply grateful to Yang, he had his son address her as "Sister-Mother."

sentences.zh: 楊或曰徐氏。

translations.literal: Yang was also called the Xu clan woman.
translations.idiomatic: Yang was also known as a member of the Xu clan.

sentences.zh: 李家駒聘妻硃，高安人，大學士軾女。

translations.literal: Zhu, betrothed wife of Li Jiaju, was from Gao'an, daughter of Grand Secretary Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu, betrothed to Li Jiaju of Gao'an, was the daughter of Grand Secretary Shi.

sentences.zh: 家駒，乾隆三十六年舉人，早卒。

translations.literal: Jiaju, a juren in the thirty-sixth year of Qianlong, died early.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaju, who had passed the juren examinations in the thirty-sixth year of the Qianlong reign, died young.

sentences.zh: 硃事父母孝，性和以肅，自諸弟妹及內外臧獲，咸敬憚之。

translations.literal: Zhu was filial in serving her parents; her nature was gentle yet dignified; from younger siblings to inner and outer servants, all respected and feared her.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu was filial toward her parents, gentle yet dignified; siblings and servants alike respected and feared her.

sentences.zh: 生惡華採，寸金尺帛不以加身。

translations.literal: In life she detested finery; not an inch of gold or foot of silk would she allow on her person.
translations.idiomatic: She despised finery in life and would not wear even a scrap of silk or gold.

sentences.zh: 及聞家駒訃，欲奔喪，飲泣不食。

translations.literal: When she heard of Jiaju's death notice she wished to rush to the mourning, weeping as she drank and refusing food.
translations.idiomatic: When she heard of Jiaju's death she wanted to go mourn him and wept without eating.

sentences.zh: 時軾督學陝西，大母喻其意，誡當待父命，始復食。

translations.literal: At the time Shi was educational commissioner in Shaanxi; her grandmother understood her intent and admonished her to wait for her father's command before she resumed eating.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was then serving as educational commissioner in Shaanxi; her grandmother understood her grief and told her to wait for her father's permission before eating again.

sentences.zh: 軾還，越半載，乃以請，遂歸於李。

translations.literal: When Shi returned, after half a year she made her request and then returned to the Li clan.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi returned home half a year later she made her request and went to live with the Li family.

sentences.zh: 事祖姑及姑，如事父母。

translations.literal: She served her grandmother-in-law and mother-in-law as she would her parents.
translations.idiomatic: She cared for her grandmother-in-law and mother-in-law as devotedly as she would her own parents.

sentences.zh: 軾有父喪，聖祖命奪情視事，疏請終喪，戚友或尼之。

translations.literal: When Shi had a father's mourning the Sage Ancestor ordered him to leave mourning and resume office; he memorialized requesting to complete mourning; kin and friends sometimes obstructed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi's father died the Emperor ordered him to leave mourning and resume office; Shi petitioned to complete the full mourning period, and some kinsmen and friends tried to dissuade him.

sentences.zh: 硃泣曰：「吾父不得歸，雖官相國，年上壽，猶無與也。

translations.literal: Zhu wept and said, "If my father cannot return, even if he becomes chief minister and lives to great age, it is still of no use.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu wept and said, "If my father cannot return home to mourn, what good is it even if he becomes chief minister and lives to a great age?

sentences.zh: 彼姑息之愛何為者？

translations.literal: What is the use of that indulgent affection?
translations.idiomatic: What use is that misplaced indulgence?

sentences.zh: 聖主當鑑吾父之誠矣！」

translations.literal: Surely the Sage Emperor will see my father's sincerity!"
translations.idiomatic: Surely the Sage Emperor will see my father's sincerity!"

sentences.zh: 卒得請。

translations.literal: In the end his request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the end his request was granted.

sentences.zh: 鄰火且及，硃坐室中不肯出，曰：「死，吾分也！

translations.literal: A neighbor's fire was about to reach them; Zhu sat in her chamber and would not come out, saying, "Death is my allotted portion!
translations.idiomatic: When a neighbor's fire threatened the house, Zhu sat in her room and refused to leave, saying, "If I die, so be it!

sentences.zh: 宋共姬何人哉？」

translations.literal: Who was Gongji of Song?"
translations.idiomatic: Who was Gongji of Song?"

sentences.zh: 姑破扃挾以避。

translations.literal: Her mother-in-law broke the bolt and dragged her away to escape.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother-in-law broke down the door and pulled her to safety.

sentences.zh: 病不肯藥，兩弟來省，曰：「吾死無恨，但恨不得終事吾父及吾舅姑！」

translations.literal: When she fell ill she refused medicine; when her two younger brothers visited she said, "I have no regrets about dying, only that I could not serve my father and in-laws to the end!"
translations.idiomatic: When she fell ill she refused medicine; when her two younger brothers visited she said, "I have no regrets about dying, only that I could not serve my father and in-laws to the end!"

sentences.zh: 又曰：「我生惡華採，寸金尺帛不以加身，死毋負我！」

translations.literal: She also said, "I despised finery in life and wore no silk or gold—in death do not dress me in finery!"
translations.idiomatic: She also said, "I despised finery in life and wore no silk or gold—in death do not dress me in finery!"

sentences.zh: 遂卒。

translations.literal: She then died.
translations.idiomatic: Then she died.

sentences.zh: 賈汝愈聘妻盧，汝愈，故城人；

translations.literal: Lu, betrothed wife of Jia Ruyu; Ruyu was from Gucheng;
