translations.idiomatic: Lu was betrothed to Jia Ruyu, who came from Gucheng;

sentences.zh: 盧，德州人，協辦大學士廕溥女。

translations.literal: Lu was from Dezhou, daughter of Assistant Grand Secretary Yin Pu.
translations.idiomatic: Lu came from Dezhou and was the daughter of Assistant Grand Secretary Yin Pu.

sentences.zh: 汝愈卒，盧矢不嫁，賈氏迎以歸，為立後。

translations.literal: When Ruyu died Lu swore not to remarry; the Jia clan welcomed her home and established an heir.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruyu died Lu vowed never to remarry; the Jia family brought her home and arranged for an heir.

sentences.zh: 袁進舉聘妻某，天津梁進忠養女也。

translations.literal: A certain woman, betrothed wife of Yuan Jinju, was the adopted daughter of Liang Jinzhong of Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Jinju's betrothed was an adopted daughter of Liang Jinzhong of Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 進忠負薪行水次，有大舟泊焉，或抱女嬰出，授進忠曰：「此女生八月矣，父之官，卒於舟，母繼殞，其善視之！」

translations.literal: Jinzhong was carrying firewood along the riverbank when someone from a large moored boat handed him an infant girl, saying, "She is eight months old; her father died on the boat while traveling to his post, and her mother died as well—please care for her!"
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhong was carrying firewood along the riverbank when someone from a large moored boat handed him an infant girl, saying, "She is eight months old; her father died on the boat while traveling to his post, and her mother died as well—please care for her!"

sentences.zh: 進忠撫以為女。

translations.literal: Jinzhong raised her as his daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhong raised her as his own daughter.

sentences.zh: 而進忠有長女悍甚，女稍長，貌端好，長女將鬻以為人妾，女不可，長女益恚。

translations.literal: Jinzhong had an elder daughter who was extremely fierce; when the girl grew somewhat and her appearance was proper and fine, the elder daughter planned to sell her as someone's concubine; the girl would not agree and the elder daughter grew angrier.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhong had a fierce elder daughter; when the girl grew up comely, the elder daughter tried to sell her as a concubine; the girl refused and the elder daughter grew even angrier.

sentences.zh: 進舉故無藉，長女咻父母使字焉。

translations.literal: Jinju was originally without means; the elder daughter urged the parents to betroth her to him.
translations.idiomatic: Jinju was a man of no means; the elder daughter pressured her parents to betroth the girl to him.

sentences.zh: 進舉行不歸，又使告其母謀罷婚，女復不可。

translations.literal: Jinju traveled and did not return; she again had someone tell his mother to plot breaking the engagement; the girl again would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Jinju went away and never returned; the elder daughter also tried to have his mother break the engagement, but the girl refused again.

sentences.zh: 進忠病，瘍生於脛，女刲股以療，家人皆不知，而長女虐愈甚。

translations.literal: Jinzhong fell ill with a sore on his shin; the girl cut flesh from her thigh to treat him; the family all did not know, while the elder daughter's abuse grew ever worse.
translations.idiomatic: When Jinzhong developed a sore on his leg the girl cut flesh from her thigh to treat him without telling anyone, while the elder daughter's abuse grew worse.

sentences.zh: 進舉母憐之，迎之歸。

translations.literal: Jinju's mother pitied her and welcomed her home.
translations.idiomatic: Jinju's mother took pity on her and brought her to live in the Yuan household.

sentences.zh: 進忠及其長女皆死，女為​​營葬，迎義母進忠妻同居。

translations.literal: Jinzhong and his elder daughter both died; the girl arranged their burials and welcomed her foster mother Jinzhong's wife to live together.
translations.idiomatic: When Jinzhong and his elder daughter died, the girl arranged their funerals and brought her foster mother Jinzhong's wife to live with her.

sentences.zh: 長女有子，失所，召為鞠之。

translations.literal: The elder daughter had a son who was lost; she summoned him and raised him.
translations.idiomatic: The elder daughter's son, left orphaned, was taken in and raised by her.

sentences.zh: 為進舉弟娶婦，生子為進舉後。

translations.literal: She arranged a wife for Jinju's younger brother; when a son was born he became Jinju's heir.
translations.idiomatic: She found a wife for Jinju's younger brother, and when a son was born he became heir to Jinju's line.

sentences.zh: 終姑及其義母喪，女遂自經死。

translations.literal: After completing mourning for her mother-in-law and foster mother the girl hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: After completing mourning for her mother-in-law and foster mother she hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 有司葬之天津西郭外五烈墓傍。

translations.literal: The authorities buried her beside the Five Martyrs' Tomb outside the west gate of Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities buried her beside the Tomb of the Five Martyrs outside Tianjin's west gate.

sentences.zh: 五烈墓者，先為三婦墓，葬譚應宸妻陳、阮某妻諸、趙某妻裴，陳、諸皆以捍強暴死，裴以節終。

translations.literal: The Five Martyrs' Tomb was first a tomb for three women, burying Chen wife of Tan Yingchen, Zhu wife of a man surnamed Ruan, and Pei wife of a man surnamed Zhao—Chen and Zhu both died resisting violent men; Pei ended her life in chastity.
translations.idiomatic: The Tomb of the Five Martyrs began as a tomb for three women: Chen, wife of Tan Yingchen; Zhu, wife of a man surnamed Ruan; and Pei, wife of a man surnamed Zhao—Chen and Zhu died resisting assailants, and Pei lived out her life in chastity.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，金振妻丁殉夫，附葬，稱節烈四婦墓。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong Ding, wife of Jin Zhen, died with her husband and was buried attached to it, called the Tomb of Four Chaste and Martyred Women.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Qianlong reign, Ding, wife of Jin Zhen, died with her husband and was buried there as well; the site was called the Tomb of the Four Chaste Martyrs.

sentences.zh: 七年，又有殷氏女誤嫁倡家，為所迫，箠楚砲烙，沃以沸湯，死，葬墓側，稱五烈墓。

translations.literal: In the seventh year there was also a daughter of the Yin clan mistakenly married into a brothel family; forced by them, beaten, branded, and scalded with boiling water, she died and was buried beside the tomb, called the Five Martyrs' Tomb.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year a daughter of the Yin clan was mistakenly married into a brothel keeper's family; beaten, branded, and scalded with boiling water until she died, she was buried beside the tomb and the site was renamed the Tomb of the Five Martyrs.

sentences.zh: 五十六年，复葬女，更為六烈墓雲。

translations.literal: In the fifty-sixth year the girl was again buried there and it was renamed the Six Martyrs' Tomb.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-sixth year, when this girl was buried there as well, the site became the Tomb of the Six Martyrs.

sentences.zh: 李應宗聘妻李，昆明人。

translations.literal: Li, betrothed wife of Li Yingzong, was from Kunming.
translations.idiomatic: Li, betrothed to Li Yingzong, came from Kunming.

sentences.zh: 所居曰廟前舖大河埂，父春榮。

translations.literal: She lived at Dahegeng, Miaowanpu; her father was Chunrong.
translations.idiomatic: She lived at Dahegeng in Miaowanpu; her father was Chunrong.

sentences.zh: 未行，應宗卒。

translations.literal: Before the marriage ceremony Yingzong died.
translations.idiomatic: Before the wedding Yingzong died.

sentences.zh: 其明年，應宗大母語春榮，將改字女，女聞，遂縊。

translations.literal: The next year Yingzong's great-grandmother told Chunrong she would change the girl's betrothal; when the girl heard she hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Yingzong's great-grandmother told Chunrong she planned to betroth the girl elsewhere; hearing this, the girl hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 縊之夕，裂綾二尺許，刺血書九十四字。

translations.literal: On the night she hanged herself she tore off about two feet of silk and pricked blood to write ninety-four characters.
translations.idiomatic: On the night she died she tore off two feet of silk and wrote ninety-four characters in her own blood.

sentences.zh: 民家女未嘗讀書，字多訛易，嘉興錢儀吉為之句讀。

translations.literal: A commoner's daughter had never studied books; many characters were erroneous or altered; Qian Yiji of Jiaxing punctuated it for her.
translations.idiomatic: The girl had never been to school and many characters were misspelled; Qian Yiji of Jiaxing added punctuation to make it readable.

sentences.zh: 曰「呈天子前」，曰「忠孝節烈」，曰「二月初九日」，二月初九日蓋女死日，事在乾隆末。

translations.literal: It read "Present before the Son of Heaven," "Loyal, filial, chaste, and martyred," and "The ninth day of the second month"—the ninth day of the second month was the day the girl died; the affair was in late Qianlong.
translations.idiomatic: It read "To be presented before the Son of Heaven," "Loyal, filial, chaste, and martyred," and "The ninth day of the second month"—the date of her death; the event occurred in the late Qianlong years.

sentences.zh: 何其仁聘妻李，路南人。

translations.literal: Li, betrothed wife of He Qiren, was from Lunan.
translations.idiomatic: Li, betrothed to He Qiren, came from Lunan.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十一年，年十六，未行。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Jiaqing she was sixteen and had not yet married.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of the Jiaqing reign she was sixteen and not yet married.

sentences.zh: 其仁及其父皆病篤，李割股畀叔母使送婿家。

translations.literal: Qiren and his father were both gravely ill; Li cut flesh from her thigh and gave it to her aunt to have sent to her betrothed's home.
translations.idiomatic: When Qiren and his father both fell gravely ill, Li cut flesh from her thigh and had her aunt send it to her betrothed's family.

sentences.zh: 至，則其仁及其父皆已卒，其仁母燖以奠。

translations.literal: When it arrived, Qiren and his father had both died; Qiren's mother warmed it for offering.
translations.idiomatic: By the time it arrived Qiren and his father had both died; Qiren's mother warmed the flesh and offered it at the grave.

sentences.zh: 李欲奔喪，母尼之，遂縊。

translations.literal: Li wished to rush to the mourning; her mother obstructed her and she hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: Li wanted to go mourn them but her mother stopped her; she hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 王前洛聘妻林，潛山人。

translations.literal: Lin, betrothed wife of Wang Qianluo, was from Qianshan.
translations.idiomatic: Lin, betrothed to Wang Qianluo, came from Qianshan.

sentences.zh: 前洛病，林父餽藥，林潛刲股入藥。

translations.literal: When Qianluo was ill Lin's father sent medicine; Lin secretly cut flesh from her thigh and put it in the medicine.
translations.idiomatic: When Qianluo fell ill Lin's father sent medicine; Lin secretly cut flesh from her thigh and mixed it into the medicine.

sentences.zh: 前洛卒，固請奔喪，引刀誓不嫁。

translations.literal: When Qianluo died she firmly requested to rush to the mourning, drew a knife and swore not to remarry.
translations.idiomatic: When Qianluo died she begged to go mourn him, drew a knife, and swore never to marry another.

sentences.zh: 節義縣主，成郡王綿懃第七女，選文緯為婿。

translations.literal: The Princess of Jiayi County was the seventh daughter of Prince Cheng Mianqin; Wenwei was selected as son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Jiayi County was the seventh daughter of Prince Cheng Mianqin; Wenwei was chosen as her betrothed.

sentences.zh: 文緯，費莫氏，內閣學士英綬子。

translations.literal: Wenwei, of the Feimo clan, was son of Grand Secretariat Academician Yingshou.
translations.idiomatic: Wenwei of the Feimo clan was the son of Academician Yingshou of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 未婚，嘉慶十八年文緯卒，主時年十六，詣文緯家守節，仁宗詔封節義縣主。

translations.literal: Unmarried, in the eighteenth year of Jiaqing Wenwei died; the princess was then sixteen; she went to Wenwei's home to preserve chastity; Emperor Renzong issued an edict enfeoffing her as Princess of Jiayi County.
translations.idiomatic: Before the marriage, in the eighteenth year of the Jiaqing reign Wenwei died; the princess was sixteen; she went to Wenwei's home to live in chastity, and Emperor Renzong enfeoffed her as Princess of Jiayi County.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year she died.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the twenty-second year of the reign.

sentences.zh: 李承宗聘妻何，巢縣漁家女也。

translations.literal: He, betrothed wife of Li Chengzong, was a fisherman's daughter from Chaoxian.
translations.idiomatic: He, betrothed to Li Chengzong, was a fisherman's daughter from Chaoxian.

sentences.zh: 兩家居濱溪，相違半里餘，而李氏廬當上流。

translations.literal: Both families lived by Binxi, separated by a little over half a li, and the Li family's hut was upstream.
translations.idiomatic: Both families lived on Binxi Creek, a little over half a li apart, with the Li household upstream.

sentences.zh: 承宗卒，女年二十，請奔喪，父母不許。

translations.literal: When Chengzong died the girl was twenty; she requested to rush to the mourning; her parents did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzong died she was twenty; she begged to go mourn him but her parents refused.

sentences.zh: 不食四日，不死；

translations.literal: She did not eat for four days but did not die;
translations.idiomatic: She fasted for four days but did not die;

sentences.zh: 自經，或拯之。

translations.literal: she hanged herself and someone rescued her.
translations.idiomatic: she tried to hang herself but was rescued.

sentences.zh: 越日自沉於溪，求其屍不得。

translations.literal: The next day she drowned herself in the creek; her corpse could not be found.
translations.idiomatic: The next day she drowned herself in the creek and her body could not be found.

sentences.zh: 後三日，屍見溪上流，正值李氏門。

translations.literal: Three days later the corpse appeared upstream on the creek, directly at the Li family's door.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later her body appeared upstream, floating directly to the Li family's door.

sentences.zh: 江亨昭妻楊，侯官人，二氏皆漁家。

translations.literal: Yang, wife of Jiang Hengzhao, was from Houguan; both clans were fishing families.
translations.idiomatic: Yang, the wife of Jiang Hengzhao, came from Houguan; both families were fishermen.

sentences.zh: 楊未嫁，與亨昭舟相值，必引避。

translations.literal: Before marriage when Yang's boat and Hengzhao's boat met she always withdrew to avoid him.
translations.idiomatic: Before marriage, whenever their boats passed on the water she always turned aside to avoid him.

sentences.zh: 或遇水次，則自匿蘆葦中。

translations.literal: If they met at the water's edge she would hide herself among the reeds.
translations.idiomatic: If they met at the shore she hid herself in the reeds.

sentences.zh: 其母非之，女曰：「漁家獨不當有恥乎？」

translations.literal: Her mother disapproved; the girl said, "Do fishermen's daughters have no sense of shame?"
translations.idiomatic: Her mother disapproved; the girl said, "Do fishermen's daughters have no sense of shame?"

sentences.zh: 既嫁，強暴窺其有色，潛逼之，楊擠使墮水。

translations.literal: After marriage a violent man seeing her beauty secretly pressed upon her; Yang pushed him and made him fall into the water.
translations.idiomatic: After she married, a ruffian who lusted after her tried to force himself on her; Yang pushed him into the water.

sentences.zh: 亨昭死，殉焉。

translations.literal: When Hengzhao died she died with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Hengzhao died she followed him in death.

sentences.zh: 吳某聘妻硃，海鹽人。

translations.literal: Zhu, betrothed wife of a man surnamed Wu, was from Haiyan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu, betrothed to a man surnamed Wu, came from Haiyan.

sentences.zh: 吳某年十八，喪父母，遂出遊不歸。

translations.literal: Wu at eighteen lost his parents and then traveled away and did not return.
translations.idiomatic: Wu was eighteen when he lost both parents; he went traveling and never returned.

sentences.zh: 硃貧，父老，闢纑織屨。

translations.literal: Zhu was poor; her father was old; she spun hemp and wove sandals.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu was poor; her father was elderly; she spun hemp and wove sandals to support them.

sentences.zh: 其兄悍，屢辱之。

translations.literal: Her elder brother was fierce and repeatedly humiliated her.
translations.idiomatic: Her elder brother was violent and often humiliated her.

sentences.zh: 硃曰：「兄貧不能食我父，我父衰，無所營，不得不就兄食。

translations.literal: Zhu said, "My brother is poor and cannot feed my father; my father is aged and has no means of support—we cannot but depend on my brother for food.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu said, "My brother is too poor to support our father; Father is old and has no other means—I must stay and help my brother feed him.

sentences.zh: 我留，乃助兄耳。」

translations.literal: By staying I am only helping my brother."
translations.idiomatic: By staying I am only helping my brother."

sentences.zh: 及父死，硃年五十八，吳不知其存亡，吳之族愍硃節，迎以歸，為立後。

translations.literal: When her father died Zhu was fifty-eight; Wu did not know whether she lived or died; Wu's clan pitied Zhu's chastity, welcomed her home, and established an heir.
translations.idiomatic: When her father died Zhu was fifty-eight; Wu, unaware whether she was alive or dead, had long since vanished—but the Wu clan honored her virtue, brought her home, and established an heir for the line.

sentences.zh: 徐文經聘妻姚，名淑金，侯官人。

translations.literal: Yao, betrothed wife of Xu Wenjing, named Shujin, was from Houguan.
translations.idiomatic: Yao, betrothed to Xu Wenjing—her given name was Shujin—came from Houguan.

sentences.zh: 文經卒，淑金屢求死，乃歸於徐。

translations.literal: When Wenjing died Shujin repeatedly sought death; she then returned to the Xu clan.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenjing died Shujin repeatedly tried to kill herself; she then went to live with the Xu family.

sentences.zh: 貧，舅歿，姑疾作，刲股以療。

translations.literal: Poor, when her uncle-in-law died and her mother-in-law fell ill she cut flesh from her thigh to treat her.
translations.idiomatic: Though poor, when her uncle-in-law died and her mother-in-law fell ill she cut flesh from her thigh to treat her.

sentences.zh: 姚掇芹供姑，自食其棄莖。

translations.literal: Yao picked celery to serve her mother-in-law and herself ate the discarded stems.
translations.idiomatic: Yao picked celery for her mother-in-law and ate the discarded stems herself.

sentences.zh: 無何，姑亦歿，嗣子以貧去。

translations.literal: Before long her mother-in-law also died; the heir because of poverty departed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long her mother-in-law died as well; the heir left because of poverty.

sentences.zh: 淑金目昏，不能治女紅，以缽為釜，以草為衾。

translations.literal: Shujin's eyes were dim and she could not do needlework; she used a bowl as a cooking pot and grass as a quilt.
translations.idiomatic: Shujin's eyesight failed and she could no longer sew; she cooked in a bowl and slept under grass for a blanket.

sentences.zh: 僦屋不償值，見逐，泣路隅。

translations.literal: She rented a house but could not pay; she was driven out and wept at the roadside.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to pay her rent she was evicted and wept by the roadside.

sentences.zh: 有負擔者，憐而周之，里人醵金助衣食，僅得不死。

translations.literal: A porter pitied her and gave her relief; neighbors collected money to help with food and clothing, and she barely avoided death.
translations.idiomatic: A porter took pity on her and gave her aid; neighbors pooled money for food and clothing, and she barely survived.

sentences.zh: 猶朝夕拜徐氏祏，祝其嗣子歸也。

translations.literal: Still morning and evening she bowed before the Xu clan spirit tablet, praying the heir would return.
translations.idiomatic: Morning and evening she still bowed before the Xu ancestral tablet, praying the heir would return.

sentences.zh: 居十餘年乃卒。

translations.literal: She lived more than ten years and then died.
translations.idiomatic: She lived on this way for more than ten years before she died.

sentences.zh: 李煜聘妻蕭，秀水人。

translations.literal: Xiao, betrothed wife of Li Yu, was from Xiushui.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao, betrothed to Li Yu, came from Xiushui.

sentences.zh: 煜酒家子，居郭南萬螺濱。

translations.literal: Yu was a wine-shop keeper's son who lived at Wanluobin south of the city wall.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was the son of a wine-shop keeper and lived at Wanluobin, just south of the city wall.

sentences.zh: 蕭未行，煜死。

translations.literal: Before Xiao had married Yu died.
translations.idiomatic: Before the wedding Yu died.

sentences.zh: 蕭無母，請於父，原歸李，翁姑遣媒止之，勿聽，遂歸李。

translations.literal: Xiao had no mother; she asked her father, wishing to return to the Li clan; her parents-in-law sent a matchmaker to stop her but she would not listen and returned to the Li clan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao's mother was dead; she begged her father to let her go to the Li household; her future in-laws sent a matchmaker to dissuade her, but she refused and went to the Li family.

sentences.zh: 視煜斂，即奉侍姑，執爨濯衣甚謹。

translations.literal: After attending to Yu's encoffining she at once served her mother-in-law, cooking and washing clothes very carefully.
translations.idiomatic: After seeing to Yu's burial she immediately began serving her mother-in-law, cooking and washing clothes with great care.

sentences.zh: 姑悍，既不欲李來，又見其貧也，晝夜詈，李唯唯無一言，鄰勿善也。

translations.literal: The mother-in-law was fierce; she neither wanted Li to come nor saw her poverty; day and night she reviled her; Li only assented without a word; neighbors disapproved.
translations.idiomatic: The mother-in-law was harsh; she had not wanted Li to come and despised her poverty; she reviled her day and night while Li endured in silence; the neighbors disapproved.

sentences.zh: 或勸姑，姑亦詈焉。

translations.literal: Some tried to persuade the mother-in-law but she reviled them as well.
translations.idiomatic: When neighbors tried to reason with the mother-in-law she reviled them too.

sentences.zh: 士大夫眾至，誡翁：「毋虐貞女，貞女光爾門，宜善視之！」

translations.literal: Scholar-officials gathered and admonished the old man, "Do not mistreat this chaste woman—she brings honor to your family; you should treat her well!"
translations.idiomatic: Scholar-officials gathered and admonished the old man, "Do not mistreat this chaste woman—she brings honor to your family; you should treat her well!"

sentences.zh: 姑終不欲李同居，眾乃於室後闢小樓居貞女，醵金以佽之。

translations.literal: The mother-in-law ultimately did not want Li to live together with her; the crowd then opened a small upper chamber behind the house for the chaste woman and collected money to support her.
translations.idiomatic: The mother-in-law still refused to let Li live with her, so the community built a small room behind the house for the chaste woman and pooled money to support her.

sentences.zh: 劉戊兒聘妻王，名孝，武陟人。

translations.literal: Wang, betrothed wife of Liu Wu'er, named Xiao, was from Wuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang, betrothed to Liu Wu'er—her given name was Xiao—came from Wuzhi.

sentences.zh: 未嫁，歲大無，戊兒行六年不歸。

translations.literal: Before marriage there was a great famine; Wu'er traveled six years and did not return.
translations.idiomatic: Before she married, during a great famine, Wu'er went away and did not return for six years.

sentences.zh: 父母欲別嫁，孝間出，如劉氏。

translations.literal: Her parents wished to betroth her elsewhere; Xiao slipped out and went to the Liu clan.
translations.idiomatic: When her parents wanted to marry her to someone else, Xiao slipped away and went to the Liu household.

sentences.zh: 值老嫗，問劉戊兒母，嫗曰：「我即戊兒母也。」

translations.literal: She met an old woman and asked for Liu Wu'er's mother; the woman said, "I am Wu'er's mother."
translations.idiomatic: She met an old woman and asked for Liu Wu'er's mother; the woman said, "I am Wu'er's mother."

sentences.zh: 孝拜且泣曰：「我王氏女，姑之子婦也！」

translations.literal: Xiao bowed and wept, saying, "I am a Wang daughter—I am your son's wife!"
translations.idiomatic: Xiao bowed and wept, saying, "I am a Wang daughter—I am your son's wife!"

sentences.zh: 嫗驚未信，孝探懷出物示嫗曰：「此非姑家聘物耶？

translations.literal: The old woman was startled and did not believe; Xiao reached into her bosom and produced an object to show the old woman, saying, "Is this not my mother-in-law's betrothal gift?
translations.idiomatic: The old woman was astonished and did not believe her; Xiao drew something from her bosom and said, "Is this not your family's betrothal gift?

sentences.zh: 吾竊持以來為信。」

translations.literal: I stole away with it as proof."
translations.idiomatic: I stole away with it as proof."

sentences.zh: 嫗視之亦泣，復以貧無食辭。

translations.literal: The old woman looked and also wept, again declining because of poverty and lack of food.
translations.idiomatic: The old woman looked and wept as well, but still refused, saying they were too poor to feed her.

sentences.zh: 曰：「吾夙知姑貧，翁歿，兩叔幼，安得所食？

translations.literal: Xiao said, "I have long known my mother-in-law is poor; when my father-in-law died the two younger uncles were young—where could food come from?
translations.idiomatic: Xiao said, "I have always known you were poor; when your husband died your two young sons-in-law had nothing to eat—

sentences.zh: 我能女紅，茲固為養姑來也。

translations.literal: I can do needlework—I came precisely to support my mother-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: I can sew and spin—that is why I came, to support you.

sentences.zh: 生未嘗一時離吾母，計無所出而後來。」

translations.literal: I have never been away from my mother until now; I came only because I could find no other way."
translations.idiomatic: I have never been away from my mother until now; I came only because I could find no other way."

sentences.zh: 因复泣曰：「如不見容，我無歸理，惟赴水死耳！」

translations.literal: She wept again and said, "If you will not take me in I have nowhere to go—I will throw myself into the water!"
translations.idiomatic: She wept again and said, "If you will not take me in I have nowhere to go—I will throw myself into the water!"

sentences.zh: 嫗告孝父母許焉。

translations.literal: The old woman told Xiao's parents and they consented.
translations.idiomatic: The old woman sent word to Xiao's parents and they agreed.

sentences.zh: 孝勤紡績，夜磨作蒸餅，使叔鬻之。

translations.literal: Xiao diligently spun; at night she ground flour and made steamed cakes for her uncles to sell.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao spun diligently and at night made steamed cakes for her brothers-in-law to sell.

sentences.zh: 姑病，日夜侍。

translations.literal: When her mother-in-law fell ill she attended day and night.
translations.idiomatic: When her mother-in-law fell ill she nursed her day and night.

sentences.zh: 居數年，鄉里感其義，率錢周其姑。

translations.literal: After several years the village was moved by her righteousness and collected money to relieve her mother-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: After several years the neighbors, moved by her devotion, pooled money to help her mother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 葺舊屋，為叔娶婦生子。

translations.literal: They repaired the old house and arranged wives for the uncles who bore sons.
translations.idiomatic: They repaired the old house and saw the brothers-in-law married and with sons.

sentences.zh: 姑卒，合葬於舅墓，乃授家事於叔，夜入室，扃戶，寂無聲。

translations.literal: When her mother-in-law died she was buried together with her father-in-law's grave; she then entrusted household affairs to her uncle, entered her room at night, bolted the door, and all was silent.
translations.idiomatic: When her mother-in-law died she was buried beside her father-in-law; Xiao turned the household over to her brother-in-law, went to her room at night, bolted the door, and all was silent.

sentences.zh: 翌晨叩戶不應，毀牖入，則自經死，衣履皆易新制者。

translations.literal: The next morning knocking brought no answer; they broke the window and entered—she had hanged herself, her clothes and shoes all newly made.
translations.idiomatic: The next morning no one answered the door; they broke in and found her hanged, dressed in newly made clothes and shoes.

sentences.zh: 時嘉慶九年二月乙酉。

translations.literal: This was on the yiyou day of the second month of the ninth year of Jiaqing.
translations.idiomatic: This was on the yiyou day of the second month of the ninth year of the Jiaqing reign.

sentences.zh: 孝年二十四至劉氏，事姑十二年，姑死乃死。

translations.literal: Xiao was twenty-four when she came to the Liu clan; she served her mother-in-law twelve years and died only after her mother-in-law died.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao was twenty-four when she joined the Liu household; she served her mother-in-law for twelve years and died only after her death.

sentences.zh: 硃某聘妻李，字容，東安人。

translations.literal: Li, betrothed wife of a man surnamed Zhu, style name Rong, was from Dong'an.
translations.idiomatic: Li, betrothed to a man surnamed Zhu—her style name was Rong—came from Dong'an.

sentences.zh: 父大純，幼字硃氏。

translations.literal: Her father was Dachun; in youth she was betrothed to the Zhu clan.
translations.idiomatic: Her father was Dachun; she had been betrothed to the Zhu clan since childhood.

sentences.zh: 硃氏子遠遊十餘年不歸，或傳已死。

translations.literal: The Zhu clan son traveled far more than ten years and did not return; some reported he had died.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhu son had been away traveling for more than ten years; some said he was dead.

sentences.zh: 女既喪父母，無昆弟，獨與其婢春華居，誓不嫁。

translations.literal: The girl having lost her parents and having no brothers lived alone with her maid Chunhua and swore not to remarry.
translations.idiomatic: After her parents died she had no brothers and lived alone with her maid Chunhua, vowing never to marry.

sentences.zh: 春華稍長，其父謀嫁之，春華義不去，容亦誓不嫁。

translations.literal: When Chunhua grew somewhat her father planned to marry her off; Chunhua out of righteousness would not leave; Rong also swore not to remarry.
translations.idiomatic: When Chunhua grew up her father wanted to marry her off; Chunhua refused to leave Rong's side, and Rong vowed never to marry either.

sentences.zh: 其父不聽，春華乃告容，俱赴水死。

translations.literal: Her father would not listen; Chunhua then told Rong and both went to the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: When her father refused to listen, Chunhua told Rong and together they drowned themselves.

sentences.zh: 武稌聘妻李，伊陽人。

translations.literal: Li, betrothed wife of Wu Ren, was from Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li, betrothed to Wu Ren, came from Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 年十一，喪母，育於武。

translations.literal: At eleven she lost her mother and was raised in the Wu household.
translations.idiomatic: She lost her mother at eleven and was raised in the Wu household.

sentences.zh: 從娣婦事舅姑謹，姑羸臥，調醫藥，治家事日勤。

translations.literal: Following her sister-in-law she served her parents-in-law carefully; when her mother-in-law lay weak in bed she prepared medicines and managed household affairs daily with diligence.
translations.idiomatic: Like her sister-in-law she dutifully cared for her in-laws; when her mother-in-law fell bedridden she prepared medicines and managed the household with tireless devotion.

sentences.zh: 姑卒，撫叔弟及二女妹。

translations.literal: When her mother-in-law died she raised her younger uncle-in-law and two younger sisters-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: When her mother-in-law died she raised her husband's younger brother and two younger sisters-in-law.

sentences.zh: 年十七，猶未婚。

translations.literal: At seventeen she was still unmarried.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen she was still unmarried.

sentences.zh: 稌墮井死，誓從井，舅止之，幼弟妹環而哭，李大慟。

translations.literal: When Ren fell into a well and died she swore to follow into the well; her father-in-law stopped her; young brothers- and sisters-in-law surrounded her weeping; Li grieved greatly.
translations.idiomatic: When Ren fell into a well and died she vowed to follow him; her father-in-law stopped her as her young brothers- and sisters-in-law wept around her.

sentences.zh: 遂總發為紒，曰：「吾當終婦事。」

translations.literal: She bound her hair as a married woman and said, "I will fulfill a wife's duties to the end."
translations.idiomatic: She bound her hair as a married woman and said, "I will fulfill a wife's duties to the end."

sentences.zh: 請於舅，立後，紡織以佐家。

translations.literal: She asked her father-in-law to establish an heir and spun and wove to help the household.
translations.idiomatic: She asked her father-in-law to arrange an heir and supported the family by spinning and weaving.

sentences.zh: 舅娶後姑，又有疾，調醫藥，治家事如前時。

translations.literal: Her father-in-law took a second wife who also fell ill; she prepared medicines and managed household affairs as before.
translations.idiomatic: When her father-in-law remarried and his new wife also fell ill, she cared for her and managed the household as before.

sentences.zh: 久之，叔弟補縣學生，兩女妹皆嫁。

translations.literal: After a long time her younger uncle-in-law became a county school student and both younger sisters-in-law were married.
translations.idiomatic: In time her brother-in-law passed the county examinations and both sisters-in-law were married.

sentences.zh: 又數年，為所後子娶婦，則語其兄曰：「妹曩不即死，誠不敢死也。

translations.literal: Several years later when an heir's son took a wife she then told her elder brother, "Your younger sister did not die at once earlier—I truly did not dare to die.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later, when the heir took a wife, she told her brother, "I did not die with Ren at once—I truly did not dare to die then.

sentences.zh: 今吾家奉舅姑宗祏幸有人，井中人待我久，我將從之！」

translations.literal: Now the family has someone to tend the ancestors; the man in the well has waited long enough—I will join him!"
translations.idiomatic: Now the family has someone to tend the ancestors; the man in the well has waited long enough—I will join him!"

sentences.zh: 晨起，從容問姑安，出行汲，自投稌所墮井死。

translations.literal: In the morning she calmly asked after her mother-in-law's wellbeing, went out to draw water, and threw herself into the well where Ren had fallen and died.
translations.idiomatic: That morning she calmly asked after her mother-in-law, went out to draw water, and threw herself into the well where Ren had died.

sentences.zh: 道光二十一年八月壬寅，稌生日也。

translations.literal: This was on the renyin day of the eighth month of the twenty-first year of Daoguang—Ren's birthday.
translations.idiomatic: This was on the renyin day of the eighth month of the twenty-first year of the Daoguang reign—Ren's birthday.

sentences.zh: 後稌死二十有一年。

translations.literal: This was twenty-one years after Ren's death.
translations.idiomatic: This was twenty-one years after Ren's death.

sentences.zh: 陳霞池聘妻錢，桐城人，居東鄉。

translations.literal: Qian, betrothed wife of Chen Xiachi, was from Tongcheng and lived in the eastern district.
translations.idiomatic: Qian, betrothed to Chen Xiachi, came from Tongcheng and lived in the eastern part of the county.

sentences.zh: 未行而霞池卒，錢請奔喪。

translations.literal: Before the marriage ceremony Xiachi died; Qian requested to rush to the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Before the wedding Xiachi died; Qian asked to go mourn him.

sentences.zh: 東鄉俗以為子死婦奔喪，於家兇，辭之。

translations.literal: Eastern district custom held that when a son died and the woman rushed to mourning it brought misfortune to the family; they declined.
translations.idiomatic: Local custom held that a betrothed woman mourning at the home of a dead fiancé brought bad luck to the family, and they refused.

sentences.zh: 錢毀容矢不嫁。

translations.literal: Qian disfigured her appearance and swore not to remarry.
translations.idiomatic: Qian marred her appearance and vowed never to marry.

sentences.zh: 久之，陳氏之族迎以歸，為立後。

translations.literal: After a long time the Chen clan welcomed her home and established an heir.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually the Chen clan brought her home and arranged for an heir.

sentences.zh: 居數十年，縣有士人往存問，為言：「朝廷旌貞女，與節烈並重，當請於有司。」

translations.literal: After decades a local scholar visited her and said, "The court honors chaste women as highly as chaste martyrs—you should petition the authorities for commendation."
translations.idiomatic: After decades a local scholar visited her and said, "The court honors chaste women as highly as chaste martyrs—you should petition the authorities for commendation."

sentences.zh: 錢聞大驚，蓋初不知其行應旌也。

translations.literal: When Qian heard she was greatly startled—for at first she had not known her conduct merited commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Qian was astonished—she had never imagined her conduct might deserve official recognition.

sentences.zh: 汪榮泰聘妻唐，名鳳鸞。

translations.literal: Tang, betrothed wife of Wang Rongtai, named Fengluan.
translations.idiomatic: Tang, betrothed to Wang Rongtai—her given name was Fengluan.

sentences.zh: 榮泰，歙人；

translations.literal: Rongtai was from She;
translations.idiomatic: Rongtai came from She;

sentences.zh: 唐，淳安人。

translations.literal: Tang was from Chun'an.
translations.idiomatic: Tang came from Chun'an.

sentences.zh: 父以許榮泰，未聘而父卒，母更許他姓。

translations.literal: Her father had promised her to Rongtai; before the betrothal ceremony her father died and her mother betrothed her to another clan.
translations.idiomatic: Her father had promised her to Rongtai; before the formal betrothal her father died and her mother arranged a new match.

sentences.zh: 他姓來聘，唐自所居樓裂所製衣履擲於庭，俄砉然躍而出，遂墮地死。

translations.literal: When the other clan came to betroth her Tang from the upper chamber of her dwelling tore the clothes and shoes she had made and threw them into the courtyard; suddenly with a crack she leaped out and fell to the ground dead.
translations.idiomatic: When the new suitor's party arrived, Tang tore up the clothes and shoes she had made and threw them into the courtyard; then she leaped from her upper room and fell dead.

sentences.zh: 榮泰請迎喪，母不許；

translations.literal: Rongtai requested to welcome the coffin; her mother did not permit it;
translations.idiomatic: Rongtai asked to bring her body home for burial; her mother refused;

sentences.zh: 母卒，乃迎喪以歸。

translations.literal: when her mother died he then welcomed the coffin home.
translations.idiomatic: only after her mother died did he bring her coffin home.

sentences.zh: 季斌敏聘妻藺，斌敏，正藍旗漢軍；

translations.literal: Lin, betrothed wife of Ji Binmin; Binmin was of the Bordered Blue Banner Han Chinese Eight Banners;
translations.idiomatic: Lin was betrothed to Ji Binmin of the Bordered Blue Banner Han Chinese Eight Banners;

sentences.zh: 藺，滄州人。

translations.literal: Lin was from Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lin came from Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 斌敏未婚卒，藺年十八，矢不嫁。

translations.literal: Binmin died unmarried; Lin was eighteen and swore not to remarry.
translations.idiomatic: Binmin died before the wedding; Lin was eighteen and vowed never to marry.

sentences.zh: 居二年，聞有媒妁至，截右耳，逾三日，又截左耳。

translations.literal: After two years when she heard matchmakers had come she cut off her right ear; after three days she cut off her left ear as well.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later, when matchmakers came, she cut off her right ear; three days later she cut off her left ear as well.

sentences.zh: 其父春以告季氏，迎以歸。

translations.literal: Her father Chun reported this to the Ji clan and they welcomed her home.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Chun told the Ji clan, and they brought her to live with them.

sentences.zh: 女事姑甚孝，為夫補行喪服。

translations.literal: The girl served her mother-in-law very filially and completed mourning garb on her husband's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: She served her mother-in-law devotedly and observed mourning for her husband.

sentences.zh: 喪終，歸訣父母，謂當死從夫，父母力勸喻之。

translations.literal: When mourning ended she returned to bid farewell to her parents, saying she ought to die and follow her husband; her parents strongly urged and reasoned with her.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended she went to bid farewell to her parents, saying she would follow her husband in death; her parents tried hard to dissuade her.

sentences.zh: 女復還，見姑，言笑如平時，即夕飲毒死。

translations.literal: The girl returned again, saw her mother-in-law, spoke and laughed as in normal times, and that very evening drank poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: She returned to her mother-in-law's home, chatted and laughed as usual, and that evening drank poison and died.

sentences.zh: 啟篋封所割兩耳，識曰「全歸」。

translations.literal: Opening a casket they found sealed the two ears she had cut off, marked with the words "Complete Return."
translations.idiomatic: In a casket they found the two ears she had cut off, sealed and marked "Complete Return."

sentences.zh: 董福慶聘妻馮，福慶，固安駐防漢軍；

translations.literal: Feng, betrothed wife of Dong Fuqing; Fuqing was a Han Chinese Banner guardsman stationed at Gu'an;
translations.idiomatic: Feng was betrothed to Dong Fuqing, a Han Chinese Banner guardsman stationed at Gu'an;

sentences.zh: 馮，霸州人也。

translations.literal: Feng was from Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Feng came from Bazhou.

sentences.zh: 福慶貧，餓猶耕，死於田。

translations.literal: Fuqing was poor; though starving he still farmed and died in the fields.
translations.idiomatic: Fuqing was so poor that though starving he still worked the fields, and died there.

sentences.zh: 女年二十，請奔喪，福慶父往沮之，曰：「子餓至死，复忍餓汝家女耶？」

translations.literal: She was twenty and asked to go mourn him; Fuqing's father tried to stop her, saying, "My son starved to death—how can I let your family's daughter starve as well?"
translations.idiomatic: She was twenty and asked to go mourn him; Fuqing's father tried to stop her, saying, "My son starved to death—how can I let your family's daughter starve as well?"

sentences.zh: 女出拜，伏地哭不起，福慶父乃諾之，遂奔喪。

translations.literal: The girl came out to bow, prostrated herself weeping and would not rise; Fuqing's father then consented and she rushed to the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: She came out to bow, prostrated herself and wept until Fuqing's father consented, and she went to mourn.

sentences.zh: 執婦禮以終，寒餒皆無懟。

translations.literal: She performed a wife's rites to the end; through cold and hunger she never complained.
translations.idiomatic: She fulfilled a wife's duties to the end, enduring cold and hunger without a word of complaint.

sentences.zh: 喬湧濤聘妻方，桐城人。

translations.literal: Fang, betrothed wife of Qiao Yongtao, was from Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Fang, betrothed to Qiao Yongtao, came from Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 湧濤卒，湧濤母丁亦病，方請於父母，歸於喬。

translations.literal: When Yongtao died his mother Ding also fell ill; Fang asked her parents and returned to the Qiao clan.
translations.idiomatic: When Yongtao died and his mother Ding also fell ill, Fang asked her parents' permission and went to the Qiao household.

sentences.zh: 以姑病寒疾，亦薄其衣當風雪。

translations.literal: Because her mother-in-law had a cold illness she also wore thin clothing against wind and snow.
translations.idiomatic: Because her mother-in-law suffered from a cold illness she too wore thin clothes even in wind and snow.

sentences.zh: 刲股以進姑，病良已。

translations.literal: She cut flesh from her thigh to present to her mother-in-law and the illness soon recovered.
translations.idiomatic: She cut flesh from her thigh for her mother-in-law, and the illness soon passed.

sentences.zh: 乃營葬湧濤，以衣負土，三日不食。

translations.literal: She then arranged Yongtao's burial, carrying earth in her garment, and did not eat for three days.
translations.idiomatic: She arranged Yongtao's burial, carrying earth in the hem of her garment, and fasted for three days.

sentences.zh: 為湧濤立後，淡食布衣，深自刻苦。

translations.literal: She established an heir for Yongtao, ate plain food and wore coarse cloth, and deeply disciplined herself.
translations.idiomatic: She arranged an heir for Yongtao's line, ate plain food, wore coarse cloth, and lived in strict austerity.

sentences.zh: 病將革，戒子婦毋以寸絲斂。

translations.literal: When her illness was about to turn critical she admonished her daughter-in-law not to encoffin her with even an inch of silk.
translations.idiomatic: On her deathbed she told her daughter-in-law not to bury her in even a thread of silk.

sentences.zh: 張氏女，名有，鄒平人。

translations.literal: A daughter of the Zhang clan, named You, was from Zouping.
translations.idiomatic: A girl surnamed Zhang, given name You, came from Zouping.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，鬻為高唐硃氏婢。

translations.literal: In a year of famine she was sold as a maid to the Zhu clan of Gaotang.
translations.idiomatic: During a famine year she was sold as a maid to the Zhu family of Gaotang.

sentences.zh: 及長，主母為議婚，有泣言幼已字人，不敢負。

translations.literal: When grown the mistress arranged a marriage; You wept and said that from youth she had been betrothed and dared not fail that pledge.
translations.idiomatic: When she grew up her mistress wanted to arrange a marriage; You wept and said she had been betrothed since childhood and could not break her pledge.

sentences.zh: 主母使求得所許字者，則已別娶有子女矣。

translations.literal: The mistress had someone seek out the man to whom she had been betrothed—he had already married another and had children.
translations.idiomatic: Her mistress tracked down her betrothed—he had already married someone else and had children.

sentences.zh: 以語有，有曰：「雖別娶，身不原更事他人。」

translations.literal: When told this, You said, "Even though he married another, I will not belong to anyone else."
translations.idiomatic: When told this, You said, "Even though he married another, I will not belong to anyone else."

sentences.zh: 主母憐而聽之。

translations.literal: The mistress pitied her and consented.
translations.idiomatic: Her mistress took pity on her and agreed.

sentences.zh: 有終不別字以死。

translations.literal: She ended her life without changing her betrothal.
translations.idiomatic: She died rather than accept another betrothal.

sentences.zh: 粉姐，失其姓，高郵人。

translations.literal: Sister Fen—her surname is lost—was from Gaoyou.
translations.idiomatic: Sister Fen, whose surname is unknown, came from Gaoyou.

sentences.zh: 父為迮氏蒼頭，字某氏子。

translations.literal: Her father was a bondservant of the Ze clan; she was betrothed to a son of a certain clan.
translations.idiomatic: Her father was a bondservant of the Ze clan; she had been betrothed to a son of another family.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，某氏子行乞，轉徙十餘年。

translations.literal: In a year of famine the son of the certain clan went begging and wandered more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: During a famine the betrothed went begging and wandered for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 女父遇之江都市上，某氏子曰：「我終不能娶，還我聘錢，聽別嫁。」

translations.literal: Her father met him in the Jiangdu market; the betrothed said, "I can never marry her—return the betrothal gift and let her marry someone else."
translations.idiomatic: Her father met him in the Jiangdu market; the betrothed said, "I can never marry her—return the betrothal gift and let her marry someone else."

sentences.zh: 女父喜，還聘錢，與析券。

translations.literal: The girl's father was pleased, returned the betrothal money, and gave him a written release.
translations.idiomatic: Her father gladly returned the betrothal money and gave him a written release.

sentences.zh: 歸告女，女嗚咽不語，夜自經。

translations.literal: Returning he told the girl; she sobbed without speaking and hanged herself that night.
translations.idiomatic: When he told her she sobbed in silence and hanged herself that night.

sentences.zh: 闞氏女，名玉，浙江仁和人。

translations.literal: A daughter of the Kan clan, named Yu, was from Renhe in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, a daughter of the Kan clan, came from Renhe in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 玉端麗，能詩文。

translations.literal: Yu was graceful and beautiful and could compose poetry and prose.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was graceful and beautiful and wrote poetry and prose.

sentences.zh: 父亡，與母及兄嫂居。

translations.literal: When her father died she lived with her mother and elder brother and sister-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: After her father died she lived with her mother, elder brother, and sister-in-law.

sentences.zh: 年十三，福王由崧帝南京，選民間女子，玉母匿諸賣菜傭家。

translations.literal: At thirteen the Prince of Fu, Zhu Yousong, became emperor at Nanjing and selected girls from among the people; Yu's mother hid her with a vegetable-selling laborer's family.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen, when the Prince of Fu Zhu Yousong became emperor at Nanjing and began selecting girls from the populace, Yu's mother hid her with a vegetable peddler's family.

sentences.zh: 玉父亡時，留百金畀玉兄備玉嫁，玉兄盪其貲，遂與傭謀字傭子。

translations.literal: When Yu's father died he left a hundred taels of gold for Yu's elder brother to prepare Yu's marriage; Yu's elder brother squandered the funds and then plotted with the laborer to betroth Yu to the laborer's son.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu's father died he had left a hundred taels for her dowry; her brother squandered it and conspired with the peddler to betroth her to the peddler's son.

sentences.zh: 玉在傭家尚待年，號泣求還，不可得，疾作，始遣歸。

translations.literal: Yu at the laborer's home was still awaiting the proper age; she wailed and begged to return but could not; when illness set in she was at last sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was still living at the peddler's home awaiting marriageable age; she wept and begged to come home but was refused; only when she fell ill was she sent back.

sentences.zh: 玉垂絕，語其母曰：「兒今且死，原埋父棺側，不作傭家鬼也。」

translations.literal: On her deathbed Yu told her mother, "I am dying now; bury me beside Father's coffin—I will not be a ghost in that peddler's household."
translations.idiomatic: On her deathbed Yu told her mother, "I am dying now; bury me beside Father's coffin—I will not be a ghost in that peddler's household."

sentences.zh: 复嚼齒曰：「兄陷我！」

translations.literal: She ground her teeth and said, "My brother ruined me!"
translations.idiomatic: She ground her teeth and said, "My brother ruined me!"

sentences.zh: 遂卒。

translations.literal: She then died.
translations.idiomatic: Then she died.

sentences.zh: 玉嘗作怨歌，好事者以琴譜其聲，曰闞玉操，辭曰：「父生我兮中道逝，母煢煢兮門衰瘁。

translations.literal: Yu once composed a song of grievance; enthusiasts set its melody to the qin, calling it the Kan Yu Melody; the words read, "Father bore me and midway departed; Mother stands alone and the gate declines in decay.
translations.idiomatic: Yu once composed a lament; enthusiasts set it to music for the qin and called it the Kan Yu Melody. It begins: "Father brought me into the world, then died midway; Mother stands alone, our house in ruin.

sentences.zh: 兄嫂難與居，抉我如目中之塵沙。

translations.literal: Elder brother and sister-in-law are hard to live with—they pluck me out like dust and sand in the eye.
translations.idiomatic: Brother and sister-in-law are unbearable—they cast me out like grit in the eye.

sentences.zh: 伊又遘此佻巧兮，胡迋我之實多。

translations.literal: He again encounters this frivolous trickster—why does he wrong me so greatly?
translations.idiomatic: That frivolous schemer has come again—why does he wrong me so deeply?

sentences.zh: 彼六禮之已愆兮，曾貞女之貺從。

translations.literal: Those six rites already violated—could a chaste woman ever follow such a gift?
translations.idiomatic: The six rites of marriage already broken—how could a chaste woman accept such a match?

sentences.zh: 矧要予以桑中兮，夫豈其為予之匹雙。

translations.literal: How much less summon me to the mulberry grove—could he ever be my proper mate?
translations.idiomatic: Much less summon me to a secret tryst in the mulberry grove—he could never be my true match.

sentences.zh: 我有母兮，癙思泣血。

translations.literal: I have a mother—I grieve in thought and weep blood.
translations.idiomatic: I have a mother—for her sake I grieve until my tears run like blood.

sentences.zh: 我父而有知兮，怒衝發。

translations.literal: If my father had knowledge his rage would burst forth.
translations.idiomatic: If my father could know, his rage would burst forth.

sentences.zh: 我兄摩挲傭之金兮，骨肉相蔑。

translations.literal: My elder brother fondles the laborer's gold—flesh and bone despise each other.
translations.idiomatic: My brother fondles the peddler's gold—kin turn against kin.

sentences.zh: 嫂旁睨兮，笑言啞啞。

translations.literal: My sister-in-law glances sidelong—her laughing words are coarse.
translations.idiomatic: My sister-in-law looks on from the side, laughing coarsely.

sentences.zh: 我忽憤氣兮，如云。

translations.literal: Suddenly my angry breath rises like clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly my fury rises like storm clouds.

sentences.zh: 指漆室女以為正兮，又告夫司命與湘君。

translations.literal: I point to the Woman of Lacquer Chamber as my standard and also tell the Lord of Fate and the Lord of Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: I take the Woman of Lacquer Chamber as my model and appeal to the Lord of Fate and the Lord of Xiang.

sentences.zh: 予不愛一死兮，弗忍速阿母之下世。

translations.literal: I do not cherish one death—I cannot bear to hasten dear Mother's passing from the world.
translations.idiomatic: It is not that I fear death—I cannot bear to hasten my dear mother's departure from this world.

sentences.zh: 原死而有憑兮，為凶之厲。

translations.literal: I wish in death to have a spirit presence and become the fierce curse upon the wicked.
translations.idiomatic: May my death leave a vengeful spirit to punish the wicked.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼哀哉，我終死兮，魂獨歸去。

translations.literal: Alas, alas—I must die at last; my soul alone returns home.
translations.idiomatic: Alas—I must die at last, and my soul alone returns home.

sentences.zh: 明告我母兮，幽告我父。

translations.literal: Openly I tell my mother; in the dark I tell my father.
translations.idiomatic: Openly I tell my mother; in the unseen world I tell my father.

sentences.zh: 匪我夙夜兮，胡然遭此行露也。

translations.literal: It is not that I rise early and retire late—why suddenly do I meet this dew on the road?
translations.idiomatic: It is not for lack of diligence—why must I walk this dew-soaked road?

sentences.zh: 縱謂行多露兮，寧能我之汙也。

translations.literal: Even if they say the road is heavy with dew—can they truly defile me?
translations.idiomatic: Even if the road is heavy with dew—they cannot truly defile me.

sentences.zh: 重曰：嘉名為玉，父之命兮。

translations.literal: The refrain says: A fine name is Yu—Father's command.
translations.idiomatic: The refrain runs: My fine name is Yu—my father's gift.

sentences.zh: 幽辱糞壤，終保貞兮。

translations.literal: Though hidden in shame like filth and earth, at last I preserve chastity.
translations.idiomatic: Though buried in shame like common earth, I preserve my chastity to the end.

sentences.zh: 憂思悄悄，淚淫淫兮。

translations.literal: Grief and thought are quiet; tears flow without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Quiet grief fills my heart; tears flow without end.

sentences.zh: 蒙恥忍詬，日當心兮。」

translations.literal: Bearing shame and abuse, day by day it burns in my heart."
translations.idiomatic: Bearing shame and abuse, day by day it burns in my heart."

translations.literal: [End of the lament.]
translations.idiomatic: [End of the lament.]

sentences.zh: 趙氏婢，失其名，為杭州趙氏婢。

translations.literal: A maid of the Zhao clan—her name is lost—was a maid of the Zhao clan of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: A maid of the Zhao family of Hangzhou, whose name is unknown.

sentences.zh: 趙氏嘗有客，言珞琭子之學，使為婢算，曰：「是當七易其夫。」

translations.literal: A guest versed in Luobozi's divination once read the maid's fortune for the Zhao family and said, "She is fated to have seven husbands."
translations.idiomatic: A guest versed in Luobozi's divination once read the maid's fortune for the Zhao family and said, "She is fated to have seven husbands."

sentences.zh: 婢恚曰：「吾嫁則有夫，有夫則有死。

translations.literal: The maid angrily said, "If I marry I have a husband; if I have a husband I have death.
translations.idiomatic: The maid angrily replied, "If I marry I will have one husband; when I have a husband I will die with him.

sentences.zh: 吾今且不嫁，誰為之夫者？」

translations.literal: If I never marry at all, who could ever be my husband?"
translations.idiomatic: If I never marry at all, who could ever be my husband?"

sentences.zh: 自是蓬首垢面，矢不嫁。

translations.literal: From then on with disheveled hair and dirty face she swore not to marry.
translations.idiomatic: From then on she wore her hair unkempt and her face unwashed, vowing never to marry.

sentences.zh: 趙氏有婚嫁輒避匿，媒氏至，詬誶不可近。

translations.literal: Whenever the Zhao clan had a marriage she hid away; when matchmakers came she reviled them so they could not approach.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Zhao family arranged a marriage she hid; when matchmakers came she cursed them until they could not approach.

sentences.zh: 主誨之，搶首乞終役。

translations.literal: Her mistress admonished her; she knocked her head on the ground begging to serve to the end.
translations.idiomatic: When her mistress admonished her she kowtowed and begged to serve out her life in the household.

sentences.zh: 年至七十餘，死於趙氏。

translations.literal: When her years reached more than seventy she died in the Zhao clan.
translations.idiomatic: She lived past seventy and died in the Zhao household.
